# Surrenders and maturities
##  Frequently asked questions
Here are the answers to some of the questions you might have about the surrender or maturity of your Royal London life, savings or investment policy. These answers don't relate to Royal London pension, car, home or business insurance policies or funeral plans.
What other options might I have instead of surrendering my policy?
Surrendering means cashing in your policy early. It may mean that you may get back less than you have paid in. It may also mean that you get back less than you would if you continued to pay your premium. If you cash in a policy that includes life cover, the life cover will stop, so we won’t pay anything when the life assured dies.
Before you decide to cash in your policy you should consider other options that you may have. These depend on the terms and conditions of your particular policy but could include the following:
  * Reducing your premium
  * Taking a break from paying your premium
  * Stopping paying your premium. If you keep your policy but stop paying the premium, we will pay less money when the policy ends than if you had continued to pay the premium.


For further information about the options available for your particular policy or cashing it in please [contact us](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/). While we can provide information, we cannot advise you what to do. If you are in any doubt as to what to do, you should contact a financial adviser for advice. If you do not have a financial adviser, you can can find more information about [how to find an adviser](https://www.royallondon.com/find-a-financial-adviser/) in your area and other useful independent resources on our site. Advisers may charge for providing such advice and should confirm any cost beforehand.
If your policy has been assigned, it means that rights to claiming on the policy have passed to someone else, for example a bank or building society. In this case, before you can cash it in we will contact the bank or building society.
How will you pay me the maturity value of my policy?
You do not need to contact us when your policy matures as we will automatically send you a cheque unless you have assigned your policy. If you have assigned your policy, it means that rights to claiming on it have passed to someone else, for example a bank or building society. In this case you will need to contact the bank or building society first.
If you have assigned your policy absolutely, it means that ownership has passed to someone else. In this case we will send the cheque to the new owner.
Do you add bonuses to my policy and how do you decide these?
If you have a with profits policy, you can read about how we manage our with profits fund, including how we decide bonuses, in the [PPFM section](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/governance-and-leadership-teams/corporate-governance/ppfm/) of our site.
What to do if I want to cash my policy in before the maturity date
  * Depending on the type of policy you have, you may be able to surrender your policy before the maturity date.
  * This means that you will not get the same amount back from your plan and any final bonus will not be included.
  * If this is something you want to discuss further, please call us on:
    * **0345 646 2092** for endowment savings plans taken out with Royal London, Refuge Assurance or United Friendly.
    * **0345 646 2106** for plans taken out with Scottish Life.
    * For CIS plans **0345 646 2107** - Lines are open 8am to 6pm Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays.
    * For plans formerly with Abbey National or Santander, please call **0345 646 2095** - Lines are open 8am to 6pm Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays.

# Tell us about a bereavement
We understand that the world can feel as though it's been turned upside down when someone dies. So we are making things easy - whether you're letting us know about an insurance claim or you're the beneficiary of a pension.
##  Information we'll ask for
We'll take your contact details so we can send any forms you might need, and keep you updated. It'd also help if you have the following information about the person who died:
  * Their full name
  * Their last known address
  * Their date of birth
  * The date they died
  * Any policy or plan numbers
  * The death certificate (we might need the certificate number)
  * If a will has been left, we will need the name of the executor if you know it.

### What to expect
### Get in touch
Let us know someone has died. You can do this online, by phone or by post.
### Keeping making payments
We'll let you know when it's ok to stop, and refund any overpaid premiums.
### We'll contact you
The person handling your claim will let you know if we need any more information.
## Getting in touch
To show you how best to get in touch with us, we need to know what kind of policy they had. Don't worry if you don't know, just choose 'I don't know' from the list below.

There's an estimated 3.3 million unclaimed pensions in the UK, worth £31.1 billion, according to research by the Pension Policy Institute (PPI)*. That's nearly £9,500 per pension - so it's worth taking the time to track down your lost pensions.
*Source: [PPI Briefing Note Number 138, Lost Pensions 2024, October 2024](https://www.pensionspolicyinstitute.org.uk/media/vh4aaq2j/20241024-ppi-bn138-lost-pensions-2024-final.pdf)
##  1. Get the details of your old pensions
Take a look at your CV. For every job you’ve had you might have had a workplace pension, and some pensions can be tracked down just by knowing the name of the company you worked for.
Check your files to see if you’ve got any pension statements from your previous providers. They’ll give you the details of any old plans. The more information you have about your previous plans, the better.
Even if you have a certificate from a previous employer, it doesn’t always mean that you have a pension entitlement. For example, you may have had a refund of your contributions when you left that employer.
Many older workplace pensions may have also needed you to be a member for a certain number of years, before you were entitled to a pension.
##  2. Contact your old pension provider
Once you know which provider your old pension was with, the first step is to contact them. When you get in touch, you should give them as much information as possible to help them reunite you with your pension savings. This includes:
  * Your plan number, if you’ve been able to find it on your old paperwork
  * Your date of birth
  * Your National Insurance number.

Royal London has been around since 1861, and in that time, a number of pension providers have joined us. You may be surprised at just how many companies we have records for.
So it could be worth having a look at our database using the dropdown below to see if any of your missing pensions are with one of those providers.
Bear in mind, providers may have changed names or been taken over in the time that's passed, so you may need to do further research to confirm any changes.
### Choose a company to get the contact details you need
Choose a company to get the contact details you need
Select... Abbey National Life Assurance Phoenix Bright Grey Caledonian Life (ROI)  Canterbury Life Assurance  Co-operative Insurance Society (CIS) Friends Provident (ROI) Irish Life (ROI) National and Provincial (N&P) Life Assurance Pegasus / Pegasus Whole of Life Progress Refuge Assurance Refuge Life Royal Liver Scottish Life Scottish Mutual Assurance Limited Scottish Provident United Assurance Group (UAG) UFLP United Friendly
When you speak to your previous provider, it’s a good idea to make sure they have the most up to date contact details for you. If you’ve moved house and not updated your address, there’s a chance you’ll be missing out on important paperwork like your yearly pension statement.


##  3. Fill in any gaps by using the Pension Tracing Service
If you think you have a missing pension, but you can’t find any information about it at all, you can try the government’s free [Pension Tracing Service](https://www.gov.uk/find-pension-contact-details). You can visit their [gov.uk website](https://www.gov.uk/find-pension-contact-details) or give them a ring on [0800 731 0175](tel:0800%20731%200175).
You should try to collect as much information as you can about the pension you've lost before using the Pension Tracing Service. Ideally, this should include:
**For a workplace pension:**
  * Name of the employer
  * Type of business
  * Your last address
  * When you worked for the employer

**For a personal pension:**
  * Name of pension or as close as you can to remembering it
  * Your last address
  * The name of any bank, insurance company or building society associated with your personal pension

The Pension Tracing Service can then use this information to search through their database of over 300,000 pensions and may be able to give you the contact details for a workplace pension or personal pension you've lost touch with. This includes details of the new company or provider name if your old pension has been taken over or changed its name over the years.
The Pension Tracing Service will only tell you the contact details of the pension’s administrator. You'll then need to contact the pension administrator to find out whether you have a pension, what value it is and what options you have for taking it.
##  How to track down a Royal London pension
If you need to track down a Royal London pension, you can give us a call on [0345 605 0050](tel:0345%20605%200050). Lines are open 8am to 6pm Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays.
### What to do with the pensions you track down
Once you’ve found the pensions you’ve lost track of and have all their details, you can decide what you’d like to do with them. These are some of the options to think about.
### Consider all your options
Your provider should confirm to you all the options available from your newly found pension.
### Combine your pensions
Having your pensions together in one place could make it easier for you to keep track of your pension savings and help you feel more in control of your financial future.
If you already have a pension with Royal London, you can transfer your other pensions to us.
[ Find out more  about Combine your pensions ](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/pension-transfers/)
### Get financial advice
If you’re not sure what the best option for you is, we recommend speaking to a financial adviser. If you don’t already have an adviser you can find one in your area.

Advisers may charge for their services – though they should agree any fees with you up front.
[ Find an adviser  about Get financial advice  ](https://www.royallondon.com/find-a-financial-adviser/)
##  Should I transfer my pension?
Combining pensions isn’t for everyone. You may lose valuable features or benefits when you transfer. For more information on the things to consider before transferring, you can read our guide.
[ Read the guide  ](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/pension-guides/pension-basics/should-I-transfer-my-pensions/)

#  Fraud and scams
We help our customers plan for and build towards financial security after they stop working. But protecting your money against fraud in the here and now is very important to ensuring your financial wellbeing too.
To help protect you from scams, we’ve pulled together some helpful guidance on what you can do if you’re worried that you’ve been targeted by scammers.
## Financial Crime Statement
We are fully committed to operating in compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.
We have implemented several policies to minimises our exposure to all forms of financial crime including money laundering, terrorist financing, fraud, bribery & corruption and market abuse. These policies include:
  * Financial Crime policy
  * Conflicts of Interest and Gifts & Entertainment policy
  * Market Conduct policy
  * Personal Account Dealing policy
  * Speak up and Whistleblow policy

The standards in these policies are driven by appropriate legislation, regulatory requirements, and industry standards. Each policy is reviewed regularly to ensure that they remain up to date, and in line with any external changes.
We carry out ongoing activity across Royal London to monitor compliance with the appropriate legislation and regulation.

**Jason Wyatt**
**Group Head of Financial Crime**
## Latest scams
Fraudsters are constantly creating new scams to trick unsuspecting customers into handing over personal information and money. This section will be updated with current scams as we become aware of them.
##  Simple steps to stay safe online
At Royal London, we take your security seriously. Tel: [0345 602 1885](tel:03456021895)
When you call, choose what type of product you have or have been contacted about and you'll be transferred to a member of our team.

[ Log in  Log in button that will open the online service page ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/online-service/) [ Register  Register button that will open up online service page  ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/online-service/)
## Find your investment or insurance product
  * ## Businesses we've rebranded as Royal London
  * ## Older policies
  * ## Find a lost pension

###  Businesses we've rebranded as Royal London
Royal London has been around since 1861 so our business looks somewhat different today than it did when we started. We've bought, owned and rebranded a number of specialist businesses, so even if you’re not sure your policy is with us - we’re here to help.
If your policy was originally taken out with one of these businesses you can select from these options to help direct your enquiry.
  * [Abbey National/Santander](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/abbey-national/ "Abbey National/Santander")
  * [Aegon Protection Insurance](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/aegon-protection-insurance/)
  * [Bright Grey](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/bright-grey/ "Bright Grey")
  * [Caledonian Life (ROI)](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/caledonian-life/ "Caledonian Life \(ROI\)")
  * [Canterbury Life Policy](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/canterbury-life/ "Canterbury Life Policy")
  * [Co-operative Insurance Society (CIS)](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/co-operative-insurance-society/ "Co-operative Insurance Society \(CIS\)")
  * [Friends Provident](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/friends-provident/ "Friends Provident")
  * [Irish Life](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/irish-life/ "Irish Life")

  * [National and Provincial Policy](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/national-and-provincial/ "National and Provincial Policy")
  * [Pegasus](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/pegasus/ "Pegasus")

  * [Refuge Assurance](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/refuge-assurance/ "Refuge Assurance")
  * [Refuge Life](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/refuge-life/ "Refuge Life")
  * [Royal Liver](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/royal-liver/ "Royal Liver")
  * [Scottish Life](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/scottish-life/ "Scottish Life")
  * [Scottish Life International/RL360 ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/scottish-life-international/)

  * [UFLP](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/united-friendly-life-and-pensions/ "UFLP")
  * [United Friendly](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/united-friendly/ "United Friendly")

###  Older policies
  * My policy was from a number of years ago – will you still have my details?
If the company your policy was with is listed on this page and your policy is live, we can trace it.
If a claim was previously made, we may not be able to trace the policy in question as we only hold our claim records for the legal minimum of 6 years.
All you need to do is give us a call on the number shown, and our experts will be happy to help.

###  Find a lost pension
  * The company I’m looking for isn’t listed. Does that mean my policy isn’t with Royal London?
We’re afraid so. But just because your policy isn’t with us, doesn’t mean all is lost.
To take your search further, there are other sources you can use that are ready and willing to help.
**For insurance policies**
- [The Policy Detective](http://policydetective.co.uk/ "The Policy Detective") can help you track down insurance policies held with companies that have either changed name or merged with other companies.
**For pension policies**
- [MoneyHelper](https://www.moneyhelper.org.uk/en/pensions-and-retirement/pension-problems/tracing-and-finding-lost-pensions "MoneyHelper") can help trace personal pension policies.
- The [Pension Tracing Service](https://www.gov.uk/find-pension-contact-details "Pensions Tracing Service") can help you find workplace pension policies.
For more information on tracking down lost pensions, visit our [Find a lost pension page](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/help-and-support/find-a-lost-pension/ "Find a lost pension").

Get the details of current financial scams, find out how to protect yourself from fraud and what to do if you're worried that you've been targeted by scammers
[ Learn more about fraud and scams  Learn more about fraud and scams ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/help-and-support/fraud-and-scams/)

##  Getting extra help

Tell us about your circumstances and our specialist team will get in touch to let you know what support we can offer.
[ Get support  Get extra support ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/help-and-support/personal-support/)

It's easy to lose track of your pensions. Even if you only have a small amount, it's still worth tracking them down as they could provide you with extra income when you retire.

Your activation email connects you with your Royal London products. You’ll receive an activation email when:

address

# Help & Support
Why do I need a mobile phone to login/register?
As part of our secure login and registration process, we’ll send a verification code to your mobile phone, so you'll need to make sure you have access to the mobile number that you use when you register and sign in.
I’ve forgotten my login details
As long as you have access to the email address that you registered with, you can [reset your password](https://login.royallondon.com/onlineservice2/Account/ResetPassword) quickly and easily.
If you don’t know the email address that you registered with, you can [get your email address here](https://login.royallondon.com/onlineservice2/Account/RetrieveEmail).
If you are still having issues logging in, please give us a ring on 0370 850 2179 between 8am and 6pm, Monday to Friday.
What if I have multiple policies with Royal London?
Once you’re logged in, you should be able to see all of your product statements. However, if any policies are missing, you may need to login to our Intermediary Online Service.
What to do if the policyholder has passed away
To notify us that someone has passed away, please give us a ring on 0370 850 2179 between 8am and 6pm Monday to Friday and we'll be able to help talk you through the process in more detail.
Or visit our [online claims page](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/help-and-support/make-a-claim/tell-us-about-a-bereavement-old-version15012024/) for further information. This link will provide more information about what you'll need to do as well as important contact telephone numbers that you may need. In some cases you can notify us using an online form and we will contact you regarding the claim either by telephone or email.
How can I stay safe online?
You can help to protect your online account and stay secure by following these few simple steps:
  * Install the latest software and app updates
  * Use strong and separate unique passwords
  * Apply a screen lock to your mobile devices
  * Install and update anti-virus software on all your devices
  * Do not use websites with personal data on public wi-fi networks
  * Sign out when you finish using online services

# How to get help with our online insurance service
## Are you in the right place?
This page is for customers with Personal Menu or Whole of Life plans taken out with Royal London since 2004 or previously Bright Grey.
Our online insurance service is designed to be easy-to-use but if you need an extra helping hand, we've hopefully got the answer to your question here.
If you’ve had an email from us to activate your My Royal London access [go to our login page](https://my.royallondon.com/) where you can login or follow the retrigger your email link to activate your access. If you’ve not heard from us yet [please register your plan today](https://www.royallondon.com/forms/register-your-details-for-online-access-to-your-policy/).
If not, you can contact us using our [online form](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/fill-in-our-form/?utm_source=customer_portal&utm_medium=support_centre) or you can call us on [0345 6094 500](tel:0345%206094%20500).
## Using the online service
Our online insurance service is currently only available for **Personal Menu** and **Whole of Life** customers. If you have one of these qualifying Personal Menu or Whole of Life plans and if Royal London holds up-to-date email and mobile phone contact details for you, you might have already received a registration email from us.
In case you can’t find this email, [visit the system log in page](https://my.royallondon.com) then click on the link and we’ll resend you your registration email.
If you have one of these plans but haven’t received an email it might be because we don’t have an email address for you. To update your details please call the customer service team on [0345 6094 500](tel:0345%206094%20500).
## FAQs: Your plan online
Here you'll find the most common questions we're asked about our online service.
Who can currently use the online insurance service?
Our online insurance service is a new service so it is currently only available for **Personal Menu** and **Whole of Life** customers but we are working to expand on this.

If you have one of these qualifying Personal Menu or Whole of Life plans and if Royal London holds up-to-date email and mobile phone contact details for you, we'll be in touch.
If you think you have already received an email from us but can't find it, please [visit the system log in page](https://my.royallondon.com) then click on the link and we’ll resend you your registration email.

If you don’t have an up-to-date email or mobile registered with us you can change that by updating your details with our helpful customer service team please call [0345 6094 500](tel:0345%206094%20500).
Why do you need my email AND mobile number?
We use these details to ensure your security for when you log in to our system. It not only makes it easier but also more secure, so we know it’s you and only you trying to access your account.
Why can’t I use the same email address to log in to different accounts or profiles?
It’s important we have a unique email address for you as we use your email address as a way to authenticate your identity and verify your account. This is why we can only allow one registration per email address at this time.
What do I do if I’ve forgotten my password?
If you can't remember your password simply [go to the log in page](https://my.royallondon.com) and select 'Forgotten password?', all you need to do is enter your email address and if you're registered you'll receive an email to reset your password to the email address we hold for you.
I can’t see my plan/cover why is that?
A number of plans and covers won't appear on the portal just yet. These include Lifestyle and Lifestyle Plus cover. If you have a plan or cover that falls into one of these categories then it won't be available to view on our portal yet.
We're working towards including these on the portal in the near future. Please note that Over 50s or Term Life insurance policies bought direct from Royal London are not yet part of this online service.
Can’t find what you’re looking for?
Our expert team is ready to help whether you want to get in touch by post, over the phone or online.
[Get in touch](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/fill-in-our-form/?utm_source=customer_portal&utm_medium=support_centre)

# How to get help with our online pension service
## Are you in the right place?
This page is for customers with Personal Menu or Whole of Life plans taken out with Royal London since 2004 or previously Bright Grey.
Our pensions online service is designed to be simple to use but we've got plenty of support available if you're experiencing technical issues.


## Help after you've logged in
If you've logged in to our online service you may have noticed an 'i' symbol next to different words. If you need a bit of extra help wherever you see the 'i' symbol simply click on the symbol and a short, helpful explanation will appear.
## FAQs: Your plan online
Here you'll find the most common questions we're asked about our online service.
Can I change my details online?
If you need to make changes to your name or your date of birth you must apply for a change of details as these have to be verified by our team. You can do this by [filling in our online form](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/help-and-support/update-your-details/pension-plan/).
Lastly, if you have a pension with your employer and you wish to make changes to your direct debit our team can help you with this, please call [0345 605 0050](tel:0345%20605%200050).
For anything else please call our team - we recommend you listen to all the options to ensure you find the best place to help you get to where you need to be. You can reach our team on [0345 605 0050](tel:0345%20605%200050).
If you're part of your employers pension scheme please call the number shown in your policy documentation.
I get a 'Sorry, online account unavailable' error when trying to register
There are 2 common reasons for this-

  * United Friendly

  * Royal Liver
  * CIS

  * If you've transferred money into your Royal London pension plan but the money is still in the process of being allocated.
  * There could be essential maintenance work taking place, there should be communications to let you know that this is the case.

  * email: eface@royallondon.com
  * telephone: [0345 605 0401](tel:0345%20605%200401).

telephone: [0345 605 0401](tel:0345%20605%200401).

Royal London House

Congleton Road

Macclesfield
SK10 4EL.

**Usernames and passwords**
The data stored within our online service is private to each user and may only be accessed in successful entry of an email address and password. We also use two step verification to ensure no one else will be able to access your account.
**Encryption**
When you connect to and sign in to our online service, you'll be using 128-bit Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) encryption. SSL is the technology that lies behind the yellow padlock that's displayed in the bottom right corner of Internet browsers. The use of SSL encryption means that no one can intercept and see the information being transferred between our customers and our online service.
**Digital certificates**
We use Verisign Class 3 digital certificates on our online service. This means that our electronic identity and authority have been independently verified. When you connect to one of our secure sites, your web browser uses the Verisign digital certificate to set up the SSL encrypted communications with our site. You can view our Verisign certificate information by double clicking the yellow padlock in the bottom right corner of your browser.
**Firewalls**
We use firewalls to restrict access to the servers that host our websites. We also make use of Intrusion Detection and Intrusion Prevention Systems (IDS and IPS respectively) – these systems constantly monitor our systems for malicious or unwanted activity and can react to block or prevent those activities.
**GDPR**

#  Manage your pension
We give you control of your pension with the option to make payments and transfers, check fund performance, pick from a range of income options when you’re ready to retire, and more.
##  Use our online service
Our online service lets you view and manage your pension plan online. Register for online service or log in to get started.
[ Log in or register  ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/online-service/)
##  Update your details
If your circumstances change, you can update your personal details, home address, bank account information and more online, or by contacting us.
[ Manage your details  ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/help-and-support/update-your-details/pension-plan/)
##  Check fund prices
Our monthly fund and portfolio updates help you see how your pension’s performing.
[ See the updates  ](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/investment-options/fund-prices/)
##  Transfer a pension
You may be able to transfer pensions from other providers into your personal or workplace pension plan. Learn more about how transfers work or get started here.
[ More about pension transfers  ](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/pension-transfers/)
##  Pay into your pension
You can make a contribution using our online service or mobile app. See what a payment might mean for your plan, and more.
[ Find out more  ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/your-products/manage-your-pension/making-pension-contributions/)
## RL (CIS) pensions
Find out how to manage pension products taken out with RL(CIS) – formally the Co-Operative Insurance Society Limited:
  * [RL (CIS) Individual personal pensions](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/your-products/manage-your-pension/rlcis-individual-personal-pension/)
  * [RL (CIS) Stakeholder pensions](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/your-products/manage-your-pension/rlcis-stakeholder-pension/)

## Pension guides
  * How much can I [pay into my pension](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/pension-guides/pension-basics/pension-allowances/)?
  * How to [boost your pension](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/pension-guides/pension-basics/how-to-boost-your-pension-pot/)
  * How to [find a lost pension](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/help-and-support/find-a-lost-pension/)
  * A guide to the [State Pension](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/pension-guides/pension-basics/what-is-the-state-pension-and-how-does-it-work/)
  * How to [nominate your beneficiaries](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/planning-ahead/estate-planning/the-importance-of-nominating-your-beneficiaries/)

##  Download our mobile app
For Royal London or Scottish Life pensions started in 2004 or later. Our mobile app helps you to keep track of your pension performance, view your investments, transfer your pension and more.
[ Get the app  ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/online-service/download-our-mobile-app/)
## Take money from your pension
#### Changes to minimum pension age
The government has confirmed a rise in the minimum pension age. You can normally start taking your pension savings any time after age 55 – even if you’re still working. This will increase to age 57 from 6 April 2028.
## [Access your pension savings If you’re ready, you can start taking money from your pension using our range of options. Explore retirement options  ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/your-products/manage-your-pension/access-your-pension/)
## [Compare your options Our helpful guide explains the ways you can take money from your pension, so you can decide what’s right for you. Read the guide  ](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/pension-guides/taking-your-pension/pension-freedoms-explained/)
## Already have an Income Release plan?
Whether you want to set up a new regular monthly payment, change or stop an existing monthly payment, take a one-off tax-free payment, or withdraw your full pension savings and close your plan, you can do it all online.
Please choose the option that best suits your needs from the following:
## [Take a one-off taxable payment If you have a Royal London Income Release plan, you can use this form to request to take a one-off taxable payment from the plan. Request a payment  ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/your-products/manage-your-pension/income-payment-request/)
## [Request Income Release plan payments Use this form to change payments, request a tax-free withdrawal, or withdraw all funds and close your Royal London Income Release plan. Get started  ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/your-products/manage-your-pension/set-up-or-change-a-payment-from-an-existing-income-release-plan/)
## More pensions support and information
Our guides, tools and information can help you understand and manage your pension – so you can save for the retirement you want.
## [Use our pension calculators See how much you could get when you retire, and your options for taking your pension. Use the calculators  ](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/pension-guides/pension-tools/)
## [Tell us about a bereavement If a loved one had a pension with us and they’ve died, you can find out how to let us know here – we’ll make the next steps as easy as possible. Let us know  ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/help-and-support/make-a-claim/tell-us-about-a-bereavement/)
## [Find a financial adviser It’s worth getting financial advice if you’re unsure about paying or transferring into your pension. Our guides explains how an adviser could help, and how to find one. Learn more about advice  ](https://www.royallondon.com/find-a-financial-adviser/)
### Find the support you need
### Find a financial adviser
We strongly recommend talking about your retirement options with a professional financial adviser.
[ Find a financial adviser  about Find a financial adviser ](https://www.royallondon.com/find-a-financial-adviser/)
### Pension Wise
Pension Wise (external site) is a government service from MoneyHelper that offers free, impartial pensions guidance.
[ Visit Pension Wise  about Pension Wise ](https://www.moneyhelper.org.uk/en/pensions-and-retirement/pension-wise)

Remember, there are limits on how much you can contribute to pension plans while still qualifying for tax relief. It’s also important to remember that tax relief depends on individual circumstances and could change in the future.
##  Workplace pension contributions
You can choose to make a one-off contribution to your workplace pension plan or change your regular contributions.
###
### Making a one off contribution
You can make a one-off contribution into your plan at any time, and you’ll receive basic tax relief on all contributions you make to your plan.
  * You can pay in up to 100% of your earnings, or £2,880 and it would be increased to £3,600 with [tax relief](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/pension-guides/pension-basics/understanding-pension-tax-relief-and-annual-allowance/).
  * If you pay in more than £60,000 each year then you could be subject to a tax charge due to the [annual allowance](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/pension-guides/pension-basics/pension-allowances/).
  * Any one-off contributions made to your plan will be invested in line with your current instructions unless you tell us otherwise.
  * Remember, the value of your investments can fall as well as rise and you may not get back the amount invested.
  * Your money is invested until at least age 55 (this will increase to age 57 from 6 April 2028) which means you should consider all your options before deciding to make the payment.

##  Make a one-off contribution to your workplace pension
Use our single contribution form to make a one-off contribution into your workplace pension.
[ Make a one-off contribution  ](https://www.royallondon.com/forms/pensions-servicing/single-contribution-application-form/)
### Changing your regular contributions
Your regular contributions are paid monthly to us by your employer and can be paid as a percentage of your salary, or as a fixed amount.
  * Regular contributions are made from your net salary, or by using [salary exchange](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/workplace-pensions/how-salary-exchange-works/).
  * You can change the regular contributions to your workplace pension at any time but remember, any changes will affect your pensions savings.
  * Pausing or decreasing your contributions could mean there’s less money available to give you an income when you stop working, and it may also change your forecast.
  * If you want to change your regular contributions, or exchange a bonus for a contribution, you should speak to your employer.

##  Personal pension contributions
If you have a personal pension with us, you can also make a one-off contribution to your pension plan or change your regular contributions. If you're saving into our [Pension Portfolio](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/personal-pensions/), your contributions are paid from your net salary, which is paid monthly or yearly by direct debit. Here’s what you need to know:
### Making a one off contribution
You can make a one-off contribution into your personal pension plan at any time, and you’ll receive basic tax relief on all contributions you make to your plan. Here’s what you need to know:
  * You can pay in up to 100% of your earnings, or £2,880 and it would be increased to £3,600 with tax relief.
  * If you pay in more than £60,000 each year then you could be subject to a tax charge due to the [annual allowance](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/pension-guides/pension-basics/pension-allowances/).
  * Any one-off contributions made to your plan will be invested in line with your current instructions unless you tell us otherwise.
  * Remember, the value of your investments can fall as well as rise and you may not get back the amount invested.
  * Your money is invested until at least age 55 (this will increase to 57 from 6 April 2028) which means you should consider all your options before deciding to make the payment.

To make a one-off contribution to your personal pension, please call us on [0345 603 0154](tel:03456030154).
### Changing your regular contributions
Here’s what you need to know:
  * The minimum regular contribution you can make is £100 a month or £1,200 a year.
  * If you've previously made a one-off contribution, it will reduce to £50 a month or £600 a year.
  * You can choose a fixed amount or set it to increase each year with your salary, Retail Prices Index (RPI) or set at a level between one and ten percent.

If you’d like to speak to us about regular contributions please phone us at [0345 850 8953](tel:03458508953).
We always recommend speaking to a financial adviser if you want to change your regular contributions. If you don’t have one, find out [where to look for an adviser](https://www.royallondon.com/find-a-financial-adviser/).

Our guides and helpful information can help you understand and manage your pension.
##  Check in on your pension
You don't need to wait for annual statements to see if you're on track for retirement. Log in or register online, or download our mobile app to view and manage your pension.

# RLCIS Stakeholder Pension Frequently Asked Questions
If you're looking for more information about the RLCIS Stakeholder Pension, our Frequently Asked Questions may have the answer you're looking for.
What is the RLCIS Stakeholder Pension?
The RLCIS Stakeholder Pension is a plan to help build up a sum of money in a tax-efficient way to support you in retirement. It's designed to meet conditions set out in legislation. These include:
  * a cap on charges
  * low minimum contributions
  * flexibility in stopping and starting contributions.

How flexible is it?
You can make one-off contributions at any time to top up your plan. You can also change your regular contributions whenever you like.
HM Revenue and Customs limits the contributions you can make - see "How much can I pay into my plan each year?".
You can stop contributing, or take a contribution holiday at any time. And you can take a contribution holiday for a total of two months in any 12 month period. But if you stop your contributions, or take a contribution holiday, your pension savings could be lower than what you would have received if you'd continued making regular contributions up to your chosen retirement age. Stopping contributions will also mean that any waiver of contribution cover will stop.
You can continue contributing to your stakeholder pension regardless of the number of times you change jobs. But if your new employer operates a company pension scheme, it may be in your best interests to join it. You may still be able to contribute to your stakeholder pension as well. You must notify us of any change of employer.
How much can I pay into my plan each year?
You can pay the higher of either 100% of your earnings or £3,600, subject to the annual allowance.
The annual allowance is the maximum amount of pension savings you can get tax relief on each tax year – based on your own contributions, any employer contributions and any contributions made on your behalf by someone else. The annual allowance is £60,000 for most people in the 2026/27 tax year.
The annual allowance applies across all your pension savings, not per policy or plan.
The minimum contribution including tax relief to the RLCIS Stakeholder Pension is £20. This applies for both monthly contributions and single contributions.
We deduct monthly contributions either from your salary or by direct debit. Single contributions are payable by cheque.
What about tax?
Your employer will pay their contributions, including any tax relief.
You'll receive tax relief on the other pension contributions into your plan. But you won't receive tax relief on any waiver of contribution premiums. We claim the tax relief at the basic rate from HM Revenue and Customs and add it to your plan.
If you're a higher or additional rate taxpayer, you can claim the extra relief through your tax return.
What are the charges?
For plans set up before 6 April 2005 (and any additional payments subsequently made to these plans) there's an annual management charge of 1% of the value of the savings you build up. So for example, if your savings are valued at £500 throughout the year, we'll deduct £5 that year. If it's valued at £7,500 throughout the year, we'll deduct £75. When we set each day’s unit price, we allow for the annual management charge.
For plans set up after 5 April 2005 (and any additional payments subsequently made to these plans), there is an annual management charge of 1.5% of the value of the funds you build up. So for example, if your fund is valued at £500 throughout the year, we'll deduct £7.50 that year. If it's valued at £7,500 throughout the year, we'll deduct £112.50. On the 10th anniversary of your plan, the annual management charge will reduce to 1% of the value of the funds you build up.
These charges are regularly reviewed and may be changed in future.
What other benefits can I choose?
You can apply for waiver of contribution cover. This can provide cover for your pension contributions if you can't work because of sickness or accident.
What happens if I die before I retire?
If you die before you retire, we'll pay your beneficiaries the value of your plan.
Can I change my mind?
If we accept your application, we'll send you a notice of your right to cancel. When you get it, you'll have 30 days to change your mind and we'll give you and your employer your money back.
title: RLCIS pension FAQ

# Online client pack - FAQs
Our online client packs allow you to review and confirm the answers provided on your application, as well as make any changes. The process is designed to be quick and simple - giving you peace of mind we’ve all the information we need in the event of a claim.
Below are answers to some frequently asked questions and if you need any further assistance, our customer contact team are on hand to help.
I’ve not received my secure code in the post yet – what should I do?
This normally takes a few days to arrive - if you’ve not received it within a week, please contact our customer contact team on 0345 609 4500 and they can re-issue.
Can I request a paper copy of the review instead of completing this online?
Yes - please contact our customer contact team who will send a paper version for you to complete and return.
I’ve lost my secure code, can I request another?
Our customer contact team can re-issue any lost codes to you.
Do I still have to complete the review if I’ve no changes?
Completing the review isn’t just about amending any errors or providing new information, it’s about giving us confirmation that you agree with the answers provided, so it’s best to complete and return the review.
What if I don’t complete the review by the date advised?
You’ll no longer be able to log in and complete this online, but you can still request a paper copy from our customer contact team.
What if the link doesn’t work when I click it?
Try copying the link and pasting it into the address field of a web browser.
What if the login is still failing, even though I’ve entered my details correctly?
Check the spelling of your name on the secure code letter in case there has been a typing error made when inputting your name on the application form. You may need to log in with an incorrect spelling and amend the error when you’re completing the review.
Also consider whether any forenames, middle names or surnames may have been mixed up on the application form and if switching those helps you log in successfully.
For any additional questions or support, call our customer contact team on 0345 609 4500.
title: Online client pack FAQs

#  Platinum Bond Plus
**This product is no longer available to new customers**
Platinum Bond Plus is a lump-sum ‘with-profits’ investment designed to help your money to grow over the medium to long term (five years or more).
[ Manage your investment  Manage your investment ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/your-products/manage-your-investment/) [ Platinum Bond Plus product guide (PDF 161KB)  Platinum Bond Plus product guide ](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/shared/capita/mkt2612-platinum-bond-plus-important-facts-lclpd0002.pdf)
What is Platinum Bond Plus?
This type of investment involves a degree of risk. Its value can go down as well as up, so you might get back less than you put in.
For a summary of your Platinum Bond Plus with-profits investment, please see our [Platinum Plus: An overview of your with-profits investment document](https://www.royallondon.com/siteassets/site-docs/rlcis/ppi-ywpi-26.pdf) (PDF - 73KB)
### Product features
We'll send you a statement once a year, on the anniversary of your investment to let you know how it's performing*
### Annual Bonus
Each year, we may add an annual bonus to your investment.
### Investment term
There's no fixed end date. So you can invest for as long as you like.
### Income
You can make withdrawals from this investment, to give you a 'regular income'.
*You can ask for a valuation of your investment at any time by calling us on **0345 605 7777**.
## More features
Cashing in
You can cash in all, or part of, your investment at any time.
When you do, we need to make sure we pay you a fair value for your investment at that time by applying a Final Bonus, or a Market Value Reduction (MVR). Remember that if you make a partial withdrawal this will reduce the value of your investment.
Final Bonus
We may apply a Final Bonus to top up your investment when you cash in your Bond, or in the event of your death. This makes sure we pay you a fair value for your investment at the time. You can find details of any Final Bonus on your annual statement. Or, if you ask for a valuation of your Bond over the phone, we’ll include this for you as part of the valuation.
Market Value Reduction (MVR)
When you cash in your Bond, we may apply a Market Value Reduction (MVR) to lower the value of your bond. This is to make sure you are paid a fair value for your investment at the time. We will not apply a MVR if you die.
Because of the economic climate and market conditions of the last few years, no MVRs have been applied to Platinum Bond Plus policies since 14th February 2013.
You can find out more about MVRs and these rates by reading our brochure.
[Platinum Bond Plus, an overview of your with-profits investment](https://www.royallondon.com/siteassets/site-docs/rlcis/ppi-ywpi-25.pdf) (PDF - 161KB)
Income
You can make withdrawals from this investment, to give you a ‘regular income’. Up to 5% each year of the total amount you invested at the time without needing to pay any tax straight away.
Death benefit
Platinum Bond Plus is also a life assurance policy. When the person covered by the plan dies, we'll pay 101% of the plan value plus any further bonuses added at that time. The death benefit won't be lower than the premiums you've paid, less any money you've withdrawn from your policy.
If you have a joint policy and one of the policyholders dies, we will convert the policy into the sole name of the surviving policyholder.
Statements
We'll send you a statement once a year, on the anniversary of your investment, to let you know how it’s performing. Your statement will tell you if we've added an Annual Bonus to your investment. You'll also be able to see the current Bonus Rate or if we'd charge you any MVR if you wanted to cash in your investment.
You can ask for a valuation of your investment at any time by calling us on 03456 057777.
## Product details
  * How we share the profits
  * Analysis and performance
  * Fees and charges

How we share the profits Analysis and performance Fees and charges
## How we share the profits
### How we share the profits
When you invest in Platinum Bond Plus, we pool your money together with lots of other investors’ money in a ‘with-profits fund'. A team of experienced investment professionals manage the fund.
Our investment strategy is to achieve growth by investing in different types of assets. These include:
  * UK and overseas shares
  * government and other bonds
  * property
  * cash
  * alternative investments and more.

Because some people want to invest for longer than others, we make sure that everyone who invests in the fund is paid out a fair value when they come to cash in.
Profits from the investments made by our expert Fund Managers are added back to the fund. Then we share them with all the investors by adding bonuses to their investments.
Your returns are ‘smoothed’ over time, to reduce the impact of the daily ups and downs of the stock market. With-profits investments are a good fit for long-term investors who:
  * Want better returns than they can usually get on cash savings
  * Don't want to be fully exposed to the unpredictability of the stock market

But remember, unlike cash savings, the cash-in value of your investment may go down as well as up. You could get back less than you've invested. Read the Market Value Reduction section of this page for more information.
We add annual bonuses and review these on a regular basis. Annual bonuses share part of the profits of the fund with policyholders and increase your bond value. You can find more details on your annual statement.
## Analysis and performance
### Asset mix (as at 31 December 2024)
The with-profits fund is made up of different types of investments (assets).
Asset mix (as at 31 December 2024)
The with-profits fund is made up of a variety of different types of investments (assets).
  * UK Shares = 10%
  * Overseas Shares = 40%
  * Property = 18%
  * UK Government Bonds = 7%
  * Corporate Bonds = 21%
  * Cash and Other = 1%
  * Alternative Investments = 3%

#### How we manage your investment
We provide a document called ‘The Principles and Practices of Financial Management’ (PPFM). This explains how we manage your investment.
[Visit our PPFM page](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/governance-and-leadership-teams/corporate-governance/ppfm/) to download the latest version.
## Fees and charges
### Fees and charges
When you invest in Platinum Bond Plus we charge you for looking after and managing your money.
#### Fees and charges summary
There's a one-off charge of 4% for making an investment in Platinum Bond Plus on ‘day one’ of your investment. We calculate this as a percentage of the amount you invest.
We also charge you an annual management charge for the yearly expenses of managing your Bond. We deduct this from the investment profits of our with-profits fund before working out bonuses.
The annual management charges applied to your Bond are:
| **Entry date after**  | **Annual management charge**  |
| --- | --- |
| 1 July 1998  | 0.25%  |
| 1 April 2002  | 0.50%  |
| 28 July 2003  | 0.75%  |
We aim to keep these charges to a minimum. We'll let you know if we make any changes.
#### What about tax?
Platinum Bond Plus can be a tax-efficient way to invest. In summary:
  * We'll cover your basic rate of income tax and capital gains tax liability, for any growth of the investments in the ‘with-profits fund’. You cannot recover this tax.
  * You can withdraw up to 5% each year of the total amount you invested without needing to pay any tax straight away. You might choose to do this to give you a 'regular income'.

You'll find more information about taxation in our brochure, “Key Features of The Co-operative Platinum Bond Plus”. We sent you a copy of this brochure when you invested.
##  Frequently Asked Questions
If you have more questions about your Platinum Bond Plus, visit our Investment FAQs page.
[ Investments FAQs  Investments FAQs  ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/your-products/manage-your-investment/rlcis-investment-faq/)

# RLCIS investment FAQ
If you're looking for more information about your RLCIS investment product, our Frequently Asked Questions may have the answer you're looking for.
  * Investment Bond FAQ
  * Platinum Bond Plus FAQ

Investment Bond FAQ Platinum Bond Plus FAQ
## Investment Bond FAQ
## Investment Bond FAQ
What is an Investment Bond?
An [Investment Bond](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/your-products/manage-your-investment/rlcis-investment-bond/) is a lump-sum investment designed for investment growth. The Investment Bond is provided by Aviva, one of the biggest names in life insurance and pensions in the UK.
It is no longer available to new customers.
How much can I invest in the Investment Bond?
Investment Bond is no longer available to new customers. The minimum investment was £5,000 and there was no maximum.
How long will my money be invested for?
The Investment Bond has no fixed term so you can invest for as long as you like. You should see it as a medium to long term investment (5 years or more).
We won't charge you for regular withdrawals of up to 7.5% per year in the first five years. But regular withdrawals above this amount, and any one-off withdrawals, are subject to an early exit charge.
Where will my money be invested?
We arrange The Investment Bond in association with Aviva, who will invest your money.
Aviva will invest your money on your behalf into the funds you choose to make up your Investment Bond. These can include our own Co-operative Investments funds.
You may want to check how the funds you chose are performing. Take a look the [latest fund factsheets](http://www.fundslibrary.co.uk/FundsLibrary.BrandedTools/AvivaConsumer/FundCentral#Price) from Aviva for more information.
Can I take money out?
The Investment Bond is a medium to long-term investment, not a savings account. You should try to leave your money in for as long as possible to give it the best chance to grow.
But you can make withdrawals, either occasional 'one-off' withdrawals, or more often as a regular 'income'. Remember that any withdrawals you make will reduce the amount you get back when you cash your investment in.
How can I find out how my investment is performing?
You can take a look at the [latest fund factsheets online](http://www.fundslibrary.co.uk/FundsLibrary.BrandedTools/AvivaConsumer/FundCentral#Price).
Aviva also send you a statement every year on the anniversary of your investment. This shows the cash-in value for your Bond at the time. You can also get an up-to-date valuation of your Investment Bond whenever you need it, by calling Aviva on **0345 302 1111**.
Is the Investment Bond covered by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme?
Yes. The Scheme was set up to protect investors if a financial services company becomes insolvent and isn't able to meet its obligations to you.
You would be able to make a claim against Aviva if they become insolvent for 100% of the value of your Investment Bond at the time.
Find out more about the [Financial Services Compensation Scheme](https://www.fscs.org.uk/).
## Platinum Bond Plus FAQ
## Platinum Bond Plus FAQ
Platinum Bond Plus is a ‘with profits’ investment. What does that mean?
With-profits investments cushion investors from the sudden ups and downs of the stock market. They use a technique called ‘smoothing’ to even out investment returns over time.
Platinum Bond Plus is a lump-sum, with-profits investment. You invest a lump sum of your money in Platinum Bond Plus. It's then pooled together with the money of lots of other investors into our ‘with-profits fund’.
How much can I invest in Platinum Bond Plus?
Platinum Bond Plus is no longer available to new customers. The minimum investment was £1000 and the maximum investment was £250,000.
How can I find out how my investment is performing?
We send you a statement once a year on the anniversary of your investment. This includes:
  * A cash-in value for your investment at the time
  * Details of any Bonuses and charges we've applied in the previous year
  * A leaflet about how the with-profits fund is performing.

You can also get an up-to-date valuation of your Platinum Bond Plus whenever you need it, by calling us on **0345 605 7777**. We may need to send you your valuation in the post, so this might take a few days.
I’ve heard that Market Value Reductions (MVRs) can sometimes apply to with-profits investments. What does this mean?
In certain circumstances when you cash in your Bond, we may reduce the cash-in value if it is greater than your fair-share of the with-profits fund. We would do this by applying an MVR.
If we didn’t do this, we would pay out more than your Bond is worth. This would reduce the amount available for other customers when they leave the with-profits fund in the future, which would be unfair.
#### When do MVRs not apply?
Importantly, MVRs can only apply if you cash in your investment. MVRs do not apply:
  * from the 10th anniversary of investments made before 1st April 2000
  * if you don’t cash in
  * to payments on death
  * to regular income payments.

Details of the MVR were provided in the Key Features document you received when you made your investment and can also be found in your Terms and Conditions document.
#### How does an MVR apply?
Due to the current economic climate and market conditions there are no MVRs currently being applied on Platinum Bond Plus policies.
#### How do we decide on the level of bonuses and MVRs?
We take decisions about applying an MVR very seriously. All decisions about bonus and MVR rates go through a rigorous governance process which
includes obtaining the approval of our Board of Directors. To ensure that we are fair to our policyholders, we follow the [Principles and Practices of Financial Management (PPFM)](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/governance-and-leadership-teams/corporate-governance/ppfm/ "PPFM").
How long will my money be invested for?
Platinum Bond Plus has no fixed investment term, so you can invest for as long as you like. You should see it as a medium to long-term investment of at least 5 years.
Where will my money be invested?
When you invest in Platinum Bond Plus, we pool your money together with lots of other investors’ money in a ‘with-profits fund'. A team of experienced investment professionals manage the fund.
Our investment strategy is to achieve growth by investing in different types of assets. These include:
  * UK and overseas shares
  * government and other bonds
  * property
  * cash
  * alternative investments and more.

Can I take money out?
Platinum Bond Plus is a medium to long-term investment, not a savings account. You should try to leave your money in for as long as possible to give it the best chance to grow.
But you can make withdrawals, either occasional ‘one-off’ withdrawals, or more often as a regular ‘income’. Remember that any withdrawals you make will lower the amount you get back when you cash your investment in.
Is Royal London covered by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme?
Yes, we're covered by the Scheme. It's designed to protect investors if a financial services company becomes insolvent and can't meet its obligations to you.
The highest level of compensation available from the Scheme is 100% of the value of your claim.
How do you manage the money that I've invested?
Our Principles and Practices of Financial Management (PPFM) documents explain how we manage our funds. They cover the standards we apply to the management of our with-profits business.
You'll find our PPFM and our shorter 'with-profits' guides on our [Principles and Practices of Financial Management page](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/governance-and-leadership-teams/corporate-governance/ppfm/).

If you're looking for more information about your RLCIS investment product, our Frequently Asked Questions may have the answer you're looking for.
  * Investment Bond FAQ
  * Platinum Bond Plus FAQ

Investment Bond FAQ Platinum Bond Plus FAQ
## Investment Bond FAQ
## Investment Bond FAQ
What is an Investment Bond?
An [Investment Bond](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/your-products/manage-your-investment/rlcis-investment-bond/) is a lump-sum investment designed for investment growth. The Investment Bond is provided by Aviva, one of the biggest names in life insurance and pensions in the UK.
It is no longer available to new customers.

Investment Bond is no longer available to new customers. The minimum investment was £5,000 and there was no maximum.
How long will my money be invested for?
The Investment Bond has no fixed term so you can invest for as long as you like. You should see it as a medium to long term investment (5 years or more).
We won't charge you for regular withdrawals of up to 7.5% per year in the first five years. But regular withdrawals above this amount, and any one-off withdrawals, are subject to an early exit charge.
Where will my money be invested?
We arrange The Investment Bond in association with Aviva, who will invest your money.
Aviva will invest your money on your behalf into the funds you choose to make up your Investment Bond. These can include our own Co-operative Investments funds.
You may want to check how the funds you chose are performing. Take a look the [latest fund factsheets](http://www.fundslibrary.co.uk/FundsLibrary.BrandedTools/AvivaConsumer/FundCentral#Price) from Aviva for more information.
Can I take money out?
The Investment Bond is a medium to long-term investment, not a savings account. You should try to leave your money in for as long as possible to give it the best chance to grow.
But you can make withdrawals, either occasional 'one-off' withdrawals, or more often as a regular 'income'. Remember that any withdrawals you make will reduce the amount you get back when you cash your investment in.
How can I find out how my investment is performing?
You can take a look at the [latest fund factsheets online](http://www.fundslibrary.co.uk/FundsLibrary.BrandedTools/AvivaConsumer/FundCentral#Price).
Aviva also send you a statement every year on the anniversary of your investment. This shows the cash-in value for your Bond at the time. You can also get an up-to-date valuation of your Investment Bond whenever you need it, by calling Aviva on **0345 302 1111**.
Is the Investment Bond covered by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme?
Yes. The Scheme was set up to protect investors if a financial services company becomes insolvent and isn't able to meet its obligations to you.
You would be able to make a claim against Aviva if they become insolvent for 100% of the value of your Investment Bond at the time.
Find out more about the [Financial Services Compensation Scheme](https://www.fscs.org.uk/).
## Platinum Bond Plus FAQ
## Platinum Bond Plus FAQ
Platinum Bond Plus is a ‘with profits’ investment. What does that mean?
With-profits investments cushion investors from the sudden ups and downs of the stock market. They use a technique called ‘smoothing’ to even out investment returns over time.
Platinum Bond Plus is a lump-sum, with-profits investment. You invest a lump sum of your money in Platinum Bond Plus. It's then pooled together with the money of lots of other investors into our ‘with-profits fund’.
How much can I invest in Platinum Bond Plus?
Platinum Bond Plus is no longer available to new customers. The minimum investment was £1000 and the maximum investment was £250,000.
How can I find out how my investment is performing?
We send you a statement once a year on the anniversary of your investment. This includes:
  * A cash-in value for your investment at the time
  * Details of any Bonuses and charges we've applied in the previous year
  * A leaflet about how the with-profits fund is performing.

You can also get an up-to-date valuation of your Platinum Bond Plus whenever you need it, by calling us on **0345 605 7777**. We may need to send you your valuation in the post, so this might take a few days.
I’ve heard that Market Value Reductions (MVRs) can sometimes apply to with-profits investments. What does this mean?
In certain circumstances when you cash in your Bond, we may reduce the cash-in value if it is greater than your fair-share of the with-profits fund. We would do this by applying an MVR.
If we didn’t do this, we would pay out more than your Bond is worth. This would reduce the amount available for other customers when they leave the with-profits fund in the future, which would be unfair.
#### When do MVRs not apply?
Importantly, MVRs can only apply if you cash in your investment. MVRs do not apply:
  * from the 10th anniversary of investments made before 1st April 2000
  * if you don’t cash in
  * to payments on death
  * to regular income payments.

Details of the MVR were provided in the Key Features document you received when you made your investment and can also be found in your Terms and Conditions document.
#### How does an MVR apply?
Due to the current economic climate and market conditions there are no MVRs currently being applied on Platinum Bond Plus policies.
#### How do we decide on the level of bonuses and MVRs?
We take decisions about applying an MVR very seriously. All decisions about bonus and MVR rates go through a rigorous governance process which
includes obtaining the approval of our Board of Directors. To ensure that we are fair to our policyholders, we follow the [Principles and Practices of Financial Management (PPFM)](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/governance-and-leadership-teams/corporate-governance/ppfm/ "PPFM").
How long will my money be invested for?
Platinum Bond Plus has no fixed investment term, so you can invest for as long as you like. You should see it as a medium to long-term investment of at least 5 years.
Where will my money be invested?
When you invest in Platinum Bond Plus, we pool your money together with lots of other investors’ money in a ‘with-profits fund'. A team of experienced investment professionals manage the fund.
Our investment strategy is to achieve growth by investing in different types of assets. These include:
  * UK and overseas shares
  * government and other bonds
  * property
  * cash
  * alternative investments and more.

Can I take money out?
Platinum Bond Plus is a medium to long-term investment, not a savings account. You should try to leave your money in for as long as possible to give it the best chance to grow.
But you can make withdrawals, either occasional ‘one-off’ withdrawals, or more often as a regular ‘income’. Remember that any withdrawals you make will lower the amount you get back when you cash your investment in.
Is Royal London covered by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme?
Yes, we're covered by the Scheme. It's designed to protect investors if a financial services company becomes insolvent and can't meet its obligations to you.
The highest level of compensation available from the Scheme is 100% of the value of your claim.
How do you manage the money that I've invested?
Our Principles and Practices of Financial Management (PPFM) documents explain how we manage our funds. They cover the standards we apply to the management of our with-profits business.
You'll find our PPFM and our shorter 'with-profits' guides on our [Principles and Practices of Financial Management page](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/governance-and-leadership-teams/corporate-governance/ppfm/).

# Change of ISA Manager FAQs

  * FCA (Financial Conduct Authority) Register

What is happening, when and why? How the transfer affects you Payments, statements and withdrawals Overflow Account FCA (Financial Conduct Authority) Register
## What is happening, when and why?
## What is happening, when and why?
What is happening?
On 1 October 2021, we changed the ISA Manager of the Platinum Plus ISA from RL Marketing (CIS) Ltd to Royal London Savings Ltd.
Why is Royal London making this change?
Following a review of the different ISAs managed by the Royal London group, we have decided to reduce our number of ISA Managers. To achieve this, we are intending to transfer all ISAs held with RL Marketing (CIS) Ltd to Royal London Savings. Following the transfer, RL Marketing (CIS) Ltd will cease to act as an ISA Manager.
Why Royal London Savings?
Royal London Savings and RL Marketing (CIS) Ltd are both part of the Royal London group. Royal London Savings is an existing, approved ISA manager, authorised and regulated by the Financial Services Authority under reference 191237.
Will all investors be transferring?
Yes, all ISA investors currently managed by RL Marketing (CIS) Ltd will be transferred unless you opt out by transferring to another ISA Manager (see "_Can I opt out of the transfer?_ " under  _How this transfer affects you_).
Which products are affected?
The transfer will only affect you if you have taken out a Royal London Platinum Plus ISA with RL Marketing (CIS) Ltd (formerly the Co-operative Insurance Society Limited). Any investment you may hold in the Platinum Plus Overflow Account is unaffected by this transfer and will remain as part of Royal London Mutual Insurance Society Limited.
Will the cost of making this change be passed on to me?
No. Royal London will pick up all the costs.
Are you making changes to the terms and conditions as a result of the transfer?
No substantive changes will be made to terms and conditions as a result of the transfer. See the full [terms and conditions](https://www.royallondon.com/siteassets/site-docs/rlcis/plat_plus_isa-terms.pdf).
However, we would like to bring to your attention something that we have always done but it hasn’t been documented in our Terms and Conditions. In the event of a death claim being outstanding for more than two (2) months, interest will be added from date of death until payment is made. This is now detailed in our Terms and Conditions. Please refer to section 6.7.
What are the new contact details?
The contact details are not affected by the transfer:
**Telephone:**
0345 605 7777 (UK)
00 44 1625 718 989 (Overseas)
**Address:** Royal London, Churchgate House, 56 Oxford Street, Manchester, M1 6EU
**Online:** [www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/)
I don’t recognise the 00 44 1625 718 989 number, what is it?
This is a head office number for Royal London with the international dialling code added. Alternatively, you can call us on 00 44 345 605 7777. Remember if you are dialling from outside the UK additional charges may apply. Check with your operator before calling us.
## How the transfer affects you
## How the transfer affects you
Do I need to do anything?
No. When the transfer goes ahead, you will keep the same policy number and if you make payments these will continue in the same way. You are not required to make any changes with your bank.
Does the transfer affect the ISA status of my investment?
No. Royal London Savings Ltd is an approved ISA manager and the bulk transfer of the policies will preserve the ISA tax wrapper.
Will the transfer affect the value of my ISA?
No. The terms and conditions of your policies will not change, and investors will still have the potential to earn bonuses on their policies.
Will I still be protected by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS)?
Yes. There will be no change to the protections afforded to investors, including those provided by the FSCS.
Will my money still benefit from Client Money protection?
Yes, nothing will change. Royal London Savings will maintain separate client money accounts for ISA policies. Your money may be held temporarily in one of these accounts whilst we process your instructions and will remain so until you present your cheque at your bank. Funds held in such client money accounts are held on trust and are segregated from our own funds.
I already hold an ISA with Royal London Savings will this be affected
No, any ISA you hold with Royal London Savings is unaffected. If you want to discuss this ISA, the contact points for this remain unchanged.
Can I opt out of the transfer?
Yes, you can opt out by nominating an alternative ISA manager to whom you would like your ISA to be transferred. If you wish to transfer your ISA to an alternative ISA manager before the transfer date, it is your responsibility to ensure you have contacted the proposed ISA manager and opened an account by no later than 1st September.
## Payments, statements and withdrawals
## Payments, statements and withdrawals
Will there be any change to the current payment terms?
No. However, from the transfer date 1st October 2021 any payment should be made payable to Royal London Savings Ltd. If you want to make a payment prior to the transfer date, please let us have your cheque by the 23rd September, to ensure that it can be paid into your ISA without delay.
Please send your payment to Royal London Savings Ltd, Royal London, 5th Floor, Churchgate House, 56 Oxford Street, Manchester, M1 6EU.
Will there be any change to the current withdrawal terms?
No, you can still transfer to another ISA provider at any time, at no charge. You will need to contact your new provider and ask them to send us the necessary paperwork.
Will I continue to get regular statements?
Yes. Statement timings won’t change and will continue to be issued as they are now.
## Overflow Account
## Overflow Account
What is an Overflow Account?
In the case where regular contributions were paid in excess of ISA limits, some customers invested in a Platinum Policy that sits outside the tax-free environment of the ISA by way of an ‘Overflow Account’. Until their closure in 2008, the Overflow Account was used to top-up contributions to an ISA in each tax year up to a maximum of the ISA limit for that tax year.
Does my Overflow Account benefit from the same tax advantages of an ISA?
No. As a non-ISA investment, the tax treatment of Overflow Accounts is different to investments in a Platinum Plus ISA. Although you would have originally taken out your Overflow Account at the same time as an ISA, it has always been outside of an ISA wrapper and does not benefit from the tax advantages. You can find more information in the brochure “Key Features of The Co-operative Platinum Plus”. You will have received this when you invested with us.
How does the transfer affect my Overflow Account?
If you hold a Platinum Plus Overflow Account, this will continue to be administered by The Royal London Mutual Insurance Society Limited and is therefore unaffected by the Transfer. The Royal London Mutual Insurance Society Limited is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority and the Prudential Regulation Authority. Registered in England and Wales number 99064. Registered office: 80 Fenchurch Street, London, EC3M 4BY.
I have an ISA and Overflow Account, can I close one and keep the other?
Yes, you can close one and keep the other.
Can I move the money into my ISA?
No, not directly. You would have to withdraw the money from your Overflow Account first. We would send you this payment. If you are making regular payments to your ISA already, then subject to ISA limits, you may be able to make a further contribution to your ISA with us.
## FCA (Financial Conduct Authority) Register
## FCA register
Where can I find the FCA register to check the details?
<https://register.fca.org.uk/>
When I visit the FCA website to look up Royal London Savings, it warns about cloned firms – is this anything I should be worried about?
No. Clone firms are fake firms set up by scammers using the name, address and 'Firm Reference Number' (FRN) of real companies authorised by the FCA. The FCA also warns consumers to use the phone number on the FCA Register to make contact with an FCA authorised firm so as to be sure they are dealing with the real firm. However, as with anything, please be careful giving out your details and only contact us on the numbers given on the letter we have sent to you or at our address:
**Royal London, Churchgate House, 56 Oxford Street, Manchester, M1 6EU**
