#  Our climate strategy
We will play our part in moving fairly to a sustainable world. This means we are committed to lowering the emissions from our investments and our own business operations, influencing policymakers and the companies we invest in, and developing climate-aware investment solutions.
Climate change presents a threat to the wellbeing of people and the planet, and there’s still a lot to do to reach global goals to limit warming. We want to help our customers invest in a responsible way that meets their needs and is good for society and the environment.
##  Our Climate Transition Plan
We’re committed to playing our part in tackling climate change. Our Climate Transition Plan shows how we will do that. It describes how we will handle the complex challenges presented by climate change and the opportunities presented by a low-carbon future. We created our plan using guidelines from the Transition Plan Taskforce's [framework](https://www.ifrs.org/content/dam/ifrs/knowledge-hub/resources/tpt/disclosure-framework-oct-2023.pdf), which is recognised as best practice in the industry.
[Discover our Climate Transition Plan (PDF)](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/shared/investment/royal-london-climate-transition-plan.pdf)
#### **Hear more about our climate strategy from Barry O'Dwyer, our Group CEO**
Read the transcript
- Barry, great to have you here today to discuss our Climate Transition Plan.
- Yeah, it's good to join you, Jo.
- So we've published our Climate Transition Plan. It describes our climate strategy and the key actions that we need to take this year and beyond. But there's no getting away from, recently we've seen significant shifts in the political landscape, which have led to growing scepticism among some politicians around the urgency of climate action, including the arrival of the new administration in the US, reversing policies, challenging consensus, and as a result, we're seeing global companies are signalling dilution of their climate commitments or just simply staying silent. In that context, people might be questioning why we haven't chosen to delay or even not publish at all our Climate Transition Plan. What would be your response to those questions?
- I think it's a valid challenge. The reality though is that the current political situation probably makes it more important than ever that we publish our Climate Transition Plan. You know, we have benefitted over the last couple of decades from a consensus on the need to take action to tackle climate change. And maybe you're right, maybe you know, consensus is breaking down in certain parts of the world. But from Royal London's perspective, it's really, really important that we retain the confidence of our members, our customers, our clients, that we take this seriously. We have made our commitments to playing our part in moving fairly to a sustainable world, and we need to see those through. You know, I'm very, very pleased with the action that we have taken thus far, but we still have lots more to do. We're dependent, like everybody else is, on government action, and maybe we'll talk a little bit more about that. But we are very, very clear on the commitments that we made, and we are doing our best to fulfil those commitments. It's important though, at all stages, that we're transparent about the progress that we make, and we're clear on the dependencies, who else we need to deliver in order for us to be able to deliver on our plans.
- From the advice of climate scientists and experts, we know that climate change presents significant risks to customer and client investment outcomes, whether that be from the physical risks of climate change or the transition risks, the risks associated with the transition to net zero. It is now widely acknowledged, for example, that the Paris target to limit global temperatures to an increase of one and a half degrees is challenged. It's increasingly unlikely. The global average temperatures in the 12-month period up to the end of April, 2025, hit 1.58 degrees above pre-industrial levels. And the UNFCCC Chief Simon Stiell recently said that progress has been made, but the world is still on a trajectory of global warming of three degrees above pre-industrial times. Some might wonder whether this undermines the viability of our climate strategy. How do you respond to that?
- Well, I suppose we, as well as virtually everybody else, never expected progress to be linear. It was always going to be non-linear in the way that we delivered progress to the Paris ambitions. But also remember that the Paris ambitions were about keeping the temperature increase well below two degrees. Obviously, there was an aspiration to keep it to one and a half degrees, and as you say, that looks increasingly unlikely now. What's important for us is that we manage our transition in a dynamic way. So in other words, we respond to what's happening in the world around us. That means that we might make more progress over certain five-year periods than we make over others. But it is important that we take that long-term perspective. So we have designed our climate strategy to be flexible, to be adaptable so that we can change it as external circumstances change.
- As you've touched on, the success of our climate strategy will be highly dependent on others, particularly policymakers. And we've always been really clear that our progress and commitments are based on the expectation that governments and policymakers will deliver on their commitments to achieve the goals of the Paris Agreement. The UK government, for instance, announced an update last November to its Nationally Determined Contributions, NDCs, now targeting a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions of 81% by 2035 compared to 1990 levels. We played our part in influencing that, we were among the businesses and actually one of the only insurance companies to sign that letter, encouraging the UK government to take that next step. How do you reflect on that growing importance for us to continue to engage with policymakers to drive progress?
- I think this is absolutely central, because without the support of policymakers, without the action of policymakers, then we're going to find it incredibly difficult to deliver on our climate commitments. And the companies that we invest in will find it incredibly difficult to deliver on their climate transition plans. So this is an area of continued focus for us. Now, we are obviously an international investor, but we're a UK-based company and most of our focus is on influencing UK policymakers, UK government. We have had a position of strong consensus on the need for action to combat climate change over the past couple of decades, but that's fraying at the seams. And therefore, part of what we see our job as doing is reinforcing good action from government, positive action on climate change and making sure that they're aware that there is a lot of support for what they're trying to do. But it is a constant battle to make sure that we retain the consensus in the population at large, and then the government follows through on its commitment to create the circumstances where we can implement and support climate transition plans.
- So alongside our engagement with policymakers through our Asset Management business, our engagement with the highest-emitting companies within our portfolio is arguably one of the biggest opportunities we have to influence positive change. We know that divestment versus engagement has been a key question among investors, and we see some investors focusing on exclusions policies. How do you reflect on why our engagement-first approach is the right approach?
- Our Asset Management business has always focused on engagement over disinvestment. The reason for that is pretty simple, which is it's relatively easy to green your portfolio by excluding investments, but selling investments to another investor doesn't actually change real-world emissions. And so the only way to influence companies is by owning them, and by owning some of the world's biggest emitters, we can have an active voice in the boardroom around the need for change. So I think it is consistent with our Purpose and the way that we run Royal London, that we do prioritise engagement over divestment. But that doesn't mean that we don't give the companies that we invest in a bit of a hard time in terms of how serious they are about their climate transition plans. So we look to see have they set emissions targets, are they supportive of the wider transition to net zero, and are they taking meaningful action?
- Our Climate Transition Plan sets out our company's position on investing in fossil fuel companies. What role do you see fossil fuel companies playing in that transition to net zero?
- All companies, all sectors have a role to play. The fossil fuel sector has a particular role to play because these are the companies that have the know-how, the talent, the skills, the operational infrastructure and the capital to both transition away from the old world of fossil fuels, but also transition into a new greener economy. So we do need these companies to transform with us, and for that they need to be supported by a set of government policies that encourages them to transition. And so it's not just local government, or national government policies, it's international co-operation. It is a very complex picture, but we do want to see international co-operation across governments that create the environment for fossil fuel companies to change what they're doing to transition to green energy. And we will continue to engage on that basis. We are focusing on where the opportunities lie for our customers in the transition to net zero. For instance, we've announced our intention to acquire Dalmore Capital, which is a big investor in UK infrastructure because we see that as a growth opportunity for our customers. But really, when you go back to our Purpose, really what we're trying to do is create the environment that our customers will enjoy retiring into. We think that the best outcomes that we will deliver for our customers are outcomes where we play our part in moving fairly to a sustainable world.
- Thanks, Barry. That was a really interesting conversation and I think really demonstrates the importance of our Climate Transition Plan and our part that we have to play in moving fairly to a sustainable world. So thank you.
- Thank you.
##  Our climate commitments
We believe the best future for our customers is one where society achieves the goals of the [Paris Agreement](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/#glossary). We want to support the societal transition to a lower-carbon world, while helping our customers and clients build financial resilience.
Our climate strategy shares how we plan to meet our climate commitments across four key areas:
  * ## Engagement for change
  * ## Net zero investments
  * ## Climate-aware investment solutions
  * ## Net zero operations

###  Engagement for change
**Advancing constructive dialogue with companies, policymakers and our industry to encourage progress**
As an investor, proactively working with companies, policymakers and others on climate-related issues is one of the most important actions we can take to progress our own climate strategy. That’s because our strategy relies heavily on these organisations taking action on climate change, too.
We engage with companies through our Asset Management business, which also runs a dedicated [Net Zero Stewardship Programme](https://www.rlam.com/globalassets/media/literature/reports/Net-Zero-Stewardship-Programme-Climate-Transition-Assessment.pdf) to focus on the highest emitting companies in its investments.
We also encourage policymakers to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, in a way that considers the impact on society.
###  Net zero investments
**Reducing emissions from our investments to achieve net zero by 2050**
There are several ways we can reduce emissions from our investments, by engaging with companies, developing climate-aware investment strategies and improving management of the investment properties we own.
We’re working to halve emissions from our investments by 2030 compared to a 2020 baseline, and to achieve net zero emissions by 2050 ([tCO2e](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/#glossary) /$m invested). We focus on reducing [Scope 1 and 2 emissions](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/#glossary) for listed equity, corporate fixed income and property assets. We also regularly review the possibility of expanding the asset classes included in our commitment as net zero methodologies evolve. Our targets do not cover sovereign debt due to our limited ability to influence changes in countries' emissions.
Our commitment includes assets that are controlled by The Royal London Mutual Insurance Society and are managed on its behalf by Royal London Asset Management Limited, as well as regulated investment funds managed by Royal London Asset Management. Our commitment excludes segregated mandates managed on behalf of external clients, unless those clients have made an explicit commitment to achieving net zero. You can find further details of the basis and assumptions underlying our commitment in our [Climate Report](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/shared/investment/royal-london-climate-tcfd-report-2025.pdf) (PDF).
###  Climate-aware investment solutions
**Developing solutions that enable customers and clients to invest in the low-carbon transition**
Climate-aware investment solutions will help us meet the long-term needs of our customers and clients, as well as wider society, during the transition to a lower-carbon economy. We offer ways for our customers to align their investments with a lower-carbon transition for certain funds and will continue to expand and adapt the options we offer.
###  Net zero operations
**Achieving net zero direct operational emissions by 2030, and for our non-investment value chain by 2050**
To reduce our direct operational emissions to net zero by 2030, we’re improving energy efficiency across our buildings. We’re also committed to buying 100% renewable electricity for our operations by 2025 – a goal that we have achieved.
By 2050, we aim to achieve net zero emissions from our [Scope 3](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/#glossary) non-investment [value chain emissions](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/#glossary), starting with a focus on key areas such as the services we buy, business travel and colleague commuting.
[More about operational emissions](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/our-operational-emissions/)
Our commitments are based on the expectation that governments and policymakers will deliver on their commitments to achieve the goals of the Paris Agreement, and that the required actions don’t go against our legal and regulatory obligations to our members and customers.
##  Responsible investment
We consider environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues in the investment solutions we develop and where we actively use our influence to support progress.
[ Find out more  ](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/investment-options/investing-responsibly/)
##  Our progress
Here we share examples of how we're playing our part in moving fairly to a sustainable world. You can read more about our progress in our [Climate Report](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/shared/investment/royal-london-climate-tcfd-report-2025.pdf) (PDF).
The actions shared in these examples may not apply to specific funds, as each has its own distinct investment objectives. You can find details specific to your funds in the relevant fund prospectus.
  * ## Engagement and net zero investments
  * ## Climate-aware investment solutions
  * ## Nature and biodiversity
  * ## Net zero operations

###  Engagement and net zero investments
**Engaging with the fossil fuels industry**
As part of [our approach to fossil fuel investing](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/shared/investment/royal-london-fossil-fuel-investments-position.pdf) (PDF), we encourage the companies in which we invest to decarbonise. We believe this is a more constructive way for us to contribute to reducing real-world emissions, rather than simply divesting without attempting to influence change.
Through our Net Zero Stewardship Programme, our Asset Management business assesses whether companies have credible climate transition plans. This includes the companies we invest in that are involved in fossil fuel production or that use fossil fuels to generate energy. We consider a plan to be credible if a company is, or is making progress towards, setting emissions reduction targets, supporting the wider transition to net zero, and demonstrating action.
You can read more about the Net Zero Stewardship Programme, including examples of our engagement with companies involved in fossil fuel activities, in Royal London Asset Management's [Stewardship and Responsible Investment Report](https://www.rlam.com/globalassets/media/literature/reports/stewardship-and-responsible-investment-report.pdf) (PDF).
###  Climate-aware investment solutions
**Developing investment solutions that enable our customers to invest in the low-carbon transition**
In 2025, we enhanced our equity tilt strategy by aligning it with our Group net zero ambition, including a 50% emissions reduction target by 2030, and launched a new Global Equity Tilt Fund—bringing total assets under management in these solutions to £42bn as at 31 December 2025.
We also acquired Dalmore Capital, strengthening our Private Assets offering and expanding our role in financing essential UK infrastructure. This supports both diversification and stable income, while facilitating our aim to drive positive environmental impact.
###  Nature and biodiversity
**Investing with nature and climate in mind**
We recognise the role that nature has to play in protecting people and planet. We are working to create greener urban spaces – driven by our nature and biodiversity strategy and roadmap for our Property portfolio, and our £800,000 charitable donation to Groundwork UK. We are considering ways to integrate nature into climate-aware investments – those that give customers and clients opportunities to invest in companies, and other assets, that align with the low-carbon transition or are credibly transitioning.
We have continued to explore natural capital investment opportunities, following the first investment by our Asset Management business into agriculture and natural capital in 2024 – the acquisition of 21,000 acres of prime farmland in a £260m joint venture with South Yorkshire Pension Authority. This has included applying regenerative agricultural practices and opportunities to protect and enhance biodiversity, carbon capture and renewable energy.
###  Net zero operations
**Reducing energy use at our offices**
We’ve reduced our operational emissions by 94% since 2019, as of 20251. Energy use is a big part of these emissions, so we have focused on improving our efficiency and switching to renewable energy sources.
We made our offices more energy efficient through a number of activities, including installing better heating systems and sensors to switch off unused lights.
We also achieved our commitment to purchase 100% renewable electricity. In 2024, we secured guarantees – called Renewable Energy Guarantees of Origin – that all the electricity we bought for our offices was from renewable sources. In 2025, we completed installation of 226 solar panels at our Alderley Park office, generating over 39,000 kilowatt hours of renewable energy.
Read more about [our operational emissions](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/our-operational-emissions/), including our continued focus on energy efficiency and using renewables at our offices.

## Our approach to fossil fuel investments
We look to support a more sustainable future by working with the companies we invest in that are involved in fossil fuel production, or that use fossil fuels to generate energy. Where we feel a company isn’t making enough progress against its plans to reduce greenhouse gas emissions or where there is a risk to our investments, we will take investment action. This can include not investing further in a company, reducing our existing investment, or divesting completely.
For example, in line with the objectives set out in our position statement, we continued to engage with the fossil fuels sector and phased out investment in companies heavily involved in thermal coal during 2025. We also continued to engage with UK policymakers to support policies that promote low-carbon energy.
You can learn more about our approach in our [Fossil Fuel Investments Position](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/shared/investment/royal-london-fossil-fuel-investments-position.pdf) (PDF).
### Glossary
When you’re reading about our climate commitments, these terms are helpful to understand.
Greenhouse gases and carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e)
We use the term ‘greenhouse gases’ to cover a number of gases identified as drivers of climate change by the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change: carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons, sulphur hexafluoride and nitrogen trifluoride.
To make things simple and comparable across businesses and other polluters, we translate the climate impact of all greenhouse gases into a single measure: 'carbon dioxide equivalent' (CO2e). For example, a gas twice as potent as carbon dioxide (from a climate impact perspective) is assigned two tonnes 'CO2e' for every one tonne emitted.
When we discuss ‘greenhouse gases’, ‘carbon’ or ‘emissions’, then usually the CO2e is our best absolute measure.
Greenhouse gas emissions scopes
The [Greenhouse Gas Protocol](https://ghgprotocol.org/sites/default/files/standards/ghg-protocol-revised.pdf) divides emissions into three 'scopes'. These are:
  * **Scope 1** : Emissions resulting directly from our business activities, such as company cars and gas used in our buildings.
  * **Scope 2** : Emissions resulting indirectly through the purchase of energy, such as through generation of the electricity we buy to light and power our buildings.
  * **Scope 3** : All other indirect emissions resulting from our business activities across our value chain, such as the goods and services we buy, travel and waste. Emissions arising from our investments are also part of Scope 3.

Net zero
Put simply, ‘net zero’ means achieving a balance between the amount of greenhouse gases emitted into the atmosphere and the amount removed from it.
Paris Agreement
A legally binding international treaty on climate change adopted by 196 parties at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP21) in December 2015. Its central aim is to strengthen the global response to the threat of climate change by keeping a global temperature rise this century well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and to pursue efforts to limit the temperature increase even further to 1.5°C.
Value chain
The value chain is the series of stages involved in producing a product or service that is sold to consumers, with each stage adding to the value of the product or service.

There are several ways we can reduce emissions from our investments, by engaging with companies, developing climate-aware investment strategies and improving management of the investment properties we own.
We’re working to halve emissions from our investments by 2030 compared to a 2020 baseline, and to achieve net zero emissions by 2050 ([tCO2e](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/#glossary) /$m invested). We focus on reducing [Scope 1 and 2 emissions](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/#glossary) for listed equity, corporate fixed income and property assets. We also regularly review the possibility of expanding the asset classes included in our commitment as net zero methodologies evolve. Our targets do not cover sovereign debt due to our limited ability to influence changes in countries' emissions.
Our commitment includes assets that are controlled by The Royal London Mutual Insurance Society and are managed on its behalf by Royal London Asset Management Limited, as well as regulated investment funds managed by Royal London Asset Management. Our commitment excludes segregated mandates managed on behalf of external clients, unless those clients have made an explicit commitment to achieving net zero. You can find further details of the basis and assumptions underlying our commitment in our [Climate Report](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/shared/investment/royal-london-climate-tcfd-report-2025.pdf) (PDF).
###  Climate-aware investment solutions
**Developing solutions that enable customers and clients to invest in the low-carbon transition**
Climate-aware investment solutions will help us meet the long-term needs of our customers and clients, as well as wider society, during the transition to a lower-carbon economy. We offer ways for our customers to align their investments with a lower-carbon transition for certain funds and will continue to expand and adapt the options we offer.
###  Net zero operations
**Achieving net zero direct operational emissions by 2030, and for our non-investment value chain by 2050**
To reduce our direct operational emissions to net zero by 2030, we’re improving energy efficiency across our buildings. We’re also committed to buying 100% renewable electricity for our operations by 2025 – a goal that we have achieved.
By 2050, we aim to achieve net zero emissions from our [Scope 3](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/#glossary) non-investment [value chain emissions](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/#glossary), starting with a focus on key areas such as the services we buy, business travel and colleague commuting.
[More about operational emissions](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/our-operational-emissions/)
Our commitments are based on the expectation that governments and policymakers will deliver on their commitments to achieve the goals of the Paris Agreement, and that the required actions don’t go against our legal and regulatory obligations to our members and customers.
##  Responsible investment
We consider environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues in the investment solutions we develop and where we actively use our influence to support progress.
[ Find out more  ](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/investment-options/investing-responsibly/)
##  Our progress
Here we share examples of how we're playing our part in moving fairly to a sustainable world. You can read more about our progress in our [Climate Report](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/shared/investment/royal-london-climate-tcfd-report-2025.pdf) (PDF).
The actions shared in these examples may not apply to specific funds, as each has its own distinct investment objectives. You can find details specific to your funds in the relevant fund prospectus.
  * ## Engagement and net zero investments
  * ## Climate-aware investment solutions
  * ## Nature and biodiversity
  * ## Net zero operations

###  Engagement and net zero investments
**Engaging with the fossil fuels industry**
As part of [our approach to fossil fuel investing](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/shared/investment/royal-london-fossil-fuel-investments-position.pdf) (PDF), we encourage the companies in which we invest to decarbonise. We believe this is a more constructive way for us to contribute to reducing real-world emissions, rather than simply divesting without attempting to influence change.
Through our Net Zero Stewardship Programme, our Asset Management business assesses whether companies have credible climate transition plans. This includes the companies we invest in that are involved in fossil fuel production or that use fossil fuels to generate energy. We consider a plan to be credible if a company is, or is making progress towards, setting emissions reduction targets, supporting the wider transition to net zero, and demonstrating action.
You can read more about the Net Zero Stewardship Programme, including examples of our engagement with companies involved in fossil fuel activities, in Royal London Asset Management's [Stewardship and Responsible Investment Report](https://www.rlam.com/globalassets/media/literature/reports/stewardship-and-responsible-investment-report.pdf) (PDF).
###  Climate-aware investment solutions
**Developing investment solutions that enable our customers to invest in the low-carbon transition**
In 2025, we enhanced our equity tilt strategy by aligning it with our Group net zero ambition, including a 50% emissions reduction target by 2030, and launched a new Global Equity Tilt Fund—bringing total assets under management in these solutions to £42bn as at 31 December 2025.
We also acquired Dalmore Capital, strengthening our Private Assets offering and expanding our role in financing essential UK infrastructure. This supports both diversification and stable income, while facilitating our aim to drive positive environmental impact.
###  Nature and biodiversity
**Investing with nature and climate in mind**
We recognise the role that nature has to play in protecting people and planet. We are working to create greener urban spaces – driven by our nature and biodiversity strategy and roadmap for our Property portfolio, and our £800,000 charitable donation to Groundwork UK. We are considering ways to integrate nature into climate-aware investments – those that give customers and clients opportunities to invest in companies, and other assets, that align with the low-carbon transition or are credibly transitioning.
We have continued to explore natural capital investment opportunities, following the first investment by our Asset Management business into agriculture and natural capital in 2024 – the acquisition of 21,000 acres of prime farmland in a £260m joint venture with South Yorkshire Pension Authority. This has included applying regenerative agricultural practices and opportunities to protect and enhance biodiversity, carbon capture and renewable energy.
###  Net zero operations
**Reducing energy use at our offices**
We’ve reduced our operational emissions by 94% since 2019, as of 20251. Energy use is a big part of these emissions, so we have focused on improving our efficiency and switching to renewable energy sources.
We made our offices more energy efficient through a number of activities, including installing better heating systems and sensors to switch off unused lights.
We also achieved our commitment to purchase 100% renewable electricity. In 2024, we secured guarantees – called Renewable Energy Guarantees of Origin – that all the electricity we bought for our offices was from renewable sources. In 2025, we completed installation of 226 solar panels at our Alderley Park office, generating over 39,000 kilowatt hours of renewable energy.
Read more about [our operational emissions](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/our-operational-emissions/), including our continued focus on energy efficiency and using renewables at our offices.

## Our approach to fossil fuel investments
We look to support a more sustainable future by working with the companies we invest in that are involved in fossil fuel production, or that use fossil fuels to generate energy. Where we feel a company isn’t making enough progress against its plans to reduce greenhouse gas emissions or where there is a risk to our investments, we will take investment action. This can include not investing further in a company, reducing our existing investment, or divesting completely.
For example, in line with the objectives set out in our position statement, we continued to engage with the fossil fuels sector and phased out investment in companies heavily involved in thermal coal during 2025. We also continued to engage with UK policymakers to support policies that promote low-carbon energy.
You can learn more about our approach in our [Fossil Fuel Investments Position](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/shared/investment/royal-london-fossil-fuel-investments-position.pdf) (PDF).
### Glossary
When you’re reading about our climate commitments, these terms are helpful to understand.
Greenhouse gases and carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e)
We use the term ‘greenhouse gases’ to cover a number of gases identified as drivers of climate change by the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change: carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons, sulphur hexafluoride and nitrogen trifluoride.
To make things simple and comparable across businesses and other polluters, we translate the climate impact of all greenhouse gases into a single measure: 'carbon dioxide equivalent' (CO2e). For example, a gas twice as potent as carbon dioxide (from a climate impact perspective) is assigned two tonnes 'CO2e' for every one tonne emitted.
When we discuss ‘greenhouse gases’, ‘carbon’ or ‘emissions’, then usually the CO2e is our best absolute measure.
Greenhouse gas emissions scopes
The [Greenhouse Gas Protocol](https://ghgprotocol.org/sites/default/files/standards/ghg-protocol-revised.pdf) divides emissions into three 'scopes'. These are:
  * **Scope 1** : Emissions resulting directly from our business activities, such as company cars and gas used in our buildings.
  * **Scope 2** : Emissions resulting indirectly through the purchase of energy, such as through generation of the electricity we buy to light and power our buildings.
  * **Scope 3** : All other indirect emissions resulting from our business activities across our value chain, such as the goods and services we buy, travel and waste. Emissions arising from our investments are also part of Scope 3.

Net zero
Put simply, ‘net zero’ means achieving a balance between the amount of greenhouse gases emitted into the atmosphere and the amount removed from it.
Paris Agreement
A legally binding international treaty on climate change adopted by 196 parties at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP21) in December 2015. Its central aim is to strengthen the global response to the threat of climate change by keeping a global temperature rise this century well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and to pursue efforts to limit the temperature increase even further to 1.5°C.
Value chain
The value chain is the series of stages involved in producing a product or service that is sold to consumers, with each stage adding to the value of the product or service.
## Sustainability reporting and policies

Additional resources detailing our approach to responsible business.


[Read our reports and policies](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/our-purpose/responsible-business/sustainability-reporting-and-policies/)

#  Our operational emissions
We’re taking action to reduce our emissions from our energy use, travel and our supply chain.
##  Our commitment
We want to play our part in moving fairly to a more sustainable world. While our investments generate most of our emissions, we’re also aware of how our own operations and [value chain](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/our-operational-emissions/#glossary) contribute to climate change.
**To reduce our emissions, we aim to:**
  * achieve net zero [direct operational emissions](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/our-operational-emissions/#glossary) by 2030
  * reach net zero emissions from our [non-investment value chain](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/our-operational-emissions/#glossary) by 2050, following a 50% reduction by 2030 from a 2019 baseline.

We believe the best future for our customers is one where society achieves the goals of the [Paris Agreement](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/our-operational-emissions/#glossary). Our climate commitments are based on the expectation that governments and policymakers will deliver on their commitments to achieve the goals of the Paris Agreement, and that the required actions do not contravene our legal and regulatory obligations to our members and customers. You can find more information on the basis and assumptions underlying our climate targets in our [Climate Report](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/shared/investment/royal-london-climate-tcfd-report-2025.pdf) (PDF).
##  Our strategy
### Operational emissions
We’re focused on managing our office buildings responsibly, as well as reducing emissions from company cars. Since energy use is a large part of our direct operational emissions, we are prioritising using renewable energy and efficiency.
  * ## Energy efficiency
  * ## Electrification
  * ## Energy generation
  * ## Offset residual emissions

###  Energy efficiency
**Ensuring our buildings and vehicles use energy as efficiently as possible**
We aim to reduce energy use by installing more efficient equipment and improving our ways of working. We look for ways to improve energy efficiency measures across our buildings, and to help us do this, we plan to use an energy management system to monitor energy use across our offices more effectively.
###  Electrification
**Using renewable electricity to power our offices and vehicles**
We buy 100% renewable electricity to power our offices. We want to make all our company cars electric. As at 31 December 2025, 82% of our UK cars are already electric and we are aiming for all our UK cars to be electric by 2026.
###  Energy generation
**Installing renewable energy technology**
We’ve installed more than 200 solar panels at our Alderley Park office and will explore opportunities for further renewable energy generation at our offices.
###  Offset residual emissions
**Using carbon offsetting for residual operational emissions**
While we prioritise reducing operational emissions through our own actions, we make use of carbon offsetting for residual emissions. Carbon offsetting is where a reduction in or removal of carbon emissions is used to compensate for emissions made elsewhere. Since 2020, our direct operations have been [carbon neutral](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/our-operational-emissions/#glossary) through the use of offsetting. Looking ahead, we’ll continue to monitor good practice around use of offsets.
### Value chain emissions
We’re working to reduce emissions from the goods and services we buy, from our colleagues commuting and working at home, and from business travel – as these are our greatest sources of value chain emissions.
  * ## Purchased goods and services
  * ## Colleague commuting and homeworking
  * ## Business travel

###  Purchased goods and services
**Supporting our suppliers to meet their net zero targets**
We connect with our suppliers to understand their climate targets and initiatives to reduce emissions. We focus on those who contribute most to our emissions. All our suppliers must accept our Supplier Code of Conduct, which includes our environmental requirements. When choosing a new supplier, we check their environmental performance alongside other considerations, and include our climate expectations in contracts if needed.
###  Colleague commuting and homeworking
**Helping colleagues to choose lower-carbon transport and use energy efficiently at home**
We support colleagues to choose lower-carbon transport and use energy efficiently at home. We offer season-ticket loans for trains, a Cycle to Work scheme, and a UK car scheme for electric or low-emissions vehicles. At our Alderley Park office, we run a shuttle bus from nearby train stations. Colleagues can work from home for 50% of the week, and so we offer advice from an external partner on heating efficiency and home improvement assessments to save carbon and costs.
###  Business travel
**Reducing business travel emissions by travelling less and choosing lower-carbon options**
We encourage colleagues to consider if travel is needed or can be avoided. We promote lower-carbon transport options within our travel booking system – such as choosing trains over flights. Every August, we limit all non-essential business travel. We’re also exploring ways to show colleagues the carbon costs of travel decisions alongside other financial costs.
##  Waste, paper and water
While our investment portfolio generates most of our emissions, we continue to take action to reduce our own operational impact that we control more directly.
We met our 2025 targets for purchase of 100% renewable electricity, and for external paper, waste and water usage. For 2025, our internal paper usage per policy was down 88% from our baseline.

renewable electricity used by our operations.

reduction in our operational emissions since 2019, as of 31 December 2025 (Scope 1 and 2 market-based emissions).
  * 82%
of our UK company cars are electric vehicles, as of 31 December 2025.

reduction in our non-investment value chain emissions since 2019, as of 31 December 2025.

Carbon neutral
Carbon neutral describes the state achieved when an entity that produces carbon emissions removes the same volume of carbon emissions from the Earth’s atmosphere.

#  Our business
Find out more about Royal London Group and see just some of the awards we've won.
## Who we are
We look after 8.5 million life and pension policies. We offer long-term savings, protection and asset management propositions in the UK and Ireland.
We champion the value of impartial advice and a significant proportion of our business is distributed via financial advisers in the UK or brokers in Ireland.
In addition, Royal London Asset Management, as one of the UK's largest asset managers, provides the capability to support Royal London's position as a value-for-money solutions provider.
## Total number of UK policies held
### 8 million
## UK
In the UK, we provide a range of products to customers, employers and pension scheme trustees, primarily through intermediaries.
We also provide protection options including life cover, critical illness cover and income protection.
Our high-quality propositions are supported by strong customer service to help customers protect themselves and their loved ones against potential life shocks, save for the future and manage their wealth in later life.
[Find out more](https://www.royallondon.com/)
## Assets under management (AUM)
### £199bn
## Royal London Asset Management
Royal London Asset Management is one of the UK's leading fund management companies working with a wide range of clients across the globe to achieve their investment goals. Our long-term, client-driven focus means that we have a long-standing commitment to responsible investment. Our investment offering gives clients access to investment solutions from all major asset classes, catering to a broad range of risk appetites, portfolio needs and market conditions.
[Visit Royal London Asset Management](http://www.rlam.com/)
## Total number of Irish policies held
### 485,000
## Royal London Ireland
Royal London Ireland has a strong heritage in Ireland and offers protection and individual pension products via financial brokers who offer impartial advice to best meet customer needs. We work closely with financial brokers to provide long-term value and a first class service to our Irish customers.
[Visit Royal London Ireland](https://www.royallondon.ie/)

#  Our history
Founded in 1861 in a London coffee shop, Royal London began as a friendly society, evolving into a purpose-driven mutual today.
_Our Committee of Management, including our founders, out and about in the 1860s._
## Our story
It began in Victorian Britain, a time where people who couldn’t afford a proper burial would receive what was known as a pauper’s funeral – a basic affair organised by the local parish.
Back then a burial like this was seen to be the ultimate disgrace. So even the poorest people would contribute to a local burial club to avoid a pauper’s funeral at all costs.
Burial clubs eventually became Friendly Societies, and in February 1861, two men named Joseph Degge and Henry Ridge met in London (tradition has it) in a coffee house on City Road, to discuss the formation of a new one.
By the end of that meeting, they’d agreed to form a business that they imagined calling the Royal London Life Insurance and Benefit Society, which was ultimately registered in April 1861 as The Royal London Friendly Society.
## [Gilbert the pelican Our pelican is an integral part of the Royal London brand and he has helped to tell our story for many years. Learn more about Gilbert  ](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/gilbert-the-pelican/)
##  Proud to be mutual
As the business grew, the decision was made in 1908 to convert from a Friendly Society to a [mutual](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/), and we’ve remained that way ever since.
Today, [Royal London](https://www.royallondon.com/) is the largest mutual life, pensions and investment company in the UK, and in the top 30 mutuals globally*, with assets under management of £199bn, 8.5 million policies in force and over 5,000 employees. Figures quoted are as at 31 December 2025.
Mutual companies like Royal London are customer-owned and it influences the decisions we make every day.
*Based on total 2022 premium income. ICMIF Global 500, 2024
[Learn more about our business](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/our-business/)

## 2025 highlights
Our performance in 2025 reflected the positive momentum across our business, as we continued to focus on helping customers make informed choices to build lasting financial resilience.
## £327m Group adjusted operating profit
Up 18% (2024: £277m), supported by the strength of our Pensions business, higher Protection contribution and our first full year in the bulk purchase annuities market.
## £199m ProfitShare payout
ProfitShare will be shared in April 2026 with eligible customers.
## £199bn assets under management (AUM)
Our AUM increased to a record £199bn (2024: £173bn) including £6bn from the acquisition of Dalmore Capital.
## 98% of protection claims paid out
We paid 98% of all protection claims, amounting to more than £821m and over 62,000 claims - for customers, families and businesses.
## 2.4 million members in total
Our total number of members increased by 6% through 2025.
## £3.5m contributed to social impact initiatives
This included extending our partnership with Turn2us, a national charity working to address financial insecurity, by another three years.
> We remain dedicated to helping our customers build their financial resilience and navigate the challenges of a changing and uncertain economic environment.
Isabel Hudson, Chair

[Read our Chair's statement](https://www.royallondon.com/siteassets/site-docs/about-us/annual-reports/annual-report-and-accounts-chairs-statement-2025.pdf)
> We have made great progress, growing and diversifying our business while delivering substantial change. In 2025, we continued to build momentum and lay further foundations to deliver for our customers.
Barry O'Dwyer, Group Chief Executive Officer

#  Investor relations
Here you'll find links to our recent announcements, including our financial results, as well as details about our credit ratings and our debt issuances.
## Investing in our business
As a mutual, you might think that Royal London doesn’t have any investors – and whilst it’s true that we don’t have any shareholders, we do have external investors, who provide us with an important part of our capital base.
External investors support our business and enable us to meet the needs of our customers by investing in our ‘subordinated debt’.
It’s a form of borrowing used by many financial institutions, and means that in the unlikely event of Royal London falling into liquidation, we would only have to pay the debt back after meeting our obligations to our policyholders. We also raise debt in order to support our general business and commercial activities.
The regulators allow this kind of debt to be treated as capital in meeting our regulatory solvency requirements, and Our Board reviews and approves our debt funding strategy while our Finance department maintains our debt programme.
Debt investors can read about our credit ratings and our debt issuances below, and you'll also find some recent financial results too.

##  Subordinated debt
We currently have debt investors, following subordinated debt issues (called ‘Notes’) in 2013, 2015, 2019 and 2023. Most of these are institutional investors, as the Notes cannot be sold directly to retail investors. By ‘subordinated’ we mean that we will pay the claims of our members and policyholders before the claims of these debt investors.
Being a mutual organisation, Royal London cannot issue debt directly. Instead we have established wholly-owned special purpose vehicles (SPVs), guaranteed by The Royal London Mutual Insurance Society Limited. The proceeds of the Notes are on-lent to Royal London from the SPVs on the same interest, repayment and subordinated terms that apply to the Notes.

## Investing in our business
As a mutual, you might think that Royal London doesn’t have any investors – and whilst it’s true that we don’t have any shareholders, we do have external investors, who provide us with an important part of our capital base.
External investors support our business and enable us to meet the needs of our customers by investing in our ‘subordinated debt’.
It’s a form of borrowing used by many financial institutions, and means that in the unlikely event of Royal London falling into liquidation, we would only have to pay the debt back after meeting our obligations to our policyholders. We also raise debt in order to support our general business and commercial activities.
The regulators allow this kind of debt to be treated as capital in meeting our regulatory solvency requirements, and Our Board reviews and approves our debt funding strategy while our Finance department maintains our debt programme.
Debt investors can read about our credit ratings and our debt issuances below, and you'll also find some recent financial results too.

A subordinated debt rating from Moody’s of Baa1(hyb), two notches below the A2 IFSR of Royal London, in line with Moody's standard notching practice for subordinated debt guaranteed by an insurance operating company.

Our Purpose – ‘Protecting today, investing in tomorrow. Together we are mutually responsible.’ – is who we are and why we exist as an organisation. It drives our strategy, shapes our culture and informs our long-term response to trends that influence members, customers, intermediaries and society.
#### Responsible business
We are proudly owned by our customers – and we use our position to drive enduring benefit for them and their families.
[Learn about our approach](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/our-purpose/responsible-business/)
#### Social impact
Through our social impact work, we support initiatives that help build financial resilience and support the fair move to a sustainable world.
[More about our social impact](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/our-purpose/social-impact/)
#### Partnerships
We support partnerships aligned to our values as a purpose-driven, customer-owned business.
[See our partnerships](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/our-purpose/partnerships/)
#### Working at Royal London
Explore our careers site to find out who we are and why it's great to work here.
[View our careers site](https://jobs.royallondon.com/)
### What our Purpose means
Our Purpose sets out the positive outcomes we want to achieve:
### Helping build financial resilience
We help build the financial resilience of customers and support those in wider society.
[ Explore financial resilience  about Helping build financial resilience ](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/our-purpose/financial-resilience/)
### Playing our part in moving fairly to a sustainable world
We continue to champion a just transition' to a low-carbon economy.
[ See our approach  about Playing our part in moving fairly to a sustainable world ](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/our-purpose/responsible-business/)
### Strengthening the mutual choice for customers
We will continue to be the leading advocate of mutuality in our sector.
[ Learn about mutuality  about Strengthening the mutual choice for customers ](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/)

We want to empower millions of people to take better financial decisions, harnessing technology to make it engaging and easy.
We focus on creating propositions that deliver value for customers and clients, offering them a diversified range of products, and driving good outcomes for all of our stakeholders.

#  Our Lions Women's rugby partnership
We are the proud Founding Partner of the first ever British & Irish Lions Women's Team.​
##  Together we're making Herstory​
After 137 years of the Lions Men’s Team, history is being made with the first Lions Women’s Team taking to the pitch in New Zealand in 2027. The team will play five matches in total, including a three-Test series against the Black Ferns:
  * **Saturday 4 September​**
Black Ferns XV v Lions (Whangārei, Semenoff Stadium)​
  * **Saturday 11 September​**
1st Test: Black Ferns v Lions (Auckland, Go Media Mt Smart Stadium)​
  * **Tuesday 14 September​**
Invitational XV v Lions (Hamilton, FMG Stadium Waikato)​
  * **Saturday 18 September​**
2nd Test: Black Ferns v Lions (Wellington, Sky Stadium)​
  * **Saturday 25 September​**
3rd Test: Black Ferns v Lions (Christchurch, One NZ Stadium)

Four unions. One jersey. Herstory in the making.
[Find out more](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/our-purpose/partnerships/lions-womens-founding-partner/)
##  £3 million Levelling the Playing Field Grant​
As part of our British & Irish Lions Women’s Team partnership, we’re investing £3 million in elite player development pathways across England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales. The purpose of this grant is to help develop more elite players and coaches across the four Home Unions to create a more balanced Lions Women's Team when they head to New Zealand in 2027.​
[Find out more](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/our-purpose/partnerships/levelling-the-playing-field-grants/)
##  Royal London Lions Women Engagement Day
We’re investing in an annual gathering of current and future star players and coaches from across the four Home Unions, known as Engagement Day. Ahead of the formation of the first ever Lions Women's Team in 2027, these events are opportunities for prospective Lions players from England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales to help build, shape and define the Lions Women’s programme.​
[Find out more](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/our-purpose/partnerships/lions-women-engagement-day/)
##  Championing Women and Girls’ Rugby Award​
We're also investing in grassroots rugby for women and girls across the UK and Ireland in the run up to the inaugural Lions Women's Tour in 2027. For each year of our sponsorship, one grassroots rugby club from each of the four Home Unions will be awarded a £10,000 grant. The grant will be awarded in recognition of their achievements in grassroots rugby for women and girls, and to help fund future development initiatives in local communities across England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales.
[Find out more](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/our-purpose/partnerships/women-and-girls-grassroots-rugby/)
##  Our Lions Women's story
In 2021, we funded a Feasibility Study to investigate if a British & Irish Lions Women’s team could be formed. Excitingly, the study concluded with positive findings which led to the creation of the historic inaugural Lions Women’s Team​.
[Find out more](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/our-purpose/partnerships/lions-womens-feasibility-study/)
##  Our ambassadors
##  Shaunagh Brown
Shaunagh Brown has been a Royal London ambassador since 2021, when she was a member of the Lions Women’s Feasibility Study steering group. A former gas engineer, firefighter and commercial diver, Shaunagh represented England as a hammer thrower at the 2014 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow before taking up rugby when she was 25 years old. She joined Harlequins in 2017 and made her England debut later that year against Canada. In 2019, she received a full time rugby contract from the Rugby Football Union and went on to earn 30 caps for the Red Roses, including playing in the final of the 2021 Rugby World Cup against New Zealand. Following her retirement from playing, Shaunagh is using her growing media profile to promote women’s sport and is a champion of resilience and inclusion.
##  Aoibheann Reilly
An Ireland rugby international across both XVs and Sevens, Aoibheann Reilly is a qualified sports scientist who shares our passion for women’s sport. A scrum half, Aoibheann has rugby in her blood and has played domestically for Celtic Challenge side Wolfhounds, and for Connacht. Following her Ireland XVs debut in the 2022 Women's Six Nations against Wales, she represented Ireland at the 2022 Rugby Sevens World Cup before returning to XVs and starting every game in the 2024 Women’s Six Nations. Having played a key role in helping Ireland qualify for the 2025 Rugby World Cup, Aoibheann was selected in Ireland's World Cup squad. She made three appearances in the tournament, against France, New Zealand and Japan, as Ireland reached the quarter finals.
##  Rhona Lloyd
Current Scotland international winger Rhona Lloyd has earned more than 60 caps for her country, scoring more than 25 tries. She played a key role in Scotland’s journey to the quarter finals of Rugby World Cup 2025, scoring twice in Scotland’s win against Fiji and once against both England and Canada, the two eventual finalists. Rhona has also represented Great Britain in Sevens and recently signed with Sale Sharks for the 2025/26 Premiership Women’s Rugby season. Outside of rugby, she’s a passionate advocate for mental health and body image in sport and is a co-host of the Women Who Sport podcast which aims to inspire and empower the next generation.
##  Siwan Lillicrap
Swansea-born Siwan Lillicrap is a former Wales rugby captain. Having made her Wales debut in the 2016 Six Nations, Siwan was appointed captain in 2019 and went on to earn 51 caps for her country during her career. She led Wales at multiple major tournaments including the 2021 Rugby World Cup in New Zealand and was the first female rugby player to receive a professional contract from the Welsh Rugby Union. Siwan now plays a key role in developing the next generation of talent as Head of the WRU’s Women’s Performance Pathway. In 2025, she was awarded an honorary degree by Swansea University for her outstanding contributions to Welsh rugby.
## Lions Women's Team FAQs
What is the Lions Women's Team?
The Lions Women's Team will be an international rugby team made up of the best women's rugby players from each of the four Home Unions (England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales). The first ever Lions Women's Team will form in 2027. For context, in men's rugby, there has been a Lions Men's Team since 1888 that comes together every four years for a summer tour.
When and where is the first ever Lions Women's Team's tour taking place?​
The Lions Women's Team's first ever tour will take place from 4 to 25 September 2027 in New Zealand. The tour will see the Lions Women's Team play matches across both North Island and South Island of New Zealand, in Whangārei, Auckland, Hamilton, Wellington and Christchurch.
What are the Lions Women's Team's fixtures for their first ever tour?​
The Lions Women's Team will play five matches in New Zealand, including a three-Test series against the Black Ferns who are New Zealand's national women's rugby team. The tour will also see the Lions play in two non-Test fixtures against a Black Ferns XV and an Invitational XV. The fixtures are as follows:​
  * **Saturday 4 September​**
Black Ferns XV v Lions (Whangārei, Semenoff Stadium)​
  * **Saturday 11 September​**
1st Test: Black Ferns v Lions (Auckland, Go Media Mt Smart Stadium)​
  * **Tuesday 14 September​**
Invitational XV v Lions (Hamilton, FMG Stadium Waikato)​
  * **Saturday 18 September​**
2nd Test: Black Ferns v Lions (Wellington, Sky Stadium)​
  * **Saturday 25 September​**
3rd Test: Black Ferns v Lions (Christchurch, One NZ Stadium)

When will the Lions Women's Team be selected for their first tour in 2027?
With the tour not starting until September 2027, the team won't be selected until some point in 2027.
Who is the Head Coach of the Lions Women's Team?​
The Head Coach of the Lions Women's Team has not been named yet.​

She made three appearances in the tournament, against France, New Zealand and Japan, as Ireland reached the quarter finals.
##  Rhona Lloyd
Current Scotland international winger Rhona Lloyd has earned more than 60 caps for her country, scoring more than 25 tries. She played a key role in Scotland’s journey to the quarter finals of Rugby World Cup 2025, scoring twice in Scotland’s win against Fiji and once against both England and Canada, the two eventual finalists. Rhona has also represented Great Britain in Sevens and recently signed with Sale Sharks for the 2025/26 Premiership Women’s Rugby season. Outside of rugby, she’s a passionate advocate for mental health and body image in sport and is a co-host of the Women Who Sport podcast which aims to inspire and empower the next generation.
##  Siwan Lillicrap
Swansea-born Siwan Lillicrap is a former Wales rugby captain. Having made her Wales debut in the 2016 Six Nations, Siwan was appointed captain in 2019 and went on to earn 51 caps for her country during her career. She led Wales at multiple major tournaments including the 2021 Rugby World Cup in New Zealand and was the first female rugby player to receive a professional contract from the Welsh Rugby Union. Siwan now plays a key role in developing the next generation of talent as Head of the WRU’s Women’s Performance Pathway. In 2025, she was awarded an honorary degree by Swansea University for her outstanding contributions to Welsh rugby.
## Lions Women's Team FAQs
What is the Lions Women's Team?
The Lions Women's Team will be an international rugby team made up of the best women's rugby players from each of the four Home Unions (England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales). The first ever Lions Women's Team will form in 2027. For context, in men's rugby, there has been a Lions Men's Team since 1888 that comes together every four years for a summer tour.
When and where is the first ever Lions Women's Team's tour taking place?​
The Lions Women's Team's first ever tour will take place from 4 to 25 September 2027 in New Zealand. The tour will see the Lions Women's Team play matches across both North Island and South Island of New Zealand, in Whangārei, Auckland, Hamilton, Wellington and Christchurch.
What are the Lions Women's Team's fixtures for their first ever tour?​
The Lions Women's Team will play five matches in New Zealand, including a three-Test series against the Black Ferns who are New Zealand's national women's rugby team. The tour will also see the Lions play in two non-Test fixtures against a Black Ferns XV and an Invitational XV. The fixtures are as follows:​
  * **Saturday 4 September​**
Black Ferns XV v Lions (Whangārei, Semenoff Stadium)​
  * **Saturday 11 September​**
1st Test: Black Ferns v Lions (Auckland, Go Media Mt Smart Stadium)​
  * **Tuesday 14 September​**
Invitational XV v Lions (Hamilton, FMG Stadium Waikato)​
  * **Saturday 18 September​**
2nd Test: Black Ferns v Lions (Wellington, Sky Stadium)​
  * **Saturday 25 September​**
3rd Test: Black Ferns v Lions (Christchurch, One NZ Stadium)

When will the Lions Women's Team be selected for their first tour in 2027?
With the tour not starting until September 2027, the team won't be selected until some point in 2027.
Who is the Head Coach of the Lions Women's Team?​
The Head Coach of the Lions Women's Team has not been named yet.​

#  Responsible business
We aim to use our mutuality for good – by helping customers build their financial resilience, and playing our part in moving fairly to a sustainable world.
Our Purpose – 'Protecting today, investing in tomorrow. Together we are mutually responsible.' – shapes everything we do. From the products we offer and the investments we make, to the initiatives we support.
We are a proudly [mutual](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/) company, owned by our customers. Without the short-term pressures of delivering for shareholders, we focus on delivering long-term benefits for our customers and, where we can, for wider society.
### Our investment beliefs
Our investment beliefs describe what we believe about markets, investing and stewardship. These are convictions that shape our investment strategy and decision making.
### Customer goals
Our customers want investment solutions that align to their financial goals, values, risk and reward preferences, and responsible investment priorities.
### Active management
Customers can achieve better outcomes from active asset management, and a well-diversified portfolio can help safeguard their money.
### Adapting to change
Our investment approach should evolve over time to reflect changing market conditions and customer needs.
### Climate
The best future for our customers is one where we collectively take actions to reach the goals of the Paris Agreement. Read more about our [climate strategy](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/our-climate-strategy/).
### Stewardship and engagement
Active stewardship is a fundamental part of active management – and engaging with companies, where there are issues to be addressed, should be prioritised over excluding them from investment. See our [Responsible Investment and Stewardship Policy](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/shared/investment/responsible-investment-and-stewardship-policy.pdf) and [Exclusions Policy](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/shared/investment/exclusions-policy.pdf).
### Trust and transparency
Transparency and robust governance build trust, and ensure our decisions are focused on delivering better long-term outcomes for our customers.

# Tax strategy
### We've made our tax strategy statement easy to read and jargon-free
**The short version? We always aim to pay the right amount of tax to the right people at the right time, striking a balance between all our stakeholders and ensuring that our customers are being treated fairly.**
We are open and transparent in our approach to tax at all times, and behave responsibly and proactively in our dealings with relevant tax authorities. Our tax strategy is reviewed and signed off by the Board.
If it’s the long version you’re after, our 2025-2026 statement on our tax strategy is available to download and [read in full](https://www.royallondon.com/siteassets/site-docs/about-us/social-responsibility/tax-strategy.pdf "read the Tax Strategy Statement in full").

#  Social impact
Through our social impact work, we drive meaningful change for wider society – helping people to build financial resilience, and helping us to play our part in moving fairly to a sustainable world.
We drive social impact by partnering with Turn2us, Cancer Research UK, Groundwork, and supporting social enterprises through our Changemakers Programme.
As a proudly customer-owned business, we focus on the long term for the benefit of our members, customers and their families – which includes delivering positive societal change.
##  Protecting today with Turn2us
Our partnership with UK charity Turn2us helps us to tackle financial insecurity – by providing practical support and guidance to people who are struggling financially, while working collaboratively across society to influence wider systemic change.
[ Our Turn2us partnership  ](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/our-purpose/social-impact/our-turn2us-partnership/)

Our partnership with Cancer Research UK aims to tackle cancer inequalities, helping protect people from facing health shocks that could prevent them saving for the future.​
[ Our Cancer Research UK partnership  ](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/our-purpose/social-impact/cruk/)
##  Our Changemakers Programme
Our Changemakers Programme develops and invests in bold ideas and sustainable solutions from ambitious social enterprises across the UK and Ireland, in collaboration with the School for Social Entrepreneurs.

Our partnership with Groundwork UK aims to help local people take the lead in revitalising green spaces, enhancing biodiversity and building healthier, more resilient communities.
[ Learn more about our partnership  ](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/our-purpose/social-impact/our-groundwork-partnership/)

committed to our social impact work for each of the past five years, totalling £11m.

donated and raised for Turn2us, helping to normalise asking for financial support and breaking the stigma around financial insecurity.

funded across the UK and Ireland to decrease unequal access to nature for urban communities.

supported and scaled through our Changemakers Programme since 2022.
