### How our lump sum calculator can help you
### See what a lump sum withdrawal would mean for your pension
Look at how any lump sum withdrawal would impact your remaining pension value and pension income.
### Find out how much you can withdraw tax-free
You can take out up to 25% tax-free, and we'll work out how much you'd owe if your lump sum is more than this.
### Make a plan for what to do next
To move forward with your lump sum withdrawal, choose one of the options after deciding how you'd like to take it out.
## How our lump sum calculator works
Our lump sum calculator gives you an idea of what taking a lump sum would mean for your retirement. It works by you inputting some of the information on your situation now and what you want in retirement. Here are some of the key steps.
  * Give us a few details about your lump sum
Tell us what you want the lump sum for, how much you want, and how much your pension is worth.
  * See the impact on your pension
We'll then show you what to expect if you take out a lump sum. You can also change your lump sum amount to see the effect on your pension.
  * Decide what to do next
Once you've reviewed the results, you can take the first step to taking your lump sum. If you're not ready, you can get more guidance from us or a financial adviser.

### About the calculator
This calculator doesn't provide advice or recommendations. What you get when you retire will depend on how your investments perform.
## Who is the lump sum calculator for?
This calculator was made with the following conditions in mind:
  * You're aged 55 or over and live in the UK
  * You haven't withdrawn money from this pension before
  * Your plan doesn't have any safeguarded or protected benefits (for example enhanced tax-free cash or guaranteed annuity rates)
  * You don't have any serious health conditions.

If your pension has safeguarded or protected benefits and you decide to take out a lump sum, it may impact these benefits.
If you have a serious health condition and have a life expectancy less than one year, you may be able to withdraw your entire pension tax-free. [Contact us](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/) for more information and support.

Death in service is a common benefit that employers offer to their staff. It pays a tax-free lump sum to a person of your choice if you die while still employed by the company.
This guide explains how the benefit works, what it means for your family, and how it differs to your life insurance cover.
## What is death in service benefit?
Death in service is a workplace benefit that pays out if you die while employed by the company. Your employer can make this payment directly to your family or to a trust, whether you die at your place of work, or outside it. All that matters is that you’re employed by the company when it happens.
Not all employers offer a death in service benefit, as it’s an additional extra rather than a legal requirement. It can also be offered in different ways. For example, some employers tie it to their workplace pension scheme.
## How much does death in service pay out?
Death in service payments are generally paid to you family as a tax-free lump sum. The amount is calculated as a multiple of your annual salary.
For example, your family could receive a payment of three or four times your typical salary. Keep in mind that the exact amount can change depending on the employer and the industry you work in.
## How is death and service paid out?
This depends on how your employer operates its death in service benefit. If you die while still on the company’s payroll, the money will either be paid directly to a person you’ve nominated (sometimes referred to as your ‘beneficiary’), or paid into a trust.
You can choose who you want to receive the money by completing a nomination of benefits letter. It’s worth noting that if the money is paid to a trust, the trustees will have the final say on this - even if you’ve already nominated a beneficiary.
### What happens if the money goes to a trust?
There are potential benefits if this happens. Your personal situation might have changed since you started working for your employer, so the trustees can make an informed decision about who should get the money. They’ll do this based on the most recent information they have about you.
For example, your situation may change if you get married, have children, separate from a partner, or get re-married.
You don’t have to nominate someone to receive your pay out, but it does help you have more control over the money goes. Our [guide to nominating beneficiaries](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/planning-ahead/estate-planning/the-importance-of-nominating-your-beneficiaries/) has more information about why this is important.
## Do I need life insurance if I have death in service cover?
You can have both at the time, but it’s important to remember that death in service doesn’t protect your family in the same way as life insurance.
There are a few pros and cons to death in service cover that can help you decide whether it’s right for you. They can also help you compare it against your current life insurance policy, as there are some big differences you should be aware of.
### Advantages of the death in service benefit:
  * You don’t need to pay a monthly or annual premium for death in service cover, as your employer pays this for you
  * There’s no need for any medical underwriting, as your company’s HR department will do all the paperwork
  * If you die while employed by the company, a tax-free lump sum can be paid out to your nominated beneficiaries
  * It can give you peace of mind that your family will have more financial security if you die.

### Disadvantages of the death in service benefit:
  * Death in service pay outs tend to be smaller than life insurance pay outs
  * You may not be in the same job forever, so you might lose your cover or move to a less generous cover if you change employer
  * Pay outs are linked to your salary, and may not be enough to support your family after you’re gone
  * The lump sum will be paid into a discretionary trust, which means that it might not go to the family members you’ve nominated
  * Some employers only offer the death in service benefit if you’re a member of their workplace pension scheme
  * You’ll lose your death in service benefit if you move jobs, or if your employer goes into administration.

Keep in mind that death in service cover will pay out on top of your life insurance policy, so there’s no harm in having both.
Not all life insurance policies are the same. You can read our guide to the [different types of life insurance](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/life-insurance-guides/types-of-life-insurance/) to help you find the right kind of cover for you.
## Am I eligible for death in service?
This depends on your employer’s terms. Some companies will make their death in service benefit available to all employees, while others will only offer it to members of their workplace pension scheme.
If you’re interested or want to check if you’re eligible, it’s worth asking your employer or checking your employment contract.
## What to know if you have a mortgage
If you have a mortgage, there are some differences between death in service and life insurance you should be aware of.
With life insurance, you can request that a part of a pay-out is used to clear a portion of your outstanding mortgage balance - before the rest goes to your chosen loved ones. This can be helpful as it takes some of the burden off your family to clear the mortgage after you’re gone.
You can’t do this with death in service cover. While your loved ones may receive a pay out if you die, there’s no guarantee they’ll use it to pay off a portion of the mortgage – which could lead to further financial complications in future.
Our [guide to mortgage protection life insurance](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/life-events/buying-a-house/) has more details you might find useful.
## Always check the terms and conditions
It’s important to check your employment contract carefully. It will help you confirm if you have death in service cover, and help you understand how your cover works.
Death in service schemes can vary, from the level of cover offered, to how the money is paid out. This is why it’s important to understand how you’re covered.
## Biography
John Fitzsimons has been writing about money for more than a decade, as editor of the B2B magazine Mortgage Solutions and then personal finance website loveMONEY. Since going freelance, he has written for the likes of the Sunday Times, Forbes, the Mirror, the Sun, and Moneywise.

You don’t have to nominate someone to receive your pay out, but it does help you have more control over the money goes. Our [guide to nominating beneficiaries](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/planning-ahead/estate-planning/the-importance-of-nominating-your-beneficiaries/) has more information about why this is important.
## Do I need life insurance if I have death in service cover?
You can have both at the time, but it’s important to remember that death in service doesn’t protect your family in the same way as life insurance.
There are a few pros and cons to death in service cover that can help you decide whether it’s right for you. They can also help you compare it against your current life insurance policy, as there are some big differences you should be aware of.
### Advantages of the death in service benefit:
  * You don’t need to pay a monthly or annual premium for death in service cover, as your employer pays this for you
  * There’s no need for any medical underwriting, as your company’s HR department will do all the paperwork
  * If you die while employed by the company, a tax-free lump sum can be paid out to your nominated beneficiaries
  * It can give you peace of mind that your family will have more financial security if you die.

### Disadvantages of the death in service benefit:
  * Death in service pay outs tend to be smaller than life insurance pay outs
  * You may not be in the same job forever, so you might lose your cover or move to a less generous cover if you change employer
  * Pay outs are linked to your salary, and may not be enough to support your family after you’re gone
  * The lump sum will be paid into a discretionary trust, which means that it might not go to the family members you’ve nominated
  * Some employers only offer the death in service benefit if you’re a member of their workplace pension scheme
  * You’ll lose your death in service benefit if you move jobs, or if your employer goes into administration.

Keep in mind that death in service cover will pay out on top of your life insurance policy, so there’s no harm in having both.
Not all life insurance policies are the same. You can read our guide to the [different types of life insurance](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/life-insurance-guides/types-of-life-insurance/) to help you find the right kind of cover for you.
## Am I eligible for death in service?
This depends on your employer’s terms. Some companies will make their death in service benefit available to all employees, while others will only offer it to members of their workplace pension scheme.
If you’re interested or want to check if you’re eligible, it’s worth asking your employer or checking your employment contract.
## What to know if you have a mortgage
If you have a mortgage, there are some differences between death in service and life insurance you should be aware of.
With life insurance, you can request that a part of a pay-out is used to clear a portion of your outstanding mortgage balance - before the rest goes to your chosen loved ones. This can be helpful as it takes some of the burden off your family to clear the mortgage after you’re gone.
You can’t do this with death in service cover. While your loved ones may receive a pay out if you die, there’s no guarantee they’ll use it to pay off a portion of the mortgage – which could lead to further financial complications in future.
Our [guide to mortgage protection life insurance](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/life-events/buying-a-house/) has more details you might find useful.
## Always check the terms and conditions
It’s important to check your employment contract carefully. It will help you confirm if you have death in service cover, and help you understand how your cover works.
Death in service schemes can vary, from the level of cover offered, to how the money is paid out. This is why it’s important to understand how you’re covered.
## Biography
John Fitzsimons has been writing about money for more than a decade, as editor of the B2B magazine Mortgage Solutions and then personal finance website loveMONEY. Since going freelance, he has written for the likes of the Sunday Times, Forbes, the Mirror, the Sun, and Moneywise.

# Power of attorney guide
  * [Why have a power of attorney?](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/planning-ahead/estate-planning/power-of-attorney-guide/#why-have-one)
  * [Power of attorney in England and Wales](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/planning-ahead/estate-planning/power-of-attorney-guide/#england)
  * [Power of attorney in Scotland](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/planning-ahead/estate-planning/power-of-attorney-guide/#POA-in-scotland)
  * [Power of attorney in Northern Ireland](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/planning-ahead/estate-planning/power-of-attorney-guide/#nireland)
  * [Where to find out more](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/planning-ahead/estate-planning/power-of-attorney-guide/#find-out-more)

##  What is power of attorney?
There may come a time when you no longer want or are able to make financial or other decisions for yourself. A power of attorney (POA) enables you to give one or more trusted friends or family members the legal authority to make decisions on your behalf, during your lifetime. This power automatically ceases on your death.
The POA lists all the specific powers you wish these people (your attorneys) to have.
##  Why have a power of attorney?
POA is not just for older and wealthier people anyone can benefit from having one. Imagine a situation where your health failed suddenly or you had a serious accident and were unable to make decisions. Having a POA in place would help your relatives immensely at a difficult time.
If you don t have a POA in place and you lose the ability to make your own decisions, your family or friends would have to go to court to get authority to make decisions on your behalf. This can be a costly, complicated and time consuming process. It is easier if you have already set up a POA that can be used.
The person who makes the POA is called the **donor** and those who act for them are **attorneys**.
## Attorney's duties
Attorneys must:
  * act in the donor's best interest and take reasonable care when making decisions on their behalf
  * act within the terms of the POA
  * keep the donor's finances and possessions separate from their own
  * keep records and accounts.

##  Power of attorney in England and Wales
In England and Wales there are two main types of lasting power of attorney (LPA):
  * a property and financial affairs lasting power of attorney and
  * a health and welfare lasting power of attorney.

### Property and financial affairs
A property and financial affairs LPA covers all aspects of someone's financial wellbeing.
An attorney could find themselves making or helping the donor to make decisions regarding their bills, savings and property. They could find themselves managing the donor's bank accounts, making certain occasional gifts on their behalf or even selling property.
The donor can choose when the property and financial affairs LPA can be used and how. For example, you can give your attorney authority to start making decisions for you right away, at a particular time for a set period, or only once you're no longer able to make decisions yourself.
### Health and welfare
With a health and welfare LPA the attorney makes, or helps the donor to make, decisions around how they are cared for. This could include anything from where they live, how they are cared for and even the day-to-day things such as what they eat. If you need extra support for instance carers to come in during the day then this would fall under the remit of a health and welfare LPA.
Such arrangements can also contain information regarding whether you would receive or reject particular types of treatment and the person acting as an attorney must ensure they understand your wishes.
A health and welfare LPA only takes effect once you're no longer able to make decisions yourself.
### How to make an LPA
There are three steps to making an LPA:
  1. Choose your attorney/s. If someone agrees to be your attorney they must keep records of all the important decisions they make for you.
  2. Fill in the relevant forms (or create online) and get them signed and properly witnessed.


You must have mental capacity at the time you set up the LPA (which means you must understand what you're doing and the consequences of having a LPA). To make sure no one has forced you into signing an LPA, when you complete the forms you will appoint a person to be a certificate provider. This is someone who confirms you know what you're signing and understand the powers it will give your attorneys.
As another safeguard, you can name people who should be informed when an application is made to register your LPA. These should be people who have your best interests at heart and who would speak up to object to the registration if they had any concerns.
You can either pay a solicitor to fill in the forms for you, complete the forms online yourself, download the forms and complete them by hand or ask for the forms to be sent to you by post by phoning the Office of the Public Guardian on [0300 456 0300](tel:%200300%20456%200300).
An LPA can only be used once it's been registered with the Office of the Public Guardian. The donor or attorneys can apply to register the LPA (if the attorneys apply to register it, the donor will be notified and can object if they want to).
You have to pay a fee to register each LPA application unless you receive certain state benefits. If you are on a low income (below £12,000) you only pay half the fee. If you think you may be entitled to a fee reduction or waiver you'll need to complete form LPA120A.
##  Power of attorney in Scotland
In Scotland there are three main types of power of attorney. These are:
  * Continuing power of attorney which allows your attorneys to make decisions for you about your money and/or property. This can include paying bills or managing your savings and investments or arranging repairs to your home or buying/selling property.
  * Welfare power of attorney which covers your health or personal welfare. This can include choosing where you live, what you eat and who you see as well as what medical treatment you receive.
  * Combined power of attorney which enables your attorneys to make both financial and welfare decisions for you.

**To make a power of attorney:**
  * Choose your attorney/s – you can have as little as one attorney or up to as many as you choose. Your attorneys must confirm they are willing to act for you. Your attorneys must keep records of their actions.
  * Draft your power of attorney. You can either use a solicitor or another professional, or you can draw up your own power of attorney. Most solicitors can help you do this and will give you legal advice. If you want to do your own power of attorney, some stationery shops sell power of attorney packs which can be used. But if you do this, make sure you look at the guidance available on the [Office of the Public Guardian website](https://www.publicguardian-scotland.gov.uk/) to avoid any costly mistakes.
  * Have your power of attorney properly witnessed. You will need to be interviewed by either a solicitor or medical practitioner to assess that you fully understand what you are doing. If they are satisfied with this, they will complete and sign a certificate confirming this.
  * Register your power of attorney with the Office of the Public Guardian (Scotland) and pay the registration fee (depending on your circumstances you may be exempt from this). Your solicitor may do this for you or you can do it yourself. If you submit the documents electronically the process is often quicker than if you send them by the post.

##  Power of attorney in Northern Ireland
In Northern Ireland there are two main types of power of attorney:
  * General POA which allows your attorney to make decisions for you about your money and/or property normally for a limited period. The general POA can only be used if the donor has mental capacity, and if the donor becomes mentally incapable it ceases and
  * Enduring POA which allows your attorney to make decisions for you about your money and/or property once you become mentally incapable.

**To make an Enduring power of attorney:**
  * Choose your attorney(s) - you can choose one or more attorney(s)
  * Completion your power of attorney - you can either use a solicitor, purchase from a stationery shop or download from the [Law Society of Northern Ireland](https://lawsoc-ni.org/). You should make sure that the most up-to-date version is used to avoid costly mistakes.
  * Have your power of attorney properly witnessed you will need to sign the form and get your signature witnessed by two independent adults.
  * When you are no longer able to manage your affairs your attorneys need to register the power of attorney with the Office of Care and Protection and pay the registration fee (depending on your circumstances you may be exempt from this).

##  Where to find out more
### England and Wales
You can find out more about lasting power of attorney at [GOV.UK Power of Attorney](https://www.gov.uk/power-of-attorney "Lasting Power of Attorney").
You can use the government’s online service to create your lasting power of attorney at [GOV.UK Make a lasting power of attorney](https://www.lastingpowerofattorney.service.gov.uk/home "MAke a lasting Power of Attorney").
You can download the lasting power of attorney forms to complete by hand at [GOV.UK LPA forms](https://www.gov.uk/lasting-power-attorney-duties "Lasting power of Attorney forms").
Find out about the role of an attorney at [GOV.UK duties](https://www.gov.uk/lasting-power-attorney-duties "Roles whike acting as an attorney").
To claim a reduction in the lasting power of attorney registration fee [GOV.UK fees](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/power-of-attorney-fees).
###
### Scotland
You can find out more about power of attorneys at:
  * [Office of the Public Guardian Scotland](https://publicguardian-scotland.gov.uk/power-of-attorney "What is a Power of Attorney")
  * [mygov.scot](https://www.mygov.scot/power-of-attorney/setting-up-a-power-of-attorney/ "Setting up a Power of Attorney")

To claim a reduction in the power of attorney registration fee visit [Office of the Public Guardian Scotland fee exemption](https://publicguardian-scotland.gov.uk/meta1/fee-exemption "Claim a reduction").
###
### Northern Ireland
You can find out more about power of attorneys at:
  * [nidirect](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/managing-your-affairs-and-enduring-power-attorney)
  * [Department of Justice](https://www.justice-ni.gov.uk/articles/information-enduring-powers-attorney-epa)

To claim a reduction in the enduring power of attorney registration fee visit [Department of Justice](https://www.justice-ni.gov.uk/publications/epa-notes-and-forms).

  * [Why have a power of attorney?](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/planning-ahead/estate-planning/power-of-attorney-guide/#why-have-one)
  * [Power of attorney in England and Wales](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/planning-ahead/estate-planning/power-of-attorney-guide/#england)
  * [Power of attorney in Scotland](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/planning-ahead/estate-planning/power-of-attorney-guide/#POA-in-scotland)
  * [Power of attorney in Northern Ireland](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/planning-ahead/estate-planning/power-of-attorney-guide/#nireland)
  * [Where to find out more](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/planning-ahead/estate-planning/power-of-attorney-guide/#find-out-more)

##  What is power of attorney?
There may come a time when you no longer want or are able to make financial or other decisions for yourself. A power of attorney (POA) enables you to give one or more trusted friends or family members the legal authority to make decisions on your behalf, during your lifetime. This power automatically ceases on your death.
The POA lists all the specific powers you wish these people (your attorneys) to have.
##  Why have a power of attorney?
POA is not just for older and wealthier people anyone can benefit from having one. Imagine a situation where your health failed suddenly or you had a serious accident and were unable to make decisions. Having a POA in place would help your relatives immensely at a difficult time.
If you don t have a POA in place and you lose the ability to make your own decisions, your family or friends would have to go to court to get authority to make decisions on your behalf. This can be a costly, complicated and time consuming process. It is easier if you have already set up a POA that can be used.
The person who makes the POA is called the **donor** and those who act for them are **attorneys**.
## Attorney's duties
Attorneys must:
  * act in the donor's best interest and take reasonable care when making decisions on their behalf
  * act within the terms of the POA
  * keep the donor's finances and possessions separate from their own
  * keep records and accounts.

##  Power of attorney in England and Wales
In England and Wales there are two main types of lasting power of attorney (LPA):
  * a property and financial affairs lasting power of attorney and
  * a health and welfare lasting power of attorney.

### Property and financial affairs
A property and financial affairs LPA covers all aspects of someone's financial wellbeing.
An attorney could find themselves making or helping the donor to make decisions regarding their bills, savings and property. They could find themselves managing the donor's bank accounts, making certain occasional gifts on their behalf or even selling property.
The donor can choose when the property and financial affairs LPA can be used and how. For example, you can give your attorney authority to start making decisions for you right away, at a particular time for a set period, or only once you're no longer able to make decisions yourself.
### Health and welfare
With a health and welfare LPA the attorney makes, or helps the donor to make, decisions around how they are cared for. This could include anything from where they live, how they are cared for and even the day-to-day things such as what they eat. If you need extra support for instance carers to come in during the day then this would fall under the remit of a health and welfare LPA.
Such arrangements can also contain information regarding whether you would receive or reject particular types of treatment and the person acting as an attorney must ensure they understand your wishes.
A health and welfare LPA only takes effect once you're no longer able to make decisions yourself.
### How to make an LPA
There are three steps to making an LPA:
  1. Choose your attorney/s. If someone agrees to be your attorney they must keep records of all the important decisions they make for you.
  2. Fill in the relevant forms (or create online) and get them signed and properly witnessed.


You must have mental capacity at the time you set up the LPA (which means you must understand what you're doing and the consequences of having a LPA). To make sure no one has forced you into signing an LPA, when you complete the forms you will appoint a person to be a certificate provider. This is someone who confirms you know what you're signing and understand the powers it will give your attorneys.
As another safeguard, you can name people who should be informed when an application is made to register your LPA. These should be people who have your best interests at heart and who would speak up to object to the registration if they had any concerns.
You can either pay a solicitor to fill in the forms for you, complete the forms online yourself, download the forms and complete them by hand or ask for the forms to be sent to you by post by phoning the Office of the Public Guardian on [0300 456 0300](tel:%200300%20456%200300).
An LPA can only be used once it's been registered with the Office of the Public Guardian. The donor or attorneys can apply to register the LPA (if the attorneys apply to register it, the donor will be notified and can object if they want to).
You have to pay a fee to register each LPA application unless you receive certain state benefits. If you are on a low income (below £12,000) you only pay half the fee. If you think you may be entitled to a fee reduction or waiver you'll need to complete form LPA120A.
##  Power of attorney in Scotland
In Scotland there are three main types of power of attorney. These are:
  * Continuing power of attorney which allows your attorneys to make decisions for you about your money and/or property. This can include paying bills or managing your savings and investments or arranging repairs to your home or buying/selling property.
  * Welfare power of attorney which covers your health or personal welfare. This can include choosing where you live, what you eat and who you see as well as what medical treatment you receive.
  * Combined power of attorney which enables your attorneys to make both financial and welfare decisions for you.

**To make a power of attorney:**
  * Choose your attorney/s – you can have as little as one attorney or up to as many as you choose. Your attorneys must confirm they are willing to act for you. Your attorneys must keep records of their actions.
  * Draft your power of attorney. You can either use a solicitor or another professional, or you can draw up your own power of attorney. Most solicitors can help you do this and will give you legal advice. If you want to do your own power of attorney, some stationery shops sell power of attorney packs which can be used. But if you do this, make sure you look at the guidance available on the [Office of the Public Guardian website](https://www.publicguardian-scotland.gov.uk/) to avoid any costly mistakes.
  * Have your power of attorney properly witnessed. You will need to be interviewed by either a solicitor or medical practitioner to assess that you fully understand what you are doing. If they are satisfied with this, they will complete and sign a certificate confirming this.
  * Register your power of attorney with the Office of the Public Guardian (Scotland) and pay the registration fee (depending on your circumstances you may be exempt from this). Your solicitor may do this for you or you can do it yourself. If you submit the documents electronically the process is often quicker than if you send them by the post.

##  Power of attorney in Northern Ireland
In Northern Ireland there are two main types of power of attorney:
  * General POA which allows your attorney to make decisions for you about your money and/or property normally for a limited period. The general POA can only be used if the donor has mental capacity, and if the donor becomes mentally incapable it ceases and
  * Enduring POA which allows your attorney to make decisions for you about your money and/or property once you become mentally incapable.

**To make an Enduring power of attorney:**
  * Choose your attorney(s) - you can choose one or more attorney(s)
  * Completion your power of attorney - you can either use a solicitor, purchase from a stationery shop or download from the [Law Society of Northern Ireland](https://lawsoc-ni.org/). You should make sure that the most up-to-date version is used to avoid costly mistakes.
  * Have your power of attorney properly witnessed you will need to sign the form and get your signature witnessed by two independent adults.
  * When you are no longer able to manage your affairs your attorneys need to register the power of attorney with the Office of Care and Protection and pay the registration fee (depending on your circumstances you may be exempt from this).

You can find out more about lasting power of attorney at [GOV.UK Power of Attorney](https://www.gov.uk/power-of-attorney "Lasting Power of Attorney").
You can use the government’s online service to create your lasting power of attorney at [GOV.UK Make a lasting power of attorney](https://www.lastingpowerofattorney.service.gov.uk/home "MAke a lasting Power of Attorney").
You can download the lasting power of attorney forms to complete by hand at [GOV.UK LPA forms](https://www.gov.uk/lasting-power-attorney-duties "Lasting power of Attorney forms").
Find out about the role of an attorney at [GOV.UK duties](https://www.gov.uk/lasting-power-attorney-duties "Roles whike acting as an attorney").
To claim a reduction in the lasting power of attorney registration fee [GOV.UK fees](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/power-of-attorney-fees).

To claim a reduction in the power of attorney registration fee visit [Office of the Public Guardian Scotland fee exemption](https://publicguardian-scotland.gov.uk/meta1/fee-exemption "Claim a reduction").

### Northern Ireland
You can find out more about power of attorneys at:
  * [nidirect](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/managing-your-affairs-and-enduring-power-attorney)
  * [Department of Justice](https://www.justice-ni.gov.uk/articles/information-enduring-powers-attorney-epa)

To claim a reduction in the enduring power of attorney registration fee visit [Department of Justice](https://www.justice-ni.gov.uk/publications/epa-notes-and-forms).

# The importance of nominating your beneficiaries
[ Clare Moffat Pensions and tax expert ](https://www.royallondon.com/author-list/clare-moffat/)
  * [ ](
  *

A nomination of beneficiary form (also sometimes known as an expression of wish form) tells the pension scheme who you would like to receive your pension when you die.
What your beneficiaries get depends on what type of pension scheme you were in. Money from pensions after death are called pension death benefits. We have more information on pension death benefits in [what happens to my pension when I die](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/pension-guides/pension-basics/what-happens-to-my-pension-when-i-die/). An up-to date form can make things easier for loved ones as it could mean pension death benefits are paid out quicker.
## What is a beneficiary nomination or expression of wish form?
A beneficiary nomination or expression of wish form is a form, which can be online or in paper, where you fill in who you would like to receive your pension death benefits. These death benefits don’t need to be paid to one person, and they can be paid to family, friends, charities or a trust.
## Why nominating your beneficiaries matters
Many pensions are currently not part of the estate for inheritance tax purposes. Your will could say that everything goes to one person, but your nomination form could say that you want your pension money to go to someone else.
But in most cases, the pension provider will make the final decision about where the money goes and that’s what keeps it out of the estate. The pension provider will try to make sure that the money goes to who you would want it to. Having an up-to-date form is good evidence of what you want. For more information on the way in which pensions can be set up together with information on income tax payable by beneficiaries, and proposed inheritance tax changes please see [What happens to my pension when I die](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/pension-guides/pension-basics/what-happens-to-my-pension-when-i-die/).
An up-to date form can also mean that pension death benefits are paid out quicker and that will help loved ones.
## When to update your beneficiaries
It’s not only important to write a form but also to review it regularly especially if there are key life events such as;
  * Marriage or civil partnership
  * Divorce or separation
  * New children or grandchildren
  * Death of an existing beneficiary
  * Changes in financial needs or relationships.

Even if nothing has changed then it’s a good idea to keep written evidence that you have checked your form and no changes are needed.
## What happens if you do not nominate anyone?
In most cases, the pension provider will decide if you haven’t filled in a form. That can take a lot more time as they will have to request a lot more evidence to try to understand what your wishes would’ve been.
## Passing your benefits on?
There are two ways to tell us how to pass your benefits on, you can either:
  * Complete our form [online](https://www.royallondon.com/forms/pensions-servicing/group-pensions-beneficiary-form/)
  * Or use our [mobile app](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/online-service/download-our-mobile-app/)

# Frequently asked questions about the application process
## [Health and wellbeing directory Our health and wellbeing directory includes a list of organisations to provide help and support for your physical and mental health. Visit our health and wellbeing directory  ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/help-and-support/health-wellbeing-directory/)
## Need to ask a question?
If you’ve got questions about the application form, please contact your adviser. Your adviser will have experience in completing the application form and will be able to support any questions you have. They can track your progress and once the application form is completed, your adviser will be notified and will let you know about any decisions that we've made.
In the meantime, you can explore the answers to some of the common questions you may have about the application form.
## Frequently asked questions
How long does it take to complete an online application?
It should take between 15 and 25 minutes to complete an online application.
Does the application form save my progress?
Yes, all information is saved, and you can come back to complete the application.
I have tried a cigarette once in my life, do I declare myself as an ex-smoker?
Yes, you should disclose this as ex-smoker. Occasional smokers have no regular pattern and smoke sporadically.
What countries are in the EU?
Learn more about and find an up-to-date list of [member countries](https://europa.eu/european-union/about-eu/countries_en#tab-0-0) (external link).
Do I need to declare the contraceptive pill when being asked: Have you been prescribed medication or treatment for four weeks or more?
No, you do not need to declare the contraceptive pill.
Do I have to say yes if I have a regular test e.g. annual blood tests?
Yes, you need to declare annual/regular tests.
When you’re asking about mental health in the last 5 years e.g. depression, anxiety, stress, or any other mental health conditions, are you looking for a clinical diagnosis only?
No, this question is looking for any time you may have had any of the symptoms relating to the above.
Who do I contact if I have any questions about the application?
Please contact your adviser in the first instance for support with completing your application. If there are specific questions or answers you would prefer not to discuss with your adviser, you can contact our dedicated team. You can email them at underwriting@royallondon.com or call [0345 6094 500](tel:0345%206094%20500). If you're giving us a call, press option 1, then option 1 again. The team are available between 8am and 6pm Monday to Friday.

Not sure how insurance works? Don't know your life insurance from your income protection? Our easy-to-read insurance guides are here to help.

If you’ve got questions about the application form, please contact your adviser. Your adviser will have experience in completing the application form and will be able to support any questions you have. They can track your progress and once the application form is completed, your adviser will be notified and will let you know about any decisions that we've made.
In the meantime, you can explore the answers to some of the common questions you may have about the application form.
## Frequently asked questions
How long does it take to complete an online application?
It should take between 15 and 25 minutes to complete an online application.
Does the application form save my progress?
Yes, all information is saved, and you can come back to complete the application.
I have tried a cigarette once in my life, do I declare myself as an ex-smoker?
Yes, you should disclose this as ex-smoker. Occasional smokers have no regular pattern and smoke sporadically.
What countries are in the EU?
Learn more about and find an up-to-date list of [member countries](https://europa.eu/european-union/about-eu/countries_en#tab-0-0) (external link).
Do I need to declare the contraceptive pill when being asked: Have you been prescribed medication or treatment for four weeks or more?
No, you do not need to declare the contraceptive pill.
Do I have to say yes if I have a regular test e.g. annual blood tests?
Yes, you need to declare annual/regular tests.
When you’re asking about mental health in the last 5 years e.g. depression, anxiety, stress, or any other mental health conditions, are you looking for a clinical diagnosis only?
No, this question is looking for any time you may have had any of the symptoms relating to the above.
Who do I contact if I have any questions about the application?
Please contact your adviser in the first instance for support with completing your application. If there are specific questions or answers you would prefer not to discuss with your adviser, you can contact our dedicated team. You can email them at underwriting@royallondon.com or call [0345 6094 500](tel:0345%206094%20500). If you're giving us a call, press option 1, then option 1 again. The team are available between 8am and 6pm Monday to Friday.

#  Why choose our Business Insurance?
You protect your company photocopier - so why not your key people?
You would probably find it unthinkable not to have insurance protecting your business contents from the effects of fire or burglary.
However, the effect of losing one of your key employees through death, illness or injury could have a much worse impact. Comprehensive cover is vital to help your business recover quickly and minimise the effect on your profits should an unfortunate event happen.
An independent financial adviser can help you decide on the right cover for your business needs.
Please note: Your plan doesn’t have a cash-in value at any time and if you stop paying your premiums your cover will stop.
### Some features of our Business Insurance
  * **Key person protection** - protect a loss in profits or the cost of having to replace an important employee whose long term absence could damage your business in a number of ways.
  * **Business loan protection** - protect your business by having a plan in place to repay a loan in the event of the loss of a key person.
  * **Shareholder/partnership protection** - make sure you don't lose control of your business, and make sure the person covered gets fair value for selling their share of the business if they're too ill to work.
  * **Key person replacement** - If you lose a key person, our Helping Hand support service gives you access to a recruitment specialist, who'll provide you with a list of suitable temporary or permanent replacement candidates within 48 hours.
  * **Standalone Relevant Life cover for employees** - make available tax efficient Life Cover for the benefit of your employees and their family.

## [Key Person Cover Protect your business from the financial impact of losing a key employee through death or illness. Find out more  ](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/business-protection/key-person-cover/)
## [Business Cover Protect your business from the death of a shareholder or partner. Find out more  ](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/business-protection/business-cover/)
## [Relevant Life Cover Provide employees with tax efficient death in service benefits without the need for, or alongside, a pension scheme. Find out more  ](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/business-protection/relevant-life-plan/)
## Helping Hand
We believe good protection is about more than just money. That's why our Helping Hand service also gives you access to independent support like a recruitment helpline which can help with sourcing cover for a key member of staff. And a legal helpline can help with any questions around employment law. Helping Hand is a package of support services and each service is provided by third parties that aren’t regulated by either the Financial Conduct Authority or the Prudential Regulation Authority. These services aren’t part of our terms and conditions and don’t form part of your insurance contract with us, so can be amended or withdrawn at any time. This means that you or your family’s access to these services could be amended or withdrawn by us in the future.
[Find out more](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/life-insurance/advised-life-cover/helping-hand/)
## Value of advice
If you think that our Business Insurance could be right for you the next step is to speak to an independent financial adviser. There are many benefits to independent advice.
[Find out more about the value of advice](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/money-guides/financial-support/getting-financial-advice/)

#  Why choose our Business Cover?
Business Cover allows you to protect your business from the impact of losing a shareholder or partner, whose death or illness would have a significant impact on the business.
Our Business Menu and Relevant Life Plans come with access to our Helping Hand support service.
Designed to be there for you during difficult times, Helping Hand gives you access to a range of support services including recruitment and legal helplines.
These plans are only available through an independent financial adviser, who can help you to understand all your options before you decide on the right cover for you and your business.
Remember these plans don't have a cash-in value at any time and if you stop paying your premiums your cover will stop.
### Some of the benefits of our Business Cover
### Financial security
You can make sure that you or your family get fair value for selling your share of the business if you are too ill to work or die.
### Peace of mind
You can protect yourself against losing control of your business if a shareholder or partner dies or is diagnosed with a critical illness.
### Underwrite Later
Cover can be started straightaway whilst we request any medical evidence we need to fully assess your application - providing you with valuable peace of mind that your business is protected straight away.
#### Helping Hand
The serious illness or death of a key member of staff in your company can have practical and emotional consequences. After all, losing key skills can mean uncertainty for customers and shareholders. We know that being able to take care of key people is just as important as protecting your business financially.
That’s why we give you access to our Helping Hand support service when you take out a Business Menu or Relevant Life Plan.
Helping Hand includes a wellbeing support service, designed to give the plan owner online access to hand-picked early care medical services, so your key people have the help and advice they need to stay healthy and able to work.
##### A Helping Hand with recovery
If, at any time, you (the plan owner), or your partner and children, suffer a serious physical or mental illness, injury or bereavement, Helping Hand will be there to offer support – even if you don’t make a claim.
You can contact RedArc, who’ll give you regular support from a dedicated nurse. They’ll provide tailored and personal support whenever it’s needed, for as long as it’s needed. Your dedicated nurse can also give you relevant literature, help to find useful organisations, and can organise additional services such as therapies, counselling or a second medical opinion, if it’s needed.
Helping Hand is a package of support services and each service is provided by third parties that aren’t regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority or the Prudential Regulation Authority. These services aren’t part of our terms and conditions and don’t form part of your insurance contract with us, so can be amended or withdrawn at any time. This means that you or your family’s access to these services could be amended or withdrawn by us in the future.
[Find out more](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/life-insurance/advised-life-cover/helping-hand/)
#### Waiver of Premium (Sickness)
Waiver of Premium (Sickness) is available as an add-on to our tailored plans and we automatically include it with Key Person Income Protection.
This means if the person covered has an accident or illness that leaves them unable to work or carry out a number of tasks, you won't have to worry about monthly policy payments as we’ll pay these for you. You can decide the amount of time between you stopping work and us paying your premiums. The choices are 4, 8, 13, 26 or 52 weeks.

#  Children's Critical Illness Cover
If you have [Life or Critical Illness Cover](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/illness-income-protection/life-or-critical-illness/) or [Critical Illness Cover](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/illness-income-protection/critical-illness-cover/) you can choose to cover your children with our [Children’s Critical Illness Cover](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/illness-income-protection/critical-illness-cover/childrens-critical-illness/). We offer three levels of cover to meet your needs and budget. And if your needs change, you can add or remove it easily over the phone – without giving us any medical information.
#### Enhanced Children's Critical Illness Cover
Children from birth to age 22, or 23 if in full time education, are covered for child-specific conditions plus our main critical illness conditions, total permanent disability (50% of the amount of Critical Illness Cover, up to £50,000) and the additional conditions on our Critical Illness Cover (50% of the amount of Critical Illness Cover, up to £35,000). This level of cover also includes terminal illness and pays £10,000 on the death of a child. You and your children will also be covered for an extra additional condition – pregnancy complications (£5,000 for each affected pregnancy).
#### **Standard Children's Critical Illness Cover**
Children from birth to age 22, or 23 if in full time education, are covered for the main critical illness conditions on our Critical Illness Cover plus total permanent disability and terminal illness (50% of the amount of Critical Illness Cover, up to £30,000). We'll also pay £5,000 on the death of a child.
#### **No Children's Critical Illness Cover**
If you don’t have any children, or if you don’t have immediate plans to start a family, you can choose not to have Children's Critical Illness Cover as part of your plan.
Our definition of children includes legally adopted children and financially dependent children up to the age of 22, or 23 if in full time education, (whether born before or after the start date of the plan).
If you make a claim for your child, it doesn’t affect your main Critical Illness Cover.
#### Helping Hand
With a Royal London Menu Plan, you’ll have access to our Helping Hand support service.
Helping Hand includes a wellbeing support service, designed to help you maintain a healthy lifestyle. It gives the plan owners online access to a range of hand-picked early care medical services, so you have the help and advice you need to stay fit and healthy and help stop small health issues becoming a big problem.
##### A Helping Hand with recovery
If you (the plan owner), or your partner and children, are going through a difficult time, such as a serious illness, injury or bereavement, Helping Hand will also be there to offer support – even if you don’t make a claim. You can contact RedArc, who’ll give you access to a dedicated nurse. They’ll provide tailored and personal support whenever it’s needed, for as long as it’s needed.
Helping Hand is a package of support services and each service is provided by third parties that aren’t regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority or the Prudential Regulation Authority. These services aren’t part of our terms and conditions and don’t form part of your insurance contract with us, so can be amended or withdrawn at any time. This means that you or your family’s access to these services could be amended or withdrawn by us in the future.

#  Helping Hand
With a Royal London Menu Plan, you'll have access to our Helping Hand support service.
Get 24/7 GP access, nurse support for recovery and bereavement, physical and mental wellbeing support and much more.
## What is Helping Hand?
Helping Hand is a package of services that support your wellbeing and can be used to help you live a healthy lifestyle.
  * Wellbeing service
Help and advice you need to stay fit, healthy and stop small health issues becoming a problem.
  * Helping Hand for recovery
Support from a dedicated RedArc nurse for serious physical or mental illness, injury and bereavement.
  * Independent helplines
Support for when you need a professional opinion or advice related to a career, legal, or healthcare issue.

##  Log in to access Helping Hand
Log in to your My Royal London account to access Helping Hand's services.
[ Log in to My Royal London  ](http://my.royallondon.com/)
### Benefits of Helping Hand's wellbeing service
### Mental wellbeing app
With Thrive, you can get recommendations to help prevent, detect and manage common mental health conditions.
### 24/7 GP service
Speak to a doctor by video, phone or message via HealthHero. Handy if you're struggling to see your GP.
### Physiotherapy advice
TrackActiveMe's app can help diagnose physical injuries and get you access to physiotherapy advice and personalised exercises to support recovery.
### Personalised health report
With LiveSmart, you can gain insight into your nutrition, fitness level, sleep pattern, mental wellbeing and brain function.
## Helping Hand for recovery
If you, your partner or children suffer a serious physical injury, mental illness, disability or bereavement, Helping Hand can help even if you’re not making a claim.

With RedArc, you can get support from a dedicated and experienced nurse who can tailor the support to meet the needs of you or your family for as long as you need it.

Their registered nurses can help in a number of ways like helping you understand your health condition, surgery and treatment options and can support you and your family as you adjust to life during and after illness. Even if you’re condition hasn’t yet been diagnosed, support is available. Conditions include but aren’t limited to:

#  Helping Hand mental and physical wellbeing support during challenging times
[ Helping Hand - an overview  ](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/life-insurance/advised-life-cover/helping-hand/) [ Mental wellbeing  ](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/life-insurance/advised-life-cover/helping-hand/wellbeing-support/#mental) [ Physical wellbeing  ](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/life-insurance/advised-life-cover/helping-hand/wellbeing-support/#physical) [ Financial wellbeing  ](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/life-insurance/advised-life-cover/helping-hand/wellbeing-support/#financial)
We know that things are tough right now so we want to assure you that we’re committed to supporting you through these challenging times.
That’s why we’ve teamed up with Thrive: Mental Wellbeing and TrackActive Me, to give our protection customers access to Thrive and TrackActive Me for free for a period of three months.
##  Mental wellbeing
Thrive: Mental Wellbeing is an NHS approved, clinically effective app designed to help build resilience against common stressors we all may face. It provides personalised goals to reduce your risks, activities to help improve resilience, stress-busting techniques, fun games, and lots more, all of which is based on clinical evidence. And if you’re experiencing difficulties at the moment, Thrive can help you identify them and guide you through ways of coping. Supporting 3.1 million people globally, we hope it’s able to provide some support to you too.
To get started, download the **_Thrive: Mental Wellbeing_** app from the Apple App Store for iPhones or Google Play Store for android phones. Create an account, and use this access code: **royallondon20**
For technical support with the app, email help@thrive.uk.com
##  Physical wellbeing
TrackActive Me helps you prevent or reduce muscle, joint and spine pain, while improving your physical health. Through the app, you can access high quality physiotherapy advice and personalised exercises for all types of injuries and conditions, to help get you back on track. And to support you to be physically strong and mobile, there are a range of other home exercise options, including pilates, yoga and the ‘Stay Strong and Healthy’ programme created based on your profile and preferences.
To access this service, [sign up](https://app.trackactiveme.com/?access_code=royallondon20) or visit [trackactiveme.com](https://www.trackactiveme.com) and sign up using this code: **royallondon20**. Once you’ve signed up on the website, you can download the app from the Apple App Store or Google Play Store.
For technical support, email support@trackactiveme.com
These additional services are for customer use only and will be available to you for a period of three months from the date you download the app, ending at the latest on **31 December 2020**.
##  Financial wellbeing
If you’re struggling financially, that can take its toll on your wellbeing too. Perhaps our [managing your finances guide](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/money-guides/) can help you steer through difficulty.
Maybe you’re thinking about getting your affairs in order but not sure where to start. Our articles on [making a will](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/planning-ahead/estate-planning/making-a-will/) and [power of attorney](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/planning-ahead/estate-planning/power-of-attorney-guide/) might help you.
If you have any questions about your protection needs, having a conversation with your financial adviser is the best place to start. You can also [contact us](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/contact-us/) for questions relating to your plan with us.
Helping Hand is a package of support services, provided by third parties that aren’t regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority. These services aren’t part of our terms and conditions, so can be amended or withdrawn at any time.

#  Insurance
**Help protect the people and lifestyle you love**
Through our range of insurance products, we work for you to help you plan for the unexpected and protect your family, your lifestyle and your future against life’s ups and downs.
## Our insurance products
There are lots of different types of insurance that can help in different situations. Depending on what you choose, life insurance can cover everything from protecting your family's lifestyle if you die to leaving a gift for family or friends or helping pay for your funeral. Other types of insurance can help provide financial security for you, your family or your business if you become ill and can't work.
**We offer three main types of insurance:**
## [Life insurance
  * Pays out money if you die or become terminally ill while covered.
  * Can help provide for your family's financial future, cover mortgage repayments, go towards funeral costs or as a gift.
  * Available through a financial adviser or directly from us.

Find life insurance that's right for you  ](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/life-insurance/)
## [Illness and income protection
  * Pays out a lump sum or regular income if you become critically ill or too injured or ill to work.
  * Can help provide financial stability while you concentrate on getting better.
  * Only available through a financial adviser.

Find illness and income protection to suit you  ](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/illness-income-protection/)
## [Business protection
  * Protects your business from financial loss if a key person becomes ill or dies.
  * Can help to protect your business loans and provide employee cover.
  * Only available through a financial adviser.

Find protection for your business  ](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/business-protection/)

#  Insurance
**Help protect the people and lifestyle you love**
Through our range of insurance products, we work for you to help you plan for the unexpected and protect your family, your lifestyle and your future against life’s ups and downs.
## Our insurance products
There are lots of different types of insurance that can help in different situations. Depending on what you choose, life insurance can cover everything from protecting your family's lifestyle if you die to leaving a gift for family or friends or helping pay for your funeral. Other types of insurance can help provide financial security for you, your family or your business if you become ill and can't work.
**We offer three main types of insurance:**
## [Life insurance
  * Pays out money if you die or become terminally ill while covered.
  * Can help provide for your family's financial future, cover mortgage repayments, go towards funeral costs or as a gift.
  * Available through a financial adviser or directly from us.

Find life insurance that's right for you  ](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/life-insurance/)
## [Illness and income protection
  * Pays out a lump sum or regular income if you become critically ill or too injured or ill to work.
  * Can help provide financial stability while you concentrate on getting better.
  * Only available through a financial adviser.

Find illness and income protection to suit you  ](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/illness-income-protection/)
## [Business protection
  * Protects your business from financial loss if a key person becomes ill or dies.
  * Can help to protect your business loans and provide employee cover.
  * Only available through a financial adviser.

Find protection for your business  ](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/business-protection/)

## Our insurance products
There are lots of different types of insurance that can help in different situations. Depending on what you choose, life insurance can cover everything from protecting your family's lifestyle if you die to leaving a gift for family or friends or helping pay for your funeral. Other types of insurance can help provide financial security for you, your family or your business if you become ill and can't work.

## [Life insurance
  * Pays out money if you die or become terminally ill while covered.
  * Can help provide for your family's financial future, cover mortgage repayments, go towards funeral costs or as a gift.
  * Available through a financial adviser or directly from us.

Find life insurance that's right for you  ](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/life-insurance/)
## [Illness and income protection
  * Pays out a lump sum or regular income if you become critically ill or too injured or ill to work.
  * Can help provide financial stability while you concentrate on getting better.
  * Only available through a financial adviser.

Find illness and income protection to suit you  ](https://www.royallondon.com/insurance/illness-income-protection/)

  * Protects your business from financial loss if a key person becomes ill or dies.

We’re proud of our strong claims record and recognise how important support is during this process. That’s why we give you one dedicated contact to manage your claim from start to finish, helping to make this as easy as possible for you.
## Stories from our customers
Discover how our support goes beyond financial help. Read real stories from people we've supported, offering not just financial relief, but emotional and practical help when it mattered most.
View transcript
My name's Andrew DaSilva. I live in Derby, massive Derby County fan. I've been a financial adviser for just over 30 years now.
Late last summer, I suddenly developed a really bad urine infection. On the back of the infection, the doctor said it'd be wise to be prostate checked as well, which I thought there's nothing wrong. All the results came back in. I went to see the consultant and he said, "Sorry to tell you, but you have got prostate cancer." When you're first told that, your head is absolutely spinning about a hundred miles an hour. Am I going to die? Is this the last year of my life? What about my family?
Offered two types of treatment, radiotherapy or prostate removal, and I opted to go for the prostate removal. Fortunately, I had a critical illness insurance policy with Royal London. It's a policy I'm a great believer in for all my clients, therefore, I had it myself. So as soon as I got my diagnosis, I went straight to the claims team with Royal London. Royal London were really empathetic and helpful from the moment I picked the phone up. I had a dedicated person helping me all the way through the claims process, so they made it clear really early that, yes, this will pay out. I wanted the money to be paid out pre the operation. They were really keen to help me get that payment process done quickly and they paid out the claim within two weeks.
Going into an operation, you're obviously really nervous because you're scared of what else they might find, but going into an operation knowing I had no financial worries at all was a really big help. I had my prostate removed at the end of January. Four weeks later, got a phone call from the nurse. She basically said, "Great news, your cancer's gone and it's not spread anywhere, so from today onwards, you are cancer free." It's one of the most emotional days of my life. It's like your football team winning the last minute away. I found the whole process of Royal London and the claims very easy. It also made the recovery process much smoother because I could completely relax with no financial stress at all. It was a big plus to have had the plan and I'm the proof that it actually does work when you need it.
