# State Pension challenge video updates
Sarah Pennells, our Consumer Finance Specialist, together with customers David, Matt, Kate, Stevie and James, spent a week taking part in the State Pension challenge. The goal was to live on the weekly State Pension amount for 2022/23 for one week to show how this might impact their daily lives.
These videos are all of Sarah’s video diaries and a [selection of our customers’](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/state-pension-hub/participants/) videos, to show how the challenge went.
Day 1
It's the first full day of the State Pension challenge and Sarah, Matthew and Kate have been looking at how far the money they have to live on will go.
Transcript for Sarah, Day 1
It’s the start of my week of living on the State Pension, and I wanted to talk to you about my approach to the challenge. My starting point is to assume that I’m living my retired life today. Now there’s no doubt that the cost-of-living crisis is going to make this challenge harder, so I’ve included in my weekly income any money that the government is giving to people on a State Pension to help with energy bills, or the cost of living. So, in my case that adds up to around £20, on top of the full State Pension of £185.15. In terms of my spending, I’m not including any costs that I won’t be paying when I’ve retired. That means my mortgage and things like work related expenses.
Now, I’ve drawn up a budget so I can see exactly what I have coming in, and what I’m likely to spend. Now I’ve just used a spreadsheet but there are plenty of online budgeting templates if you prefer. I have to say, having seen the budget, I’m a bit nervous about trying to make this money last the week. But I’ll be back tomorrow with another update and I’ll be talking about my food shopping.
Transcript for Matthew, Day 1
In terms of planning for the week ahead, key things I'm trying to do, centred around, having ample food supplies and meals well planned out for two reasons, one to avoid unnecessary takeaways if at all possible, and to also to ensure where possible that there's limited or no food wastage.
I think that latter point is something that is particularly important to do, knowing how fussy my children are when it comes to eating. But also recognising that, you know, good quality food can be put to further use after its initial meal use or that's the hope anyway, but now I'm looking forward to the challenge as the name gives away, and also having a greater perspective on how unfortunately, a lot of the population live in a period of their life where arguably, it should be those best years when they get to enjoy the fruits of their labour.
But at the same time now more than ever, I can only imagine it's particularly difficult and something they would never have envisaged in years gone by. But bring it on. Thank you
Transcript for Kate, Day 1
Hi, I'm Kate. I'm 34. And I'm full time employed as a veterinary nurse. I'm keen to do the pension challenge, just to see how we can work within a budget. I'm quite fortunate that I don't have to, you know, account for every penny, when going shopping and things like that. So, it'll be interesting to see how I work with when I've got quite a tight budget. I've gone through my outgoings and ingoings so weekly income on the pension would be £205. That would include all my discounts and things with the Winter Warmer energy bills and stuff like that. And my outgoings would be £119. That is taken off my mortgage because my mortgage should have hopefully been fully paid by then. I'm hoping to pay it the next 20 years. So, by pension age, I would have cleared my mortgage, so we've taken that off the actual outgoings and that leaves me £85.50 to spend.
Normally I go to the shops a couple of times a week, three or four times a week and just buy bits as and when I need to. I'm quite savvy when it comes to shopping anyway. You know, I hunt for the bargains and buy things that are on offer and things like that anyway, so I'm going to carry on with the way I'm spending generally and see how we do. I haven't planned for a budget yet. I might need to later on in the week, but we'll see how we get on. I plan to go shopping tomorrow and buy fresh bits and bobs to keep me going a little bit. Yeah, we'll see how we get on, exciting.
Day 2
Sarah, Matthew and David have been food shopping on their State Pension budget - how have they found it? Did they need to make any compromises on what they would normally buy?
Transcript for Sarah, Day 2
I'm just back from doing my food shop as part of the State Pension challenge and it's been a really interesting experience because I'm quite comfortable budgeting. And although I'm a bit of a foodie, I really like cooking and certainly like eating food. I'm quite happy to make meals from scratch, I do it all the time and I've done it on quite a tight budget.
So yesterday evening, I went back over my budget, and I looked at the foods that I thought I needed to buy. So, I looked online, to work out exactly how much everything cost. I went to discount supermarket that's just down the road from me. And when I got there, the price of a few items was different from what I expected. And I think in one case, something was out of stock, so I needed to buy a more expensive option.
In another case or two, I think the discount had ended so I was paying full price. So, I ended up spending about £2.50 more than I planned so here's my receipt.
I spent £14.63 and I have got a couple of other bits to buy. And although I don't think of myself as somebody who kind of throws money around when it comes to food, and I certainly try not to waste food.
It just gave me a glimpse into how different things would be if I was to retire just on the State Pension.
Transcript for Matthew, Day 2
Deliberately tried to buy in bulk when it comes to food for two reasons, one is you can probably get more value for money by buying large quantities.
I would imagine, I think that goes without saying, but secondly it allows you to plan out meals, portion sizes, and that has that knock on effect of hopefully reducing or avoiding food wastage altogether.
And that there has helped me massively in working at my budget and planning for the week ahead because I think if you weren't to do that you know it would leave you with the dilemma of obviously spending too much.
But again, having residual food, leftover that effectively goes to waste.
The experience so far has been very cathartic. It certainly focused the mind and has made me realise massively, with a combination of rising prices in conjunction with a fixed limited budget, how difficult it must be.
In regards to making sure that you get as much value as you possibly can out of the expenditure, you can make. So challenging, but not impossible.
Transcript for David, Day 2
Today is day two of the pension challenge, and I have done my weekly shopping which I do every week, obviously, and it just depends on the day when I’m available. But because I usually shop at Sainsbury’s and I know that I see adverts all the time comparing other grocery stores, particularly Aldi and Lidl, I decided to use these as an option.
And whilst I’ve used them in the past, I thought I’m going to devote my entire weekly shopping and see if the adverts are true. And I have to say, looking at my receipts, I’m flabbergasted at the cost, which was just over £16, and that’s well within budget I wanted to spend of £20 that I had allocated.
But I got more for my buck as it were, which is great, and plan to probably shop there again, even after the task. But, yes, there were certain things I couldn’t get that I would have liked to have got.
But generally, by and large, everything that I wanted was there and it just baffled my mind that I’m buying that for a much dearer price than what I’ve got for it at the store. So actually I’ve learned something.
Day 3
Our group are half way through the State Pension challenge - what are the participants spending their money on?
Transcript for Sarah, Day 3
For day three of the State Pension Challenge, I'd like to talk to you in a bit more detail about my bills.
My energy bill is definitely the biggest cost and I was on a fixed price tariff until last month, but since then, my direct debit has risen quite sharply. So, it's now £164 a month or £37 a week.
But, my other costs really add up to, so, my council tax is £26 a week.
My mobile phone is £6.30 a week, and my water bill, one of the few paper bills, I have, is another £5.34.
Now, I reckon I could save some money on my broadband and TV package when I retire because the package I have at the moment, is, is a lot for work and I also added in Netflix, which I could give up if I had to. I own my own car and I don't pay car finance. I own it outright but when I add up the cost of insurance and the MOT and servicing, that's about another £17.
Now it's pretty difficult to work out how much I'm spending on petrol because every time I go to the pumps the price has risen. But I think it's probably about £15 a week at the moment.
Now I've been pretty lucky with my car in that I haven't had any large repair bills over the last couple of years.
But I think what this challenge has shown me is that you definitely need some savings, some fallback to pay those unexpected bills because if I was to get a large repair bill that would really throw out my budget.
Anyway, that's my key takeaway for today. I'll be back again tomorrow, talking about my pets, and what they cost, and whether I can afford them on the State Pension.
Transcript for David, Day 3
Hi. It's the third day of the pension task. I've actually just come home from my yoga class. I took the train that cost me £10, but I'd allocated that in my budget. And the class that I took is also £10, but I've already paid for that in advance. So, I asked them what the concession would be if I was a pensioner.
And I, as far as I'm aware, I would get £2 of that. So, I would have paid effectively, £8 and because I know the yoga instructor, I think it might be a little bit less if I was a pensioner. So, yeah, all in all paid, effectively, £20 for today's activity. I consider it a hobby, but it's also a bit of entertainment, and it keeps me healthy and hopefully young and limber for many years to come. So that’s it for today, my own cost really that I had budget for and has come out of the expenses of the £60 left and I have to live on for the rest of the week.
Day 4
On day 4, Sarah faced a tough question: if she retired on the State Pension, could she afford to keep her beloved dogs?
Transcript for Sarah, Day 4
Hello, as you can see, I've got some company for my day for video.
So, these are my two rescue greyhounds Lottie and Maddie, and they're definitely part of the family. And I do more walking because I have them.
But they are expensive. So, it's not the cost of the dog food that works out. That works out to about £17 a week, but dry dog food, and another £3 or so for the chicken and tinned food.
But my lovely girls are very accident prone, so the vet bills are expensive, I have pet insurance, and that used to cost £130 a month for both of them.
But last month, because I've made a couple of expensive claims in the last year, it went up to £180, that's £43 a week and I couldn't afford that on my State Pension.
Now, not all dogs are as accident prone, of course, but in my case, if I would have paid the vet bills as I went along I'd have paid more, than I'd been doing in premiums, there is help available. The PDSA will give low cost, or sometimes free treatment, depending on your circumstances.
So, my case on the State Pension, I qualify for low-cost help for both my dogs as long as I lived in a PDSA hospital catchment area.
But it has really given me some food for thought, because I definitely would like to have a dog when I retire.
I'll be back with another update tomorrow. Minus the dogs.
Transcript for Stevie, Day 4
Hi. Today is day four of living on the State Pension amount and considering it’s been really hot the last few days and hot today I decided, as I’m working from home, on my lunch break, to put a wash on. I thought I could do quite a few loads and get them dry quite quickly and then to realise that I’ve run out of washing liquid. So, when I went to get some lunch, I realised oh I’ve got to stock up on washing liquid. Although then that was nearly most of my budget for the day gone.
And it does make me think again, like surely if you’re on the State Pension amount, that you can’t afford to wash your clothes and can’t afford to buy necessary products that are absolutely vital like washing powder to wash your clothes and body wash to wash yourself. They’re all extra costs that you need to factor in and surely when all these things start to run out you just wouldn’t have enough in your budget or allowance to get them all. So, that’s quite worrying.
Day 5
As we near closer to the end of the State Pension challenge, what have our participants got planned for the weekend? Have they budgeted enough? Sarah, James and David share how socialising and leisure activities are something we might take for granted.
Transcript for Sarah, Day 5
Hello, for day five of the State Pension challenge video. I've come to my local park, now I come here every day, I walk my dogs here, and I've recently started running again,
So, I do that a few times a week, and I've also signed up to online workout classes, that cost me £16 a month or £3.70 a week.
In terms of my limited socialising budget, I don't really think it's been a problem this week, and that's partly because it's been so hot. And I also did go to work event where I got a meal, And I wouldn't normally go to those kind of things, and think, great, free food, but I sort of did this week because of my limited food budget.
At the weekends, I might meet up with friends on a Friday. We quite often might get a take-away, or one of us will cook. So, this Friday, I can't afford to take away. But I can cook for my friend and myself, the food I've already bought, and that's within my budget.
And I'd also signed up before I knew I was doing this State Pension challenge to an event on Saturday that happens to be free. So, I have got some things booked in, which I'm really pleased about.
Now, I did look in my local area to see what's available for people in their sixties, seventies, and older. And it's kind of a mix of, you know, free walks, and low-cost exercise classes. So costing £4 or £5. Lots of volunteering opportunities. And those kinds of things.
I am feeling a bit apprehensive about my weekend just because I'm much more aware of my budget than I would normally be, but I will do another update and let you know how I get on.
Transcript for James, Day 5
This is day 5 of the State Pension Challenge and again today, there’s not anything new to show so still would have around, let me just check, £52 left to spend for the week. So I guess the thing to kind of think about is how I might use that in retirement which would mostly be for social occasions on the weekend right?
But I’m quite like my dad who is generally pretty happy doing his own thing, his own hobbies at home. Which in my case, I will probably be doing a bit of language learning, playing video games that kind of thing which you know, which I would spend a little bit of money on each month, but not much on a weekly basis. Let’s say even at that cost, you know, £10 to £15 a week. that’s still using amount left over but you know thinking about long-term impact of living on just the State Pension. I mean, it’s like yeah, like I said before, you need nothing to go wrong at all, which is not how the world goes obviously.
Transcript for David, Day 5
It's day five of the pension challenge, and not too much to report today. But I did have to go to the shops again, as I was running out a few things. So, basically, bought the bare essentials. One of them, I actually put back on the shelf, because I realised, I actually didn’t need it. And that was tomato sauce. But I realised I had still had a little left at home, but I ended up spending £14.93. So, whilst I still have just under £40 left, I thought that was still pretty cutting it fine, which has got me a little bit worried for the rest of the weekend.
However, only two more days to go, so it should be okay. Other than that, happy where I'm at. And yeah, I'll just be glad when the week is done to know that I have survived or not.
Day 6
The weekend has arrived but did this mean our participants found it easier or more difficult to stick to the State Pension budget allowance? Hear from Sarah and David about what impact the budget had on their weekend plans.
Transcript for Sarah, Day 6
Hi. It's Saturday, which means it's day six of the State Pension challenge, and I've been thinking about what I've been doing differently this week.
Now, there's lots of things but one example is that on a Saturday morning, I quite often join an online art class once or twice a month. It costs £20 and I absolutely love it! But I've decided not to do it this week because of my tight budget.
Now, at the moment, I'm on track to spend less than the State Pension challenge amount but I'm well aware that living on the State Pension for a week is worlds apart from living on it day to day for the rest of your retired life.
And although I've tried to make this experience realistic, and I've tried to include all my regular spending, there have been some one-off costs, such as my holidays that I haven't included, and those would take me way over my State Pension budget.
Now, I love my job, but when I finally do retire, there's lots that I want to be able to do.
So, one of the things I'm going to do next is to look in real detail at how much the lifestyle I'd like in retirement would cost me, and whether I'm on track to be able to afford it.
Now, I'll be back with a final State Pension challenge update tomorrow.
Transcript for David, Day 6
It's day six of the pension challenge, not too much to report today, but, uh, going out later for a party, as I may have alluded to already and no expense thankfully, because all food is being provided for the party, just a small gift that I've picked up two days ago, and, yeah, ready for that.
Tomorrow should be a challenge, because, it’s end of the week, but probably see what I need to do, and I have to stock up in terms of food. But other than that, all expenses going well and still have a little left in the kitty, which I'm really pleased about.
Day 7
As the State Pension challenge comes to an end, Sarah and Kate reflect on what they discovered, how they felt, and the impact it may have on their future decisions.
Transcript for Sarah, Day 7
Hi, it's Sunday, it's day seven, the last day of the State Pension challenge and I want to tell you how I've done and some next steps.
In all, I've spent £185.12 which is just under the full new State Pension amount of £185.15, but I'm well aware that I've not included things like spending on birthday and Christmas presents, my holidays and my pet insurance, which I couldn't afford on the State Pension.
There are three next steps I'm going to take, and the first is to get a State Pension forecast, and that will tell me how much State Pension I'm on track to get when I retire.
And because the amount of State Pension you get depends on your National Insurance record, it's really important to get a State Pension forecast, and you can do this on the government’s gov.uk website.
My second step is to take my State Pension challenge budget and use it to do a life in retirement budget. So I can work out what the lifestyle I'd like, could cost me.
And the third step is to look at how much income my workplace and private pensions could generate on top of the State Pension, and see if there's a gap between the life I'd like when I retire, and the life I could afford.
And if there is, the State Pension challenge has really incentivised me to do something about it.
Now you can see more State Pension challenge videos and follow our step-by-step guide to getting a State Pension forecast on the State Pension hub on our website, royallondon.com
Transcript for Kate, Day 7
So, my overall experience with a pension challenge is that I could probably survive on the pension. It would be just surviving, I wouldn't have much of a life to go out and do anything with, you know, you'd really have to cut back on things. And I think I’d have cut out my swimming membership and hairdressers ‘appointments, just to, you know, enjoy nicer things, treats and days out with grandchildren, etc. So, and I think could really have to rethink what I'm spending my money on and prioritise it.
When I'm a pensioner, that's going to be another thirty years plus, I'm only 34 at the minute. So, you know, I'm looking at least 65 by the time I come to retire. I don't know what the pension is going to be like by that point. It might still be State Pension, that might have gone. It might just be the workplace pension, I'm not sure. And I don't know how much is in my actual workplace pension. But I just know that I would like to, you know, put as much as I can way now, that can afford, to live as comfortably as they come in the future because, this has not been a nice week, and for trying to put your epic, and then I wouldn't wanna look like this every week. So, that's my final experience of everything.
Transcript for David, Day 7
It's really me it made me think of how I want to spend my pension and how important it will be to budget, which I do anyway, but this seems to really be cutting it fine. I did a calculation on a spreadsheet and worked out that I had £43.14 left. Which to me, I'm happy about.
I'm a saver by nature, so sad as it seems. I'm glad I won the challenge as it were in that sense. But £40, you know, come a few years’ time. I don't think that will be much. And I don't want to be scraping the pennies together just so that I can live a life that, you know, a comfortable life, that I think every pensioner is, is deserving.
So yeah, it's left me with a lot of thoughts.
In a way that makes me think we need to really look at how we either fund pensioners or inform pensions and also make people aware.
I think too many of my contemporaries and the younger generation live in a sense of buy now, pay later. Live for the day. Live your best life now, you know, don't worry about saving for the future.
And that's why I think it's important that people are aware of having their own pensions because the State Pension it's just going to pay for the basics.
Transcript for James, Day 7
This thing hasn't really changed my kind of outlook of what I'm doing anyway, I've been paying into a pension since 2014, I think.
And, uh, I think even, even together enough that would give you kind of an amount equal to the State Pension, on top of the State Pension in the future, would be a huge difference into the quality of life that you can look forward to retirement.
Because, you know, we, we're not working all that time, just have a subsistence kind of, you know, just getting by experience of life, right?
You want, you want to take time to do the things you enjoy.
So, it hasn't changed my perspective, or my goals.
It's just shown me that I'm going to keep doing exactly as I am, so that when, you know, unexpected things do happen, or if I want to try and go on a cruise or something, that I'll hopefully have the money to do that.
We'll see.
Transcript for Matthew, Day 7
So, what it's brought home to me is the need, not to be reliant on the government, wholly and solely, but have some form of strong plan b in the form of retirement saving of a personal nature, and looking to start that as early as possible as well.
Because looking to leave it to the 11th hour, inevitably will result in perhaps greater problems and therefore, planning to fail is failing to plan, as the old adage goes.
So, it's certainly sharpened my focus and ensuring that's the case particularly as the world changes both in a climatic sense but also as prices inevitably get higher and making sure that what we've got keeps pace with that, those changes is more important than ever.
Transcript for Stevie, Day 7
Hi, I've been living on the State Pension wage for the last week, today's the seventh day, and I have kept in with my budget, although that has been extremely difficult.
If I'd done the stuff that I wanted to, bought the stuff I wanted to buy, I would have been out of pocket, maybe, on the third, fourth day.
The whole thing has really made me realise that it's just impossible to survive on the State Pension amount.
I do think it needs to go up in order for people to survive and live a comfortable life at retirement, but if that's not going to happen, to really keep myself safe, I need to plan for my future better.
Even now, at 31, I feel, I need to be really saving more and more in my private pension, and saving alongside that as well.

#  Company pension plan
A company pension plan is a type of workplace pension set up by your employer. You may have also heard this called an occupational pension scheme. The plan is run by trustees on your employer’s behalf. You’ll have an individual account with the plan. And as the scheme is established under trust, your account is held separately from your employer’s business.
Depending on your age and salary, you’ll be automatically enrolled into your employer’s company pension plan. You don’t need to do anything.
What’s more, when you save for your future, your employer will too.
### Making contributions
Your contributions are taken from your salary before tax, so you don't pay any tax on your contributions. These tax savings mean that it costs you less to save for your future.
Let’s look at an example for someone who pays basic rate tax with matched contributions from their employer.
  * You decide to contribute £100 each month.
  * This £100 is taken from your pay before any tax is deducted. This means your tax bill will be lower by £20 (as a 20% tax payer). So your £100 pension contribution will only cost you £80.
  * Your employer agrees to match your contribution, so your £80 quickly becomes £200.

## Top up your pension savings
You can make single contributions and/or regular voluntary contributions into your account at any time, as long as the trustees agree. The amount of tax relief you can benefit from depends on your individual circumstances and may change in the future.
Remember that investment returns are never guaranteed. So while by making a single contribution into your plan there’s a chance your savings could grow, their value can also go down. This means you could get back less than you put in.
#### You could have all your pension savings in one place
You may be able to transfer pension savings from other pension plans into your Royal London pension.
Transfer payments from one pension plan to another don’t receive tax relief. Transferring may not be in your best interests as you could lose valuable benefits which cant be replaced. You should speak to a financial adviser before you make a decision.
Visit our [transfer web page](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/pension-transfers/) to find out more.
## Investing your pension savings
Your pension savings are locked away until you reach age 551 and invested to help them grow.
And the longer your money’s invested, the more time it has to grow. So the earlier you start saving, the better off you could be.
Of course, investment returns are never guaranteed. So while your savings could grow, their value can also go down. This means you could get back less than what you put into your plan.
## Your retirement options
If the trustees agree, you can access your pension savings any time after age 551 – even if you’re still working. And you’ll normally have three main ways to enjoy the money you’ve saved – buy a secure income, dip in when it suits you or take it all as cash. You can also normally take up to a quarter of your pension savings completely tax free.
Find out more about [your retirement options](https://www.royallondon.com/retirement-planning/).
1This will increase to age 57 from 6 April 2028.
##  Share in our success
As a mutual, we think our members should share in our success. So if we do well, we’ll aim to boost your pension savings by adding a share of our profits to your plan each year.
We call it **ProfitShare** and you won’t find it anywhere else.
[ Learn more about ProfitShare  ](https://www.royallondon.com/profitshare/)

#  Group personal pension
A group personal pension is a type of workplace pension set up by your employer. It’s a collection of individual pension plans – and one of these plans will belong to you.
Depending on your age and salary, you’ll be automatically enrolled into your employer’s group personal pension. You don’t need to do anything.
What’s more, when you save for your future, your employer will too.
A pension is one of the most tax-efficient ways to save for your future. And, depending on how your employer's group personal pension is set up, you'll either receive tax relief on your pension contributions or you'll benefit from tax savings through salary exchange. Tax treatment depends on your individual circumstances and could change in the future. Speak to your employer to find out how you make your contributions.
## [Tax relief Each time you save into your plan so will your employer. You'll also receive tax relief from the government. This can help to boost your pension savings. How tax relief works  ](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/workplace-pensions/how-tax-relief-works/)
## [Salary exchange With salary exchange, you agree to give up part of your salary for a pension contribution. As your salary is reduced, you pay less tax and National Insurance Contributions. Your employer will also contribute which can help to boost your pension savings. How salary exchange works  ](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/workplace-pensions/how-salary-exchange-works/)
###
Single contributions
You can make single contributions into your plan at any time. Any single contributions you make will benefit from tax relief – helping to boost your pension savings.
Remember that investment returns are never guaranteed. So while there's a chance your savings could grow, their value can also go down. This means you could get back less than you put in.
### Transfer payments
You may be able to [transfer pension savings](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/pension-transfers/) from other pension plans. This could make it easier for you to keep track of them. Transfer payments from one pension plan to another don't receive tax relief.
Transferring may not be in your best interests as you could lose valuable benefits which can't be replaced. You should speak to a financial adviser before you make a decision.
## Investing your pension savings
Your pension savings are invested and aim to grow.
And the longer your money’s invested, the more time it has to grow. So the earlier you start saving, the better off you could be.
Of course, this isn’t guaranteed. So if your investments perform poorly, you could get back less than you started with.
## Your retirement options
You can normally start taking your pension savings any time after age 55 - even if you're still working. This will change to age 57 from 6 April 2028. And you’ll have three main ways to enjoy the money you’ve invested – buy a secure income, dip in when it suits you or take it all as cash. You can also normally take up to a quarter of your pension savings completely tax free.
Find out more about your [retirement options](https://www.royallondon.com/retirement-planning/).
##  Share in our success
As a mutual, we think our customers should share in our success. So when we do well, we’ll aim to boost your pension savings by adding a share of our profits to your plan each year.
We call this your **ProfitShare.**
[ Learn more about ProfitShare  ](https://www.royallondon.com/profitshare/)

You can make single contributions into your plan at any time. Any single contributions you make will benefit from tax relief – helping to boost your pension savings.
Remember that investment returns are never guaranteed. So while there’s a chance your savings could grow, their value can also go down. This means you could get back less than you put in.
#### Transfer payments
You may be able to [transfer pension savings](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/pension-transfers/) from other pension plans. This could make it easier for you to keep track of them. Transfer payments from one pension plan to another don’t receive tax relief.
Transferring may not be in your best interests as you could lose valuable benefits which can’t be replaced. You should speak to a financial adviser before you make a decision.
## Investing your pension savings
Your pension savings are invested and aim to grow.
And the longer your money’s invested, the more time it has to grow. So the earlier you start saving, the better off you could be.
Of course, this isn’t guaranteed. So if your investments perform poorly, you could get back less than you started with.
## Your retirement options
You can normally start taking your pension savings any time after age 55 - even if you're still working. This will change to age 57 from 6 April 2028. And you’ll have three main ways to enjoy the money you’ve saved – buy a secure income, dip in when it suits you or take it all as cash. You can also take up to a quarter of your pension savings completely tax free.
Find out more about your [retirement options](https://www.royallondon.com/retirement-planning/).
##  Share in our success
As a mutual, we think our members should share in our success. So when we do well, we’ll aim to boost your pension savings by adding a share of our profits to your plan each year.
We call it **ProfitShare** and you won’t find it anywhere else.
[ Learn more about ProfitShare  ](https://www.royallondon.com/profitshare/)

#  How tax relief works
Unlike other types of savings plans, pensions benefit from tax relief.
If you’re a basic rate taxpayer, you’ll automatically get 20% tax relief on money you pay into your pension. So for every £80 you put in; the government will top it up to £100.
Let’s look at an example for Sam. Sam pays basic rate tax and earns £2,000 a month. They pay 5% of their salary into their pension and their employer also pays in 3%.
  * Sam pays £80 into their pension each month
  * They get £20 on top of this in tax relief from the government
  * This means Sam only needs to pay in £80 to get a £100 contribution into their pension
  * Because Sam’s employer also pays into their pension, that original £80 contribution quickly becomes £160.

## Paying more in
With tax relief, the more you pay into your pension, the more help you’ll get from the government to save for your future. Let’s take a look at some more examples for someone paying basic rate tax:
| **You pay**  | **Tax relief added as a boost to your contribution**  | **Total pension contribution**  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| £100  | £25  | £125  |
| £160  | £40  | £200  |
| £240  | £60  | £300  |
The above figures are an example to show you how tax relief works, based on UK income tax rates and bands, excluding Scotland. You should speak to your employer to find out more about your own pension contributions, and how much they’re paying in.
If you pay more than the basic rate of income tax you could benefit from additional tax relief which you can claim from HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC). Remember, tax relief depends on your individual circumstances and where you live in the UK and may change in the future.

4. Important information about changes we are making to your pension plan

#  Important changes we're making to your pension plan
We’re upgrading your Police Mutual workplace pension to bring it in line with our newest workplace pension product Retirement Solutions.
## About the changes
What changes are you making?
We’re upgrading your workplace pension, which you originally took out with Police Mutual, with effect from **1 August 2024** to bring it in line with our newest workplace pension product Retirement Solutions. This will allow you to take advantage of enhanced features and services already available to other workplace customers. Here’s a copy of the [letter](https://www.royallondon.com/siteassets/site-docs/pensions/lt-pp-l-0041-customer-letter.pdf) we sent you earlier this year about the changes.
Why are you making the changes?
We want our longstanding workplace customers like you to have access to the same improved options and experiences as our new workplace customers. We’re upgrading your pension to allow you to access several features you don’t currently have, which could help you to achieve your retirement goals, including:
  * our latest digital offering including access to our [mobile app](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/online-service/download-our-mobile-app/);
  * a comprehensive range of investment options with [ESG](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/investment-options/investing-responsibly/) (environmental, social and governance) considerations;
  * access to our [financial wellbeing guidance](https://www.royallondon.com/articles-guides/financial-wellbeing/) service; and
  * a share in our profits which can boost your retirement savings, which we call ‘[ProfitShare](https://www.royallondon.com/profitshare/)’.

How does Royal London benefit by making these changes?
Mutual companies such as Royal London are customer-owned. This means that a share of our profits goes to customers, not shareholders and it influences the decisions we make every day.
By upgrading our customers' workplace pensions to bring them in line with our newest workplace pension product, we will have fewer legacy pension systems to maintain. We will also have fewer versions of the plan terms and conditions to amend in the future, for example due to a change in pensions legislation or if we want to introduce new features.
We want our longstanding workplace customers like you to have access to the same improved options and experiences as our new workplace customers.
When are you planning on making the changes?
We’re writing to you now to give you as much notice as we can of the changes we are making to your pension. We will also send you a reminder about the upgrade later in the year.
In **August 2024** , unless you have already taken your pension or transferred it to an alternative pension product, we’ll upgrade your pension and send you a **Retirement Solutions** ‘welcome pack’.
You’ll automatically be allocated a new **Retirement Solutions** plan number and this new number will be quoted on all future correspondence you receive from us.
How do I know the changes being made are in my best interests?
We want our longstanding workplace customers like you to have access to the same improved options and experiences as our new workplace customers. We're upgrading your pension to allow you to access several features you don't currently have, which could help you to achieve your retirement goals.
We’ve agreed this approach with the Royal London Independent Governance Committee (IGC) which has a mandate to assess the value for money provided to workplace pension customers like you. We’re making these changes to meet the IGC’s expectations and they’re supportive of this approach.
We’ve also informed our regulator, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) about what we are doing.
Can I opt out of the changes?
No. We’ve agreed with the Royal London IGC that we’ll upgrade all Police Mutual Group Personal Pensions to bring them in line with our Retirement Solutions product. It won’t be possible for you to opt out of the changes for your pension and retain the current terms.
If you don’t want your pension to be upgraded, you can choose to transfer your pension to a different pension product, with Royal London or another provider. Royal London will not apply any exit charges if you choose to transfer your pension. Alternatively, if you are age 55 or over you could choose to access your pension savings.
If you don’t want your pension to be upgraded and instead want to transfer to another pension product or take your pension savings (if age 55 or over) then you must do so by **1 August 2024**.
If you decide that you want to transfer your pension to an alternative pension product, we recommend that you get independent financial advice from a regulated financial adviser. Financial advisers will normally charge you a fee but they should let you know in advance how much their services will cost. If you don’t have a financial adviser, you can [get help finding one](https://www.royallondon.com/find-a-financial-adviser/) on our website.
## What will the changes mean for me?
How will the changes impact my current plan?
We’ve sent you an **'important changes affecting your workplace pension' leaflet (PDF)** which summarises the key differences between the current terms of your plan and the new terms that will apply once the upgrade is made.
If you have any other questions about the changes then don’t hesitate to get in touch.
Will I keep the same plan number?
No, when we upgrade your pension we’ll send you a **Retirement Solutions ‘welcome pack’**.
You’ll automatically be allocated a new **Retirement Solutions** plan number and this new number will be quoted on all future correspondence you receive from us.
Will the charges I currently pay change?
If you are (or were) a Royal London employee, the charges that you pay under your Police Mutual workplace pension will reduce to **0.24%** of your plan value each year once it’s upgraded. This is to bring these in line with the charges being paid under the Royal London staff pension (RL GPP).
Otherwise, the charges you currently pay will not change – they will remain at **0.6%** of your plan value each year.
Will the fund my pension is invested in change?
When the changes are made, your pension will automatically be invested in the **Royal London Long Term** fund which our investment experts have identified as a replacement investment fund that’s the closest match to the fund your pension is currently invested in. The **Royal London Long Term** fund is a new fund we’ve created specifically for the upgrade, but it operates in a similar way as your current investment option within the Police Mutual GPP. For more information, please see the [fund factsheet](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/shared/factsheets/fs5pd0002-with-profits-factsheet.pdf).
Once the changes are made, you don’t have to stay invested in this fund and can choose to switch into an alternative investment option at any time. You can [find more information](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/investment-options/) about the **Royal London Long Term fund** and our alternative options.
Will I still be able to contribute to my pension?
As long as you are resident in the UK:
  * If you aren't currently contributing, you can choose to start making contributions at any point after the changes have been made; or
  * If you are currently contributing, you can continue to do so, including increasing contributions or transferring in other pension plans you may have, after the changes have been made. However, you’ll need to complete and return the declaration and direct debit instruction form.

If you're resident outside of the UK, unfortunately you won't be able to start or increase contributions to your pension.
When will I be able to access my pension benefits?
The minimum pension age is currently age 55. This is the earliest age at which most people can normally access their pension benefits. The government is changing the minimum pension age from age 55 to age 57 from April 2028, however your pension has a protected pension age of 55 and this will be retained as part of the upgrade.
We’ll send you information as you approach your chosen pension age to provide you with information about the different options that are available and to help you to decide what’s best for your personal circumstances.
A guidance service is also available through the government backed website [Pension Wise](https://www.moneyhelper.org.uk/en/pensions-and-retirement/pension-wise) (opens in a new window) for people over age 50.
Will my chosen retirement age change?
Your chosen retirement age won’t change after the upgrade unless you’re already beyond your current chosen retirement age. If this applies to you, we confirmed in the letter that we sent you earlier this year what we’ll change your chosen retirement age on your pension to (in most cases this will be your age at your next birthday), unless you choose to take your pension savings before **1 August 2024** or provide us with an alternative retirement age to use.
What will happen if I need to make changes to my plan before the upgrade?
To make sure that the upgrade happens as smoothly as possible, we may need to defer making certain requested changes for a short period of time until the upgrade has happened.
Here’s examples of some of the servicing deferments that may apply. This is not an exhaustive list and we will always act to ensure you are not detrimentally impacted by any deferment that may occur during this time.
| **Type of change**  | **Examples of the change**  | **What will happen**  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Personal details change  | Change of name, address, marital status, contact details  | Any changes that are advised within **2 weeks** of the upgrade will be applied as part of the upgrade  |
| Plan change  | Making new contributions into your plan  | Any requests within **1 month** of the upgrade will be applied after the upgrade  |
| Plan change  | Changing the chosen retirement age on your plan  | Any changes advised within **2 weeks** of the upgrade will be applied as part of the upgrade  |
To upgrade your pension, we need to transfer it from one administration system to another which can take a few days. During this time it’s unlikely that we will be able to provide you with an up-to-date plan value or process any request to withdraw any funds (if you are age 55 or over). We will, however, keep a log of any such requests made, and process these as soon as the upgrade is complete.
The scheme has changed what does that mean?
Most pension plans (like yours) form part of a registered pension scheme. The scheme is governed by the rules of that scheme and operates in line with current pension and tax legislation.
After the upgrade, your plan will form part of the Royal London Personal Pension Scheme (No2).
Under that pension scheme you will have more flexibility around how you can take your retirement savings when you come to retire.
How can I access a copy of the Retirement Solutions Group Personal Plan terms and conditions?
You can view a copy of the [Retirement Solutions Group Pension Plan terms and conditions](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/consumer/workplace-migration/14gpc25-group-personal-pension-plan-booklet.pdf) (PDF) here.
Why will the upgrade mean that my plan is now written under Scots law?
The terms and conditions applying after the upgrade clearly state that your plan will be governed by Scots Law unless we agree with you that a different law should apply. This is because the trust under which the plan will be administered was established under Scots Law. However, the actual legal framework for pensions is governed by UK wide statute.
In the unlikely event that an issue arises in the future that leads to you taking legal action against Royal London, it is ultimately for the court to decide whether or not it has jurisdiction to hear a case. If, for example, the planholder is based in England and Royal London is registered in England, we cannot envisage any situation where an English court would refuse to hear a case if asked to by a planholder. We can think of no reason why Royal London would insist on a case for a non-Scottish planholder being heard in Scotland – that would breach our Customer Duty obligations.
What is ProfitShare?
When we do well, we'll aim to boost your pension savings by adding a share of our profits to your plan each year. We call this [ProfitShare](https://www.royallondon.com/profitshare/).
Although we can’t guarantee we’ll be able to award ProfitShare every year, our continued strength in how we run our business for our customers means we shared £163 million of our profits over 2 million customers in 2024.
ProfitShare is just one of the ways we express our mutuality. Mutual companies such as Royal London are customer-owned. This means that a share of our profits goes to customers, not shareholders and it influences the decisions we make every day.
What functionality is available under the Royal London mobile app?
Our [mobile app](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/online-service/download-our-mobile-app/) isn’t just about showing you what you’ve got - it’s about helping you plan for your future and putting the power in your hands.
You can use our app to explore different outlooks based on your investment approach as well as contributions you’ve made, or money you’ve taken out. And the benefits don’t stop there. As a mutual we aim to put you first so our mobile app also provides you with helpful guides, covering key topics like budgeting, dealing with life events or even helping you get started with investing.
Can I choose to transfer my Police Mutual GPP into my existing Retirement Solutions plan?
Yes, you can transfer your Police Mutual GPP into another pension, including an existing Retirement Solutions plan or Royal London staff pension (RL GPP) at any time.
If you’re a current or former Royal London employee you’re likely to already have a staff pension plan (RL GPP) or Retirement Solutions plan relating to that employment and you can choose to transfer your Police Mutual GPP into that plan at any time. If you don’t transfer into this plan we will upgrade your Police Mutual GPP to a Retirement Solutions GPP and this would then mean you’d continue to have two plans.
## What do I need to do now?
I’m still contributing to my pension and want to proceed with the upgrade
If you're happy for us to upgrade the terms of your workplace pension, please complete and return the **declaration and direct debit instruction form** we sent you as soon as possible.
You can either post the form back to us using the pre-paid envelope or alternatively you can [upload a copy](http://www.royallondon.com/workplaceupgrade) of the completed form online. We require the form to be returned so your regular contributions can continue.
I’m no longer contributing to my pension and want to proceed with the upgrade
If you're happy for us to upgrade the terms of your workplace pension you don't need to do anything else.
I don’t want you to proceed with the upgrade
If you don’t want us to upgrade the terms of your workplace pension, you’ll need to take steps to transfer your pension to an alternative pension product before **1 August 2024**. This is because you won’t have the option to opt out and stay on your existing terms.
We have alternative pension products that may be suitable, or you can consider an alternative pension product with another provider.
There will be no exit charge or penalty applied if you decide to transfer your pension to an alternative pension product with us or another provider.
## Need further information?
Who is Royal London?
Royal London is the largest mutual life, pensions, and investment company in the UK.
More information about Royal London and what we stand for can be [found on our website](https://www.royallondon.com/).
Where can I find out more about Retirement Solutions?
You can read the Retirement Solutions Group Pension Plan [key features document](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/adviser/key-features/14kfi26-group-personal-pension-key-features.pdf) (PDF) here.
How can I contact you if I have any queries?
We can provide general information about the upgrade however we cannot provide advice about what is best for you.
You can get in touch by emailing gpp.transfer@pmas.co.uk or by calling [01543 441 630](tel:01543%20441%20630).
I want independent advice about my pension and these changes?
We recommend speaking to a financial adviser. A financial adviser can give you personalised advice and recommendations. If you don't already have an adviser you can find one by visiting [royallondon.com/find-a-financial-adviser](https://www.royallondon.com/find-a-financial-adviser/).
Financial advisers will normally charge you a fee but they should let you know in advance how much their services will cost.
Once your pension has been upgraded you will be able to pay for financial advice directly from your pension plan (this option is not available under the existing Police Mutual GPP).

  * access to our [financial wellbeing guidance](https://www.royallondon.com/articles-guides/financial-wellbeing/) service; and
  * a share in our profits which can boost your retirement savings, which we call ‘[ProfitShare](https://www.royallondon.com/profitshare/)’.

How does Royal London benefit by making these changes?
Mutual companies such as Royal London are customer-owned. This means that a share of our profits goes to customers, not shareholders and it influences the decisions we make every day.
By upgrading our customers' workplace pensions to bring them in line with our newest workplace pension product, we will have fewer legacy pension systems to maintain. We will also have fewer versions of the plan terms and conditions to amend in the future, for example due to a change in pensions legislation or if we want to introduce new features.
We want our longstanding workplace customers like you to have access to the same improved options and experiences as our new workplace customers.
When are you planning on making the changes?
We’re writing to you now to give you as much notice as we can of the changes we are making to your pension. We will also send you a reminder about the upgrade later in the year.
In **August 2024** , unless you have already taken your pension or transferred it to an alternative pension product, we’ll upgrade your pension and send you a **Retirement Solutions** ‘welcome pack’.
You’ll automatically be allocated a new **Retirement Solutions** plan number and this new number will be quoted on all future correspondence you receive from us.
How do I know the changes being made are in my best interests?
We want our longstanding workplace customers like you to have access to the same improved options and experiences as our new workplace customers. We're upgrading your pension to allow you to access several features you don't currently have, which could help you to achieve your retirement goals.
We’ve agreed this approach with the Royal London Independent Governance Committee (IGC) which has a mandate to assess the value for money provided to workplace pension customers like you. We’re making these changes to meet the IGC’s expectations and they’re supportive of this approach.
We’ve also informed our regulator, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) about what we are doing.
Can I opt out of the changes?
No. We’ve agreed with the Royal London IGC that we’ll upgrade all Police Mutual Group Personal Pensions to bring them in line with our Retirement Solutions product. It won’t be possible for you to opt out of the changes for your pension and retain the current terms.
If you don’t want your pension to be upgraded, you can choose to transfer your pension to a different pension product, with Royal London or another provider. Royal London will not apply any exit charges if you choose to transfer your pension. Alternatively, if you are age 55 or over you could choose to access your pension savings.
If you don’t want your pension to be upgraded and instead want to transfer to another pension product or take your pension savings (if age 55 or over) then you must do so by **1 August 2024**.
If you decide that you want to transfer your pension to an alternative pension product, we recommend that you get independent financial advice from a regulated financial adviser. Financial advisers will normally charge you a fee but they should let you know in advance how much their services will cost. If you don’t have a financial adviser, you can [get help finding one](https://www.royallondon.com/find-a-financial-adviser/) on our website.
## What will the changes mean for me?
How will the changes impact my current plan?
We’ve sent you an **'important changes affecting your workplace pension' leaflet (PDF)** which summarises the key differences between the current terms of your plan and the new terms that will apply once the upgrade is made.
If you have any other questions about the changes then don’t hesitate to get in touch.
Will I keep the same plan number?
No, when we upgrade your pension we’ll send you a **Retirement Solutions ‘welcome pack’**.
You’ll automatically be allocated a new **Retirement Solutions** plan number and this new number will be quoted on all future correspondence you receive from us.
Will the charges I currently pay change?
If you are (or were) a Royal London employee, the charges that you pay under your Police Mutual workplace pension will reduce to **0.24%** of your plan value each year once it’s upgraded. This is to bring these in line with the charges being paid under the Royal London staff pension (RL GPP).
Otherwise, the charges you currently pay will not change – they will remain at **0.6%** of your plan value each year.
Will the fund my pension is invested in change?
When the changes are made, your pension will automatically be invested in the **Royal London Long Term** fund which our investment experts have identified as a replacement investment fund that’s the closest match to the fund your pension is currently invested in. The **Royal London Long Term** fund is a new fund we’ve created specifically for the upgrade, but it operates in a similar way as your current investment option within the Police Mutual GPP. For more information, please see the [fund factsheet](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/shared/factsheets/fs5pd0002-with-profits-factsheet.pdf).
Once the changes are made, you don’t have to stay invested in this fund and can choose to switch into an alternative investment option at any time. You can [find more information](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/investment-options/) about the **Royal London Long Term fund** and our alternative options.
Will I still be able to contribute to my pension?
As long as you are resident in the UK:
  * If you aren't currently contributing, you can choose to start making contributions at any point after the changes have been made; or
  * If you are currently contributing, you can continue to do so, including increasing contributions or transferring in other pension plans you may have, after the changes have been made. However, you’ll need to complete and return the declaration and direct debit instruction form.

If you're resident outside of the UK, unfortunately you won't be able to start or increase contributions to your pension.
When will I be able to access my pension benefits?
The minimum pension age is currently age 55. This is the earliest age at which most people can normally access their pension benefits. The government is changing the minimum pension age from age 55 to age 57 from April 2028, however your pension has a protected pension age of 55 and this will be retained as part of the upgrade.
We’ll send you information as you approach your chosen pension age to provide you with information about the different options that are available and to help you to decide what’s best for your personal circumstances.
A guidance service is also available through the government backed website [Pension Wise](https://www.moneyhelper.org.uk/en/pensions-and-retirement/pension-wise) (opens in a new window) for people over age 50.
Will my chosen retirement age change?
Your chosen retirement age won’t change after the upgrade unless you’re already beyond your current chosen retirement age. If this applies to you, we confirmed in the letter that we sent you earlier this year what we’ll change your chosen retirement age on your pension to (in most cases this will be your age at your next birthday), unless you choose to take your pension savings before **1 August 2024** or provide us with an alternative retirement age to use.
What will happen if I need to make changes to my plan before the upgrade?
To make sure that the upgrade happens as smoothly as possible, we may need to defer making certain requested changes for a short period of time until the upgrade has happened.
Here’s examples of some of the servicing deferments that may apply. This is not an exhaustive list and we will always act to ensure you are not detrimentally impacted by any deferment that may occur during this time.
| **Type of change**  | **Examples of the change**  | **What will happen**  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Personal details change  | Change of name, address, marital status, contact details  | Any changes that are advised within **2 weeks** of the upgrade will be applied as part of the upgrade  |
| Plan change  | Making new contributions into your plan  | Any requests within **1 month** of the upgrade will be applied after the upgrade  |
| Plan change  | Changing the chosen retirement age on your plan  | Any changes advised within **2 weeks** of the upgrade will be applied as part of the upgrade  |
To upgrade your pension, we need to transfer it from one administration system to another which can take a few days. During this time it’s unlikely that we will be able to provide you with an up-to-date plan value or process any request to withdraw any funds (if you are age 55 or over). We will, however, keep a log of any such requests made, and process these as soon as the upgrade is complete.
The scheme has changed what does that mean?
Most pension plans (like yours) form part of a registered pension scheme. The scheme is governed by the rules of that scheme and operates in line with current pension and tax legislation.
After the upgrade, your plan will form part of the Royal London Personal Pension Scheme (No2).
Under that pension scheme you will have more flexibility around how you can take your retirement savings when you come to retire.
How can I access a copy of the Retirement Solutions Group Personal Plan terms and conditions?
You can view a copy of the [Retirement Solutions Group Pension Plan terms and conditions](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/consumer/workplace-migration/14gpc25-group-personal-pension-plan-booklet.pdf) (PDF) here.
Why will the upgrade mean that my plan is now written under Scots law?
The terms and conditions applying after the upgrade clearly state that your plan will be governed by Scots Law unless we agree with you that a different law should apply. This is because the trust under which the plan will be administered was established under Scots Law. However, the actual legal framework for pensions is governed by UK wide statute.
In the unlikely event that an issue arises in the future that leads to you taking legal action against Royal London, it is ultimately for the court to decide whether or not it has jurisdiction to hear a case. If, for example, the planholder is based in England and Royal London is registered in England, we cannot envisage any situation where an English court would refuse to hear a case if asked to by a planholder. We can think of no reason why Royal London would insist on a case for a non-Scottish planholder being heard in Scotland – that would breach our Customer Duty obligations.
What is ProfitShare?
When we do well, we'll aim to boost your pension savings by adding a share of our profits to your plan each year. We call this [ProfitShare](https://www.royallondon.com/profitshare/).
Although we can’t guarantee we’ll be able to award ProfitShare every year, our continued strength in how we run our business for our customers means we shared £163 million of our profits over 2 million customers in 2024.
ProfitShare is just one of the ways we express our mutuality. Mutual companies such as Royal London are customer-owned. This means that a share of our profits goes to customers, not shareholders and it influences the decisions we make every day.
What functionality is available under the Royal London mobile app?
Our [mobile app](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/online-service/download-our-mobile-app/) isn’t just about showing you what you’ve got - it’s about helping you plan for your future and putting the power in your hands.
You can use our app to explore different outlooks based on your investment approach as well as contributions you’ve made, or money you’ve taken out. And the benefits don’t stop there. As a mutual we aim to put you first so our mobile app also provides you with helpful guides, covering key topics like budgeting, dealing with life events or even helping you get started with investing.
Can I choose to transfer my Police Mutual GPP into my existing Retirement Solutions plan?
Yes, you can transfer your Police Mutual GPP into another pension, including an existing Retirement Solutions plan or Royal London staff pension (RL GPP) at any time.
If you’re a current or former Royal London employee you’re likely to already have a staff pension plan (RL GPP) or Retirement Solutions plan relating to that employment and you can choose to transfer your Police Mutual GPP into that plan at any time. If you don’t transfer into this plan we will upgrade your Police Mutual GPP to a Retirement Solutions GPP and this would then mean you’d continue to have two plans.
## What do I need to do now?
I’m still contributing to my pension and want to proceed with the upgrade
If you're happy for us to upgrade the terms of your workplace pension, please complete and return the **declaration and direct debit instruction form** we sent you as soon as possible.
You can either post the form back to us using the pre-paid envelope or alternatively you can [upload a copy](http://www.royallondon.com/workplaceupgrade) of the completed form online. We require the form to be returned so your regular contributions can continue.
I’m no longer contributing to my pension and want to proceed with the upgrade
If you're happy for us to upgrade the terms of your workplace pension you don't need to do anything else.
I don’t want you to proceed with the upgrade
If you don’t want us to upgrade the terms of your workplace pension, you’ll need to take steps to transfer your pension to an alternative pension product before **1 August 2024**. This is because you won’t have the option to opt out and stay on your existing terms.
We have alternative pension products that may be suitable, or you can consider an alternative pension product with another provider.
There will be no exit charge or penalty applied if you decide to transfer your pension to an alternative pension product with us or another provider.
## Need further information?
Who is Royal London?
Royal London is the largest mutual life, pensions, and investment company in the UK.
More information about Royal London and what we stand for can be [found on our website](https://www.royallondon.com/).
Where can I find out more about Retirement Solutions?
You can read the Retirement Solutions Group Pension Plan [key features document](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/adviser/key-features/14kfi26-group-personal-pension-key-features.pdf) (PDF) here.
How can I contact you if I have any queries?
We can provide general information about the upgrade however we cannot provide advice about what is best for you.
You can get in touch by emailing gpp.transfer@pmas.co.uk or by calling [01543 441 630](tel:01543%20441%20630).
I want independent advice about my pension and these changes?
We recommend speaking to a financial adviser. A financial adviser can give you personalised advice and recommendations. If you don't already have an adviser you can find one by visiting [royallondon.com/find-a-financial-adviser](https://www.royallondon.com/find-a-financial-adviser/).
Financial advisers will normally charge you a fee but they should let you know in advance how much their services will cost.
Once your pension has been upgraded you will be able to pay for financial advice directly from your pension plan (this option is not available under the existing Police Mutual GPP).
## Key information
## What we're doing
  * Upgrading your Police Mutual workplace pension from **1 August** to our newest workplace pension product **Retirement Solutions**.

## About Retirement Solutions
  * [Upgraded T&Cs](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/consumer/workplace-migration/14gpc25-group-personal-pension-plan-booklet.pdf) (PDF)
  * [Key features](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/adviser/key-features/14kfi26-group-personal-pension-key-features.pdf) (PDF)
  * [Comparison leaflet](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/consumer/workplace-migration/lpl0004-pmas-comparison-leaflet-n-rl.pdf) (PDF)
  * [Comparison leaflet for former/current Royal London staff](https://www.royallondon.com/globalassets/docs/consumer/workplace-migration/lpl0005-pmas-comparison-leaflet-rl.pdf) (PDF)

## Need help
  * Contact us
  * [Find an adviser](https://www.royallondon.com/find-a-financial-adviser/)

##  Giving your pension and ISA a boost
When we do well, we'll aim to boost your pension and stocks and shares ISA by adding a share of our profits to your plan each year. We've called this ProfitShare.
Although we can’t guarantee we’ll be able to award ProfitShare every year, our continued strength in how we run our business for our customers means we're sharing **£199 million of our profits** with approximately **2.4 million eligible customers** in April 2026.
ProfitShare is just one of the ways we express our [mutuality](https://www.royallondon.com/about-us/how-we-are-run/mutuality/). Mutual companies such as Royal London are proudly customer-owned. This means that a share of our profits goes to customers, not shareholders and it influences the decisions we make every day.
If you're eligible for ProfitShare, you can see what's been applied to your pension plan with our [mobile app](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/online-service/download-our-mobile-app/). What's more, you can stay up to date with your pension savings, look at what you've paid in and see what your plan could be worth in the future.
## One-off contributions and transfers
ProfitShare is based on the value of the pension and stocks and shares ISA you've got invested with us on the date it’s awarded. Which means any one-off contributions you make before 6pm on Tuesday 31 March will qualify for ProfitShare this year. If we get your contribution after this date, then it will count towards any ProfitShare award we could make next year.

It’s not only contributions that count towards ProfitShare, but any pensions and ISAs that you transfer into your Royal London plans will also qualify for ProfitShare in the future. So, if you’re considering making a [one-off contribution](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/pension-guides/pension-basics/benefits-of-making-a-one-off-pension-contribution/), [pension transfer](https://www.royallondon.com/pensions/pension-transfers/) or [ISA transfer](https://www.royallondon.com/isa/transfers/) to your plan(s), you could help your pension and ISA grow with ProfitShare.
Remember, while your savings could grow, their value can also go down, as investment returns aren’t guaranteed. This means you could get back less than you put into your plan. If you need help you should [speak to a financial adviser](https://www.royallondon.com/find-a-financial-adviser/).
###
### Eligible plans
You'll be eligible for ProfitShare if you have taken out a pension plan with Royal London since 1 July 2001, or if you have taken out a stocks and shares ISA with Royal London since 15 September 2025. If that applies to you, we’ll automatically set up a ProfitShare account under your plan. You don’t need to lift a finger.
If you’re a member of an occupational scheme, your eligibility for ProfitShare is based on the date your scheme began – not the date you joined. If you’re unsure about the date your scheme began, you should speak to your employer or the scheme trustees.
Unfortunately, we're unable to offer ProfitShare under our Crest Secure, Retirement Account contracts or any self-invested retirement savings you have. Any plans set up with The Co-operative Insurance Society Limited (CIS) also won't qualify.
ProfitShare awards will be applied as at 1 April each year. To qualify, your plan must be in force on 31 December the previous year and on the date the award is given.

## Funding your retirement
As the UK’s largest mutual life, pensions and investment company,1 everything we do is in the best interest of our customers. So, when you choose our products you're not only putting your money in reliable hands, but in responsible ones too. We can help you save money for your future and invest responsibly, so we can all build a future worth living in.
1 Based on total 2022 premium income. ICMIF Global 500, 2024.
## [Using your pension When it comes to accessing your pension savings you can:
  * Take a cash lump sum
  * Get flexible access to your savings, also known as pension drawdown
  * Buy a secure income, also known as a pension annuity
  * Leave your money invested until you decide to take it.

Whatever you decide to do, you can usually take up to 25% of your pension savings completely tax free. Find out more about using your pension  ](https://www.royallondon.com/retirement-planning/using-pension/)
  * ## Coming up to retirement
  * ## In retirement

###  Coming up to retirement
  * Can I access my pension savings early?
Your pension savings are locked in until you reach age 55 (increasing to age 57 from 6 April 2028). It may be possible for you to access your pension savings before then if your health means you can no longer carry on working.
  * What happens when I'm ready to take my pension savings?
We'll send you a letter before your chosen pension age. We'll explain your options and then, when you're ready, you can decide what you want to do.
  * What happens if I die before I start taking my pension savings?
Your pension can provide support to your loved ones if you die before taking your savings.
Income Tax does not apply if death occurs before age 75 and beneficiaries:
- Withdraw funds within two years of notifying the pension scheme about your death, or from the date the scheme was expected to know or could reasonably have been expected to know.
- Receive income from an annuity set up after 6 April 2015.
- Access funds from a drawdown pot, as long as the pension was first accessed after 6 April 2015.
- Do not take lump sums exceeding the lump sum and death benefit allowance (LSDBA).

[More guidance on coming up to retirement](https://www.royallondon.com/retirement-planning/retirement-guidance/approaching-retirement/)
###  In retirement
  * How will my income be taxed?
Normally 25% of your pension savings will be tax-free and the remaining 75% is taxable.
HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) calculate the tax you need to pay and tell us how much to take off before anything is paid to you.
Find out more about [how much tax you may need to pay](https://www.royallondon.com/guides-tools/pension-guides/taking-your-pension/understanding-pension-tax-rules/).
  * Once I've started to take my pension, can I change the amount I receive each month?
You might be able to if you've chosen to access your pension flexibly (also known as pension drawdown). You can't usually change your mind once you've bought a secure income, also known as a pension annuity. We recommend you [speak to a financial adviser](https://www.royallondon.com/find-a-financial-adviser/) about your options.
  * Can I have a job even though I'm taking my pension?
You can work for as long as you like. You’ll still be taxed on the money you earn, whether that’s from your pension or your job, and you should look into this carefully.
Here's information about [how tax affects your pension](https://www.gov.uk/tax-on-pension).

[More guidance on in retirement](https://www.royallondon.com/retirement-planning/retirement-guidance/in-retirement/)

## [Your plan online Depending on the type of pension plan you have, you can access details of your pension savings with our secure online service. Find out about our online service  ](https://www.royallondon.com/existing-customers/online-service/)
